q: A company runs its production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. The CTO requires automatic failover to a standby database if an AZ outage occurs, with minimal administrative effort. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Create an RDS read replica in a second AZ and manually promote it during outages
Enable Multi-AZ deployment on the RDS DB instance
Take daily manual snapshots and restore them in another AZ after an outage
Deploy a second standalone RDS instance and configure application-level replication
explain: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby replica in another AZ and fails over automatically with no manual steps. Read replicas are asynchronous and require manual promotion, snapshots have a high RTO, and application-level replication adds heavy operational burden.

q: A financial services company must retain transaction logs for 7 years for compliance. The logs are accessed frequently for 30 days, then almost never. Which S3 lifecycle approach is MOST cost-effective while meeting the retention requirement?
options: Keep all objects in S3 Standard for the full 7 years
Store the logs in S3 Standard-IA from day one
Move objects to S3 One Zone-IA after 30 days
Transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days and expire them after 7 years
explain: Glacier Flexible Retrieval costs a fraction of Standard for rarely accessed archives, and expiration enforces the 7-year retention. Keeping everything in Standard for 7 years is wasteful, One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ (less resilience for compliance records), and Standard-IA from day one is pricier than Glacier for archival data.

q: A web application runs on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. During an AZ impairment, the application must keep serving traffic with no manual intervention. Which design provides this resilience?
options: Deploy the Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs with the ALB spanning the same AZs
Run all instances in a single AZ and keep daily AMIs
Deploy a second ALB in another Region and switch DNS manually during outages
Place the instances in a cluster placement group in one AZ
explain: Spreading the Auto Scaling group and the ALB across AZs means the loss of one AZ leaves healthy targets serving traffic automatically. A single AZ is a single point of failure, manual DNS switching is slow, and a cluster placement group concentrates instances in one AZ.

q: An order-processing system has a web tier that writes directly to a backend processing tier. During traffic spikes the backend is overwhelmed and orders are lost. Which change makes the architecture resilient to spikes?
options: Increase the instance size of the backend servers
Add more backend servers permanently
Place an SQS queue between the web tier and the backend so requests are buffered and processed asynchronously
Write orders to a local file on the web servers
explain: Decoupling with SQS buffers bursts so the backend processes at its own pace and no orders are lost. Bigger or more permanent servers over-provision for peaks, and local files are neither durable nor shared across the fleet.

q: A company needs a disaster recovery strategy for a non-critical internal application. An RTO of 24 hours is acceptable and cost must be minimized. Which strategy is MOST appropriate?
options: Multi-site active/active deployment
Backup and restore using automated backups replicated to a second Region
Warm standby with a scaled-down copy running in a second Region
Pilot light with the core database replicated continuously
explain: Backup and restore is the cheapest DR strategy and comfortably meets a 24-hour RTO. Multi-site, warm standby, and pilot light all run live infrastructure in a second Region, which costs far more than this application's requirements justify.

q: A company hosts its website in one Region and wants DNS to automatically route users to a standby site in a second Region when health checks fail. Which Route 53 routing policy should be used?
options: Failover routing with health checks on the primary record
Weighted routing with 50/50 weights
Geolocation routing
Simple routing
explain: Failover routing uses health checks to shift traffic from the primary to the secondary record automatically. Weighted routing splits traffic continuously, geolocation routes by user location, and simple routing has no health-based failover.

q: A VPC has private subnets in three AZs with workloads that need outbound internet access. The single NAT gateway in one AZ is a single point of failure. What is the resilient design?
options: Move the workloads to public subnets
Add a second NAT gateway in the same AZ
Replace the NAT gateway with an internet gateway attached to the private subnets
Deploy one NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet through its AZ-local NAT gateway
explain: One NAT gateway per AZ removes the single point of failure and keeps traffic within the AZ. A second gateway in the same AZ still fails with that AZ, public subnets expose the workloads, and an internet gateway cannot be attached to private subnets for outbound-only access.

q: A mobile gaming company uses DynamoDB in a single Region. Players on other continents see high write latency, and the game must stay available during a regional outage. Which solution meets both needs?
options: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
Add a DAX cluster in each Region
Use DynamoDB global tables to replicate data across Regions with active-active writes
Increase provisioned write capacity
explain: Global tables provide multi-Region, active-active replication with local reads and writes everywhere. Point-in-time recovery is a backup feature, DAX only accelerates reads, and more write capacity does nothing for latency or regional outages.

q: A company runs Aurora MySQL and needs read replicas in a second Region with typical replication lag under one second plus fast cross-region failover for disaster recovery. Which feature should be used?
options: Aurora read replicas in the same Region
Aurora Global Database
RDS Multi-AZ deployment
Ongoing replication with AWS DMS
explain: Aurora Global Database is purpose-built for cross-region reads with sub-second lag and fast failover. Same-Region replicas don't help cross-region DR, Multi-AZ is within one Region, and DMS adds operational overhead for a use case Aurora handles natively.

q: A company must be able to recover EC2-backed workloads in a second Region after a regional disaster. Which approach provides cross-region recovery for EBS volumes?
options: Copy EBS snapshots to the second Region so volumes can be recreated there
Enable EBS encryption in the primary Region
Increase the EBS volume size
Store application data on instance store volumes
explain: EBS snapshots are regional, but copying them to another Region lets you recreate volumes there. Encryption doesn't enable cross-region recovery, volume size is irrelevant, and instance store data is ephemeral and lost on stop.

q: A media site serves content from an ALB origin through CloudFront. The company wants CloudFront to automatically serve from a backup origin if the primary returns errors. How should this be configured?
options: Create two CloudFront distributions and switch DNS manually
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the origin
Configure a CloudFront origin group with the ALB as the primary origin and the backup as the secondary for failover
Add a second cache behavior with a longer TTL
explain: Origin groups let CloudFront fail over to a secondary origin automatically based on error status codes. Two distributions with manual DNS switching is slow, Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than providing failover, and cache behaviors don't define backup origins.

q: A company needs objects uploaded to an S3 bucket in us-east-1 to be automatically replicated to a bucket in eu-west-1 for disaster recovery. What must be true for cross-region replication to work?
options: Both buckets must use S3 Intelligent-Tiering
The destination bucket must be in the same account's default VPC
Replication works on unversioned buckets by default
Versioning must be enabled on both the source and destination buckets, with an IAM role granting S3 replication permissions
explain: S3 replication requires versioning on both buckets and an IAM role authorizing the replication. Storage class doesn't matter, buckets aren't in VPCs, and replication does not work without versioning.

q: A stateful web application stores user sessions on individual EC2 instances. When Auto Scaling terminates instances, users are logged out. Which change makes the fleet resilient to instance replacement?
options: Use larger EC2 instances so they are terminated less often
Store session state externally in ElastiCache or DynamoDB so any instance can serve any user
Disable Auto Scaling termination policies
Copy session files between instances with rsync
explain: Externalizing session state makes instances stateless, so any instance can serve any request after scaling events. Larger instances still get terminated, disabling termination breaks scaling, and rsync between ephemeral instances is fragile and not scalable.

q: A fleet of EC2 instances across multiple AZs needs a shared file system that remains available if an AZ fails. Which storage service should be used?
options: Amazon EFS, which replicates data across multiple AZs and can be mounted from any AZ
An EBS volume attached to one instance and shared over NFS
Instance store volumes on each instance
A single EBS volume with Multi-Attach in one AZ
explain: EFS is a regional service that stores data redundantly across AZs. EBS volumes live in a single AZ, instance store is ephemeral, and Multi-Attach doesn't span AZs — all leave an AZ failure taking the data with it.

q: A Lambda function processes events asynchronously. Occasionally invocations fail due to transient downstream errors and the events are lost. How should failed events be captured for later retry?
options: Increase the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes
Enable Lambda provisioned concurrency
Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) or an on-failure destination so failed events are retained for redrive
Give the Lambda function more memory
explain: A DLQ or on-failure destination (SQS, SNS, Lambda, or EventBridge) preserves failed asynchronous invocations for analysis and redrive. Timeout, memory, and provisioned concurrency address performance, not the loss of failed events.

q: A company has EC2, RDS, and EFS resources across multiple accounts and needs centralized, policy-based backups with cross-region copies for compliance. Which service provides this with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Write custom backup scripts using the AWS CLI in each account
Manually create snapshots on a fixed schedule
Use CloudFormation to schedule snapshots per resource
AWS Backup with backup plans, cross-account management, and cross-region copy rules
explain: AWS Backup centralizes backup policies, scheduling, retention, and cross-region copies across services and accounts. Custom scripts, manual snapshots, and per-resource CloudFormation scheduling all multiply operational effort and are easy to get wrong.

q: A company caches session data in ElastiCache for Redis with a single node. A node failure would lose cached data and cause a database surge. Which configuration adds resilience?
options: Switch to ElastiCache for Memcached with one node
Enable Multi-AZ with automatic failover using a Redis replication group with replica nodes
Increase the node type to the largest available
Disable encryption in transit
explain: A Redis replication group with Multi-AZ automatic failover promotes a replica if the primary fails, preserving cached data. Memcached offers no replication or failover, a bigger node is still a single point of failure, and encryption settings don't affect availability.

q: A company wants a DR strategy where the critical database is continuously replicated to a second Region, but application servers are only provisioned when a disaster is declared. An RTO of a few hours is acceptable. Which strategy is this?
options: Pilot light
Multi-site active/active
Backup and restore
Warm standby
explain: Pilot light keeps only the critical core (like the replicated database) always running, with remaining resources provisioned at failover time. Warm standby runs a scaled-down full stack continuously, backup and restore keeps no live copy, and multi-site runs everything active.

q: A company needs an RTO measured in minutes for its e-commerce platform and can afford to run a scaled-down version of the full stack in a second Region at all times. Which DR strategy fits?
options: Backup and restore
Pilot light
Warm standby
Single-Region Multi-AZ only
explain: Warm standby runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy in the second Region, enabling failover in minutes. Pilot light needs hours to provision the app tier, backup and restore takes longer still, and single-Region Multi-AZ doesn't cover regional disasters.

q: A company worries that an operator error or compromised credentials could permanently delete critical S3 objects. Which combination BEST protects against accidental or malicious deletion?
options: Enable S3 server access logging
Use the S3 Standard-IA storage class
Apply a bucket policy denying all deletes
Enable versioning with MFA Delete so deleting object versions requires multi-factor authentication
explain: Versioning preserves prior versions of objects, and MFA Delete requires a hardware or virtual MFA device to permanently delete versions. Access logging is detective only, storage class is irrelevant, and denying all deletes would break legitimate application operations.

q: A company's RDS database is read-heavy. The team wants to offload reads AND have automatic failover. Which statement about combining RDS features is correct?
options: Multi-AZ alone handles both read scaling and automatic failover
Use read replicas to scale reads and Multi-AZ for automatic failover — they serve different purposes
Read replicas provide automatic failover while Multi-AZ provides read scaling
Neither feature helps; add a larger DB instance instead
explain: Read replicas scale read traffic but require manual promotion on failure; Multi-AZ provides a synchronous standby with automatic failover but cannot serve reads. They are complementary features, not substitutes, and a bigger instance addresses neither scaling pattern cleanly.

q: A company connects its on-premises datacenter to AWS with Direct Connect. To stay connected if the Direct Connect location fails, what should be added?
options: A Site-to-Site VPN connection as a backup path to the VPC
A second virtual interface on the same Direct Connect connection
An internet gateway in the VPC
A NAT gateway in each AZ
explain: A Site-to-Site VPN over the public internet provides an independent backup path if the Direct Connect location fails. A second virtual interface on the same connection shares the same failure domain, and internet or NAT gateways don't connect on-premises networks.

q: Messages in an SQS queue are sometimes processed twice because consumers occasionally exceed the visibility timeout. The company wants each message processed successfully without loss. What should be configured?
options: Delete and recreate the queue daily
Set the visibility timeout to zero
Set the visibility timeout to exceed the maximum processing time and configure a dead-letter queue with a redrive policy for poison messages
Replace SQS with SNS
explain: A visibility timeout longer than the worst-case processing time prevents premature redelivery, while a DLQ isolates poison messages that repeatedly fail. Zero timeout causes constant duplication, recreating the queue loses messages, and SNS is a notification fan-out service, not a work queue.

q: A global SaaS company requires near-zero RTO and RPO for its platform and has the budget for full duplication. Which DR strategy delivers the lowest RTO and RPO?
options: Backup and restore
Pilot light
Warm standby
Multi-site active/active across Regions
explain: Multi-site active/active runs the full workload in multiple Regions simultaneously, giving near-zero RTO/RPO at the highest cost. Backup and restore, pilot light, and warm standby all trade slower recovery for lower cost.

q: An ALB distributes traffic to EC2 targets. Unhealthy instances must be removed from rotation automatically. Which ALB feature handles this?
options: Sticky sessions
Target group health checks that mark unhealthy targets out of service
Connection draining alone
Access logs
explain: Target group health checks probe each target and automatically stop routing to unhealthy ones. Sticky sessions pin users to targets, connection draining only affects deregistration timing, and access logs are for analysis, not traffic control.

q: An Auto Scaling group uses EC2 health checks only. Instances with a failed application (but a running OS) stay in service. What improves this?
options: Use ELB health checks so the load balancer's application-level checks drive Auto Scaling replacements
Increase the health check grace period to 24 hours
Disable health checks entirely
Set the minimum group size to zero
explain: ELB health checks test the application endpoint, so a hung application triggers instance replacement even when the OS is fine. EC2 checks only verify the hypervisor view. A longer grace period delays detection, disabling checks removes protection, and minimum size doesn't detect failures.

q: A company needs automated, scheduled EBS snapshots with retention policies and cross-account sharing for DR, without custom scripts. Which service should be used?
options: Amazon S3 lifecycle policies
AWS Config rules
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) lifecycle policies
AWS CloudTrail
explain: DLM automates snapshot creation, retention, and cross-account sharing through lifecycle policies. S3 lifecycle policies manage objects, Config evaluates compliance, and CloudTrail audits API calls — none schedule EBS snapshots.

q: A company has 20 VPCs that must communicate with each other and with on-premises networks. The VPC peering mesh is becoming unmanageable. Which design simplifies resilient connectivity?
options: Consolidate everything into one large VPC
Build VPC peering between every pair of VPCs
Use internet gateways with public IPs for inter-VPC traffic
AWS Transit Gateway as a central hub with route tables and VPN/Direct Connect attachments
explain: Transit Gateway provides hub-and-spoke routing that scales beyond peering meshes and centralizes on-premises attachments. A single giant VPC breaks isolation boundaries, full-mesh peering grows quadratically, and public internet routing is insecure and unreliable.

q: A company needs protection against accidental DynamoDB table deletion or corruption, with per-second restore granularity over the last 35 days. Which feature provides this?
options: Point-in-time recovery (PITR) with continuous backups
DynamoDB Streams
DAX
Global tables
explain: PITR keeps continuous backups enabling restore to any second in the preceding 35 days. Streams capture change records for processing, DAX is a read cache, and global tables replicate across Regions rather than providing point-in-time restore.

q: A payment processing system must process transactions in order and exactly once, even across retries. Which messaging solution meets these requirements?
options: Standard SQS queue
SQS FIFO queue with content-based deduplication and message group IDs
SNS topic with email subscriptions
EventBridge default event bus
explain: SQS FIFO guarantees ordering within a message group and exactly-once processing via deduplication IDs. Standard queues offer at-least-once delivery with best-effort ordering, while SNS and EventBridge don't provide FIFO ordering with deduplication.

q: A company serves product images to users worldwide from an S3 bucket in a single Region. Users far from the Region report slow load times. Which solution provides the LOWEST latency globally?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
Replicate the bucket with cross-region replication to every Region
Serve the images through CloudFront with the S3 bucket as origin so content is cached at edge locations
Request an increase to the S3 bucket request rate limits
explain: CloudFront caches content at hundreds of edge locations close to users, cutting latency worldwide. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, replicating to every Region is operationally heavy, and S3 already scales request rates automatically.

q: A media company has contributors worldwide uploading large video files to a central S3 bucket. Uploads over long distances are slow. Which feature speeds up the uploads?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration, which routes uploads through nearby CloudFront edge locations onto the AWS backbone
CloudFront signed URLs
S3 Select
Multipart download
explain: Transfer Acceleration uses the AWS edge network so uploads travel over optimized backbone paths instead of the public internet. Signed URLs control access rather than speed, S3 Select filters retrievals, and multipart download applies to downloads.

q: An application reads the same DynamoDB items millions of times per day and needs microsecond response times. Which solution provides this with the LEAST application change?
options: Increase DynamoDB provisioned read capacity
Add ElastiCache for Memcached and rewrite the data access code
Enable DynamoDB global tables
Add DAX in front of DynamoDB — it is API-compatible and caches reads in memory for microsecond latency
explain: DAX is a drop-in, API-compatible cache for DynamoDB delivering microsecond reads for cached items. More read capacity doesn't reach microsecond latency, Memcached requires code changes, and global tables address multi-Region writes rather than read latency.

q: A relational database is overwhelmed by repeated identical read queries. Which solution reduces database load with minimal changes?
options: Enable Multi-AZ on the database
Place ElastiCache (Redis) in front of the database to cache frequent query results
Take more frequent snapshots
Enable storage autoscaling
explain: Caching repeated queries in ElastiCache absorbs the read load so the database handles only cache misses. Multi-AZ is for failover, snapshots are for recovery, and storage autoscaling addresses disk space — none reduce query load.

q: An analytics dashboard runs heavy read queries against the production RDS instance, slowing down transactions. How can reads be scaled without affecting writes?
options: Enable Multi-AZ
Increase the backup retention period
Create RDS read replicas and direct reporting queries to the replica endpoints
Enable deletion protection
explain: Read replicas offload read traffic to separate endpoints while writes stay on the primary. Multi-AZ standbys can't serve reads, backup retention doesn't scale performance, and deletion protection is a safety control.

q: A real-time trading application needs a load balancer handling millions of TCP requests per second with ultra-low latency and static IP addresses. Which load balancer is BEST?
options: Network Load Balancer — operates at Layer 4 with ultra-high throughput and static IP addresses
Application Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer
Gateway Load Balancer
explain: NLB is built for extreme TCP/UDP performance at Layer 4 with static IPs and preserved source addresses. ALB is Layer 7 with more per-request processing, Classic is legacy, and Gateway LB is for routing through virtual appliances.

q: A REST API backed by Lambda has spiky traffic and many repeated identical GET requests. Backend costs are rising. Which API Gateway feature reduces backend calls?
options: Enable CORS
Increase the Lambda timeout
Deploy the API to a second Region
Enable API Gateway caching with an appropriate TTL so repeated requests are served from the cache
explain: API Gateway caching serves repeated requests without invoking the backend, cutting Lambda invocations and latency. CORS enables cross-origin access, timeout affects long requests, and a second Region adds complexity without reducing backend calls.

q: A Lambda-backed API suffers cold starts that cause latency spikes after idle periods. Which feature keeps execution environments initialized?
options: Reserved concurrency
Provisioned concurrency
Lambda destinations
A larger deployment package
explain: Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes execution environments so requests skip cold starts. Reserved concurrency only caps maximum concurrency, destinations handle async results, and package size doesn't prevent cold starts.

q: A database workload needs 16,000 sustained IOPS on EBS at the LOWEST cost. Which volume type is MOST appropriate?
options: Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
Cold HDD (sc1)
General Purpose SSD (gp3) with provisioned IOPS
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2)
explain: gp3 supports up to 16,000 provisioned IOPS independently of volume size at a lower price than io2. HDD volume types can't deliver 16,000 IOPS, and io2 is the pricier choice reserved for higher IOPS or 99.999% durability needs.

q: A batch job needs maximum IOPS for temporary scratch data that is deleted when the job finishes. Which storage is BEST?
options: Instance store volumes — physically attached SSDs with very high IOPS for temporary data
The EBS gp3 root volume
Amazon EFS
S3 Standard
explain: Instance store provides locally attached NVMe SSDs with the highest IOPS for ephemeral scratch space. EBS and EFS are network-attached with lower peak IOPS, and S3 is object storage with much higher per-request latency.

q: An HPC application with tightly coupled nodes needs the lowest possible network latency between EC2 instances. Which placement strategy should be used?
options: Spread placement group
Partition placement group
No placement group
Cluster placement group within a single AZ for low-latency, high-throughput networking
explain: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one AZ for minimal latency and full-bisection bandwidth. Spread and partition groups optimize for failure isolation, and no placement group gives no latency guarantees.

q: A company runs its application stack in three Regions and wants each user routed to the Region with the lowest latency. Which Route 53 policy achieves this?
options: Geolocation routing
Latency-based routing
Failover routing
Multivalue answer routing
explain: Latency-based routing directs each user to the Region with the lowest measured latency to them. Geolocation routes by geography regardless of latency, failover is for primary/secondary DR, and multivalue returns multiple healthy records without latency awareness.

q: A global application uses TCP-based protocols (not HTTP) and needs fixed entry IP addresses plus intelligent routing to healthy Regional endpoints. Which service provides this?
options: CloudFront
Route 53 latency-based routing alone
AWS Global Accelerator with static Anycast IPs routing to healthy endpoints
VPC peering
explain: Global Accelerator provides static Anycast IPs and routes TCP/UDP traffic to optimal healthy endpoints with continuous health checks. CloudFront is for HTTP caching, Route 53 alone doesn't provide static entry IPs, and VPC peering is private inter-VPC connectivity.

q: A website needs to personalize content at the edge based on the viewer's country, with minimal origin load. Which solution runs compute closest to viewers?
options: Lambda@Edge triggered on viewer request to customize responses at edge locations
Run personalization logic on the origin EC2 fleet
S3 static website hosting
Route 53 health checks
explain: Lambda@Edge executes at CloudFront edge locations on viewer request, personalizing content near the user without hitting the origin. Origin-based logic adds latency and load, S3 static hosting can't run code, and health checks don't personalize content.

q: An application uploads 50 GB video files to S3 over unreliable networks, and failed uploads must resume without restarting. Which approach is BEST?
options: Single PUT operations with retries
S3 Select
Stage the files on EBS first
Multipart upload — parts upload in parallel and failed parts can be retried individually
explain: Multipart upload splits large objects into parts uploaded in parallel, and only failed parts need retrying. A single PUT must restart entirely on failure, S3 Select is for retrieving subsets, and staging on EBS doesn't solve network reliability.

q: A network-intensive application on EC2 needs up to 100 Gbps throughput with low jitter. Which networking feature should be enabled?
options: Classic networking
Enhanced networking with the Elastic Network Adapter (ENA)
A NAT gateway
VPC Flow Logs
explain: ENA provides enhanced networking with up to 100 Gbps bandwidth and consistent low-latency performance. Classic networking is legacy with lower throughput, NAT gateways serve outbound internet access, and Flow Logs are for traffic analysis.

q: A distributed machine learning training job needs OS-bypass, low-latency node-to-node communication. Which network adapter is purpose-built for this?
options: ENA
Virtual interface (VIF)
Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA)
Internet gateway
explain: EFA provides OS-bypass networking for tightly coupled HPC and ML workloads using MPI or NCCL. ENA is general enhanced networking, a VIF is a Direct Connect construct, and an internet gateway provides internet access.

q: A new mobile app has unpredictable traffic spikes and the team doesn't want to manage capacity planning. Which DynamoDB capacity mode is BEST?
options: On-demand mode — scales automatically and charges per request
Provisioned mode with low fixed capacity
Provisioned mode with auto scaling disabled
DAX only
explain: On-demand scales instantly to any traffic level with per-request pricing and no capacity planning. Fixed provisioned capacity throttles on spikes, and DAX is a cache that still needs an underlying capacity mode.

q: A database has variable workloads with peaks 10x the baseline. The team wants automatic scaling without managing read replicas. Which Aurora option fits?
options: Aurora provisioned with a fixed instance size
RDS Multi-AZ
Aurora Global Database
Aurora Serverless v2 — scales capacity up and down automatically in fine-grained increments
explain: Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts capacity in fine increments based on demand, handling 10x peaks without manual intervention. Fixed provisioned instances must be sized for the peak, Multi-AZ is for failover, and Global Database is for cross-region reads.

q: An HPC scratch workload needs a POSIX file system with hundreds of GB/s throughput integrated with S3. Which service is purpose-built for this?
options: Amazon EFS Standard
Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon EBS io2
AWS Storage Gateway
explain: FSx for Lustre delivers massive parallel throughput for scratch HPC workloads with native S3 integration. EFS tops out far lower, EBS is block storage per instance, and Storage Gateway is for hybrid on-premises connectivity.

q: An analytics job scans 500 GB CSV files in S3 but only needs 5% of the columns. How can data transfer and cost be reduced?
options: Download the full files faster with Transfer Acceleration
Replicate the files to more Regions
Use S3 Select to retrieve only the needed columns server-side
Increase the EC2 instance size running the job
explain: S3 Select filters data inside S3 using SQL expressions, returning only the needed columns and slashing transfer. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, replication multiplies storage, and a bigger instance doesn't reduce the data scanned.

q: An application needs a simple, horizontally scalable cache for key-value data with no need for replication or persistence. Which engine is BEST?
options: ElastiCache for Memcached — simple multithreaded caching that scales horizontally with sharding
ElastiCache for Redis with Multi-AZ
DynamoDB global tables
RDS read replicas
explain: Memcached is the purpose-built choice for simple, shardable caching without replication or persistence overhead. Redis adds unneeded complexity here, while DynamoDB global tables and RDS replicas are databases, not caches.

q: A company needs low-latency reads of its Aurora database from a second continent. Which solution provides this?
options: Increase the primary instance size
Enable Aurora backtrack
Add more storage to the cluster
Create cross-region Aurora read replicas (or an Aurora Global Database) close to the users
explain: Cross-region read replicas place read capacity near distant users, cutting latency. A bigger primary doesn't shorten network distance, backtrack is for rewinding data changes, and storage size doesn't affect read latency.

q: A web application serves both static assets and dynamic API responses globally. Which combination gives the BEST global performance?
options: Serve everything directly from the ALB in one Region
Use CloudFront to cache static assets at the edge while dynamic API calls go to the regional ALB origin
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for API responses
Add more Availability Zones to the ALB
explain: CloudFront caches static content at edge locations while dynamic requests pass through to the ALB origin — the standard global performance pattern. Serving everything from one Region keeps latency high for distant users, Transfer Acceleration is for uploads, and more AZs improve resilience rather than global latency.

q: A Lambda function scales to thousands of concurrent executions, overwhelming the RDS database with connections. Which solution pools connections efficiently?
options: Increase the RDS max_connections parameter indefinitely
Deploy the Lambda function with larger memory
Amazon RDS Proxy — manages connection pooling so thousands of Lambda invocations share a small pool of database connections
Add RDS read replicas
explain: RDS Proxy multiplexes thousands of application connections into a small pool of database connections, which is exactly the Lambda connection-storm problem. Raising max_connections risks database overload, memory doesn't reduce connections, and read replicas don't pool them.

q: An IoT platform ingests millions of sensor events per second and needs real-time processing with replay capability. Which service is purpose-built for this?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams — real-time streaming ingestion with ordered per-shard processing and replay
SQS standard queue
SNS topic
EventBridge archive
explain: Kinesis Data Streams is built for high-throughput ordered streaming with configurable retention and replay. SQS is a decoupling queue without replay, SNS is fan-out notifications, and EventBridge archive covers events rather than massive sensor streams.

q: A company needs lightweight URL rewrites and header manipulation at CloudFront edge locations with minimal latency and cost. Which is MOST appropriate?
options: Lambda@Edge on origin response
Run the rewrites on the origin servers
API Gateway mapping templates
CloudFront Functions — designed for lightweight, high-scale edge customizations
explain: CloudFront Functions is purpose-built for simple, high-volume edge logic like URL rewrites with sub-millisecond startup. Lambda@Edge suits heavier compute, origin rewrites add latency, and API Gateway templates don't run at CloudFront edge locations.

q: Read traffic on an Aurora cluster varies widely. The company wants read capacity to scale automatically. Which feature provides this?
options: Manually add read replicas during peaks
Aurora Auto Scaling policies that add and remove Aurora Replicas based on CPU utilization or connections
Enable Multi-AZ
Increase the writer instance size
explain: Aurora Auto Scaling adds and removes read replicas automatically based on metrics. Manual scaling is slow and operationally heavy, Multi-AZ is for failover, and a bigger writer doesn't add read capacity.

q: A developer needs to list objects in one specific S3 bucket but currently has s3:* permissions on all buckets. Following best practices, what should the administrator do?
options: Leave the permissions as-is; broader access is more convenient
Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy instead
Replace the policy with one granting only s3:ListBucket and s3:GetObject on the specific bucket (least privilege)
Share the root account credentials with the developer
explain: Least privilege means granting only the permissions needed on only the resources needed. Broader policies and root credential sharing violate security best practices and expand the blast radius of compromised credentials.

q: An application running on EC2 needs to read from DynamoDB. What is the MOST secure way to grant these permissions?
options: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance (instance profile) — credentials are rotated automatically and never stored on the instance
Embed long-term access keys in the application code
Store access keys in an S3 bucket the instance can read
Use the root account access keys
explain: IAM roles deliver temporary credentials automatically with no secrets to store or rotate. Embedded or stored long-term keys can leak, and root keys must never be used by applications.

q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between security groups and network ACLs?
options: Both are stateless and operate at the subnet level
Security groups support deny rules; NACLs do not
NACLs are stateful; security groups are stateless
Security groups are stateful, allow-only rules applied at the instance (ENI) level; NACLs are stateless with allow and deny rules applied at the subnet level
explain: Security groups are stateful (return traffic is automatic), allow-only, and attach to ENIs; NACLs are stateless (each direction needs rules), support explicit denies, and attach to subnets. The other options reverse these properties.

q: A web application behind an ALB is being targeted by SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which AWS service provides managed rule sets to block these?
options: AWS Shield Standard
AWS WAF with managed rules for SQLi and XSS
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
explain: AWS WAF inspects Layer 7 requests and its managed rules block SQL injection and XSS patterns. Shield mitigates DDoS, GuardDuty detects threats from logs, and Config evaluates resource compliance — none filter web requests.

q: A company expects large-scale DDoS attacks and wants 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team plus cost protection against scaling during attacks. Which offering provides this?
options: AWS Shield Standard
AWS WAF rate-based rules only
AWS Shield Advanced
CloudFront signed URLs
explain: Shield Advanced adds the DDoS Response Team, advanced attack visibility, and cost protection on top of Standard's automatic protections. WAF rate rules help with floods but don't include DRT support or cost protection, and signed URLs control content access.

q: Database credentials are hardcoded in application config files and rotated manually once a year. Which service enables automatic rotation with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation for RDS credentials
Store the credentials in code comments
Email new credentials to the team quarterly
AWS CloudTrail
explain: Secrets Manager rotates RDS credentials automatically on a schedule with no code changes for supported integrations. Hardcoded, emailed, or commented credentials are insecure and manual, while CloudTrail only audits API activity.

q: EC2 instances in private subnets need to access S3 without traffic traversing the public internet and without NAT gateway data processing charges. Which solution provides this?
options: Assign public IPs to the instances
Open all outbound traffic in the NACL
Use a NAT instance
Create a VPC gateway endpoint for S3 and add it to the private subnet route tables
explain: A gateway endpoint keeps S3 traffic on the private AWS network with no data processing charges. Public IPs and open NACLs expose the instances, and NAT instances still incur data charges and management overhead.

q: Administrators currently SSH into EC2 instances through a bastion host with port 22 open. The security team wants to eliminate open inbound SSH ports entirely. Which solution is BEST?
options: Open port 22 to the whole internet for convenience
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager — browser/CLI shell access controlled by IAM with no inbound ports or bastion hosts
Share one SSH key pair among all administrators
Move the instances to public subnets
explain: Session Manager provides audited shell access through IAM with no bastion hosts, key management, or open ports. Opening SSH broadly or sharing keys weakens security, and public subnets increase exposure.

q: A company must audit all API activity across all Regions and detect tampering of the log files. Which configuration meets these requirements?
options: VPC Flow Logs only
CloudTrail with a single-Region trail
An organization CloudTrail trail logging all Regions with log file integrity validation enabled
AWS Config without CloudTrail
explain: An organization trail captures management events in every Region across accounts, and log file integrity validation uses digest files to detect tampering. Flow Logs capture network traffic rather than API calls, single-Region trails miss other Regions, and Config tracks resource configuration, not API activity.

q: A data lake bucket must never be publicly accessible, and the company wants a guardrail against future misconfiguration. Which control is MOST effective?
options: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account and bucket level
Name the bucket with a random string
Rely on the default ACLs alone
Enable S3 server access logging
explain: Block Public Access overrides any policy or ACL that would grant public access, at both account and bucket scope. Obscure names, default ACLs, and access logging don't prevent a future policy mistake from exposing the bucket.

q: A company serves private S3 content through CloudFront and must ensure the bucket is accessible ONLY via CloudFront, never directly. Which configuration enforces this?
options: Make the bucket public and rely on signed URLs
Use the S3 website endpoint as the CloudFront origin
Allow s3:GetObject for everyone in the bucket policy
Use Origin Access Control (OAC) with a bucket policy granting GetObject only to the CloudFront distribution
explain: OAC lets the bucket policy restrict GetObject to the specific CloudFront distribution, blocking direct S3 access. Public buckets or open policies defeat the purpose, and the S3 website endpoint doesn't support OAC.

q: A company needs free, auto-renewing TLS certificates for its ALB and CloudFront distribution. Which service provides this?
options: Purchase certificates from a third-party CA and install them manually each year
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) — provisions free public certificates with automatic renewal, integrated with ALB and CloudFront
Self-signed certificates
AWS KMS
explain: ACM issues free public certificates that renew automatically and deploy directly to ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway. Manual CA certificates create renewal toil, self-signed certificates trigger browser warnings, and KMS manages encryption keys rather than TLS certificates.

q: A company wants continuous, ML-powered threat detection across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs without deploying agents. Which service provides this?
options: AWS WAF
Amazon Inspector
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Artifact
explain: GuardDuty analyzes CloudTrail, Flow Logs, and DNS logs with machine learning to detect threats, with no agents required. WAF filters web requests, Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

q: A custom NACL allows inbound HTTP traffic, but return traffic is being blocked. What is the likely misconfiguration?
options: The NACL is missing outbound rules for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) — NACLs are stateless, so return traffic needs explicit rules
Security groups are stateful
The internet gateway is missing
The route table needs a NAT gateway
explain: Because NACLs are stateless, the inbound allow for port 80 doesn't cover the outbound ephemeral-port return traffic — it needs its own rule. Security groups being stateful is correct behavior, and gateway or route issues would block traffic in both directions.

q: A company must encrypt S3 objects with keys it can audit and disable independently, with a trail of key usage in CloudTrail. Which encryption option meets this?
options: SSE-S3 with Amazon S3-managed keys
Client-side encryption with hardcoded keys
No encryption; rely on bucket policies
SSE-KMS with a customer managed key — key usage is logged to CloudTrail and the key can be disabled independently
explain: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key gives independent key control, audit trails in CloudTrail, and the ability to disable the key. SSE-S3 offers no key visibility or independent control, hardcoded keys are insecure, and bucket policies don't encrypt data.

q: A mobile app needs user sign-up and sign-in with social identity providers and MFA, without building a custom authentication system. Which service provides managed user directories?
options: Create IAM users for each app customer
Amazon Cognito user pools
AWS Organizations
Security groups
explain: Cognito user pools provide managed sign-up, sign-in, social federation, and MFA out of the box. IAM users are for AWS operators, not app customers; Organizations manages accounts; security groups are network firewalls.

q: Applications in private subnets must call a third-party SaaS API exposed through AWS PrivateLink, without traffic traversing the internet. Which endpoint type is used?
options: Gateway endpoint
Internet gateway
Interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) with Private DNS enabled
NAT gateway
explain: Interface endpoints use PrivateLink to reach services privately, including third-party SaaS endpoints. Gateway endpoints only support S3 and DynamoDB, while internet and NAT gateways send traffic over the public internet.

q: A company with many AWS accounts wants to prevent any resource deployment outside approved Regions. Which control enforces this centrally?
options: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations denying actions outside the approved Regions
IAM identity policies on each user granting full access
AWS Budgets
Security groups
explain: SCPs set central guardrails across an organization, such as denying EC2 and other actions outside approved Regions. IAM policies grant permissions rather than restrict centrally, Budgets only alert on spend, and security groups control network traffic.

q: A company stores millions of objects in S3 and needs to discover where PII is stored to meet privacy requirements. Which service uses machine learning to find sensitive data in S3?
options: Amazon Athena
AWS Glue
Amazon CloudWatch
Amazon Macie
explain: Macie uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data like PII across S3 buckets. Athena queries data with SQL, Glue is ETL, and CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.

q: Which is the STRONGEST widely-adopted control to protect IAM user sign-ins against stolen passwords?
options: Longer passwords only
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) requiring a second factor such as a hardware key or virtual MFA device
Sharing passwords through encrypted email
Rotating passwords every 5 years
explain: MFA requires something the user has in addition to something they know, neutralizing stolen passwords. Longer passwords still fall to phishing, sharing passwords is never safe, and infrequent rotation doesn't stop credential theft.

q: Regulations require certain S3 records to be immutable (WORM) for 5 years, even against administrator action. Which feature enforces this?
options: S3 versioning alone
Bucket policies denying PutObject
S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a 5-year retention period
S3 lifecycle expiration
explain: Object Lock Compliance mode makes objects immutable for the retention period — not even the root user can shorten it. Versioning alone still allows version deletion, bucket policies can be changed, and lifecycle expiration deletes rather than preserves.

q: A company must encrypt all EBS volumes and RDS databases at rest using centrally managed keys. Which approach meets this with the LEAST effort?
options: Enable EBS default encryption and RDS encryption with AWS KMS customer managed keys
Encrypt data only in the application layer
Use unencrypted volumes behind a VPN
Manually encrypt each snapshot with a password
explain: EBS default encryption and RDS encryption with KMS apply transparently with centralized key management. Application-layer encryption adds code complexity, VPNs protect transit rather than stored data, and manual snapshot encryption doesn't scale.

q: A company uses Direct Connect for private connectivity, but compliance requires all traffic between on-premises and AWS to be encrypted. Which solution adds encryption?
options: Direct Connect is encrypted by default, so nothing is needed
Send the traffic over the public internet instead
Disable the Direct Connect connection
Run a Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection (or use MACsec) to encrypt traffic in transit
explain: Direct Connect is private but not encrypted by default; a VPN over the DX connection (or MACsec on dedicated connections) encrypts traffic in transit. The public internet would be less private, and disabling the connection removes connectivity entirely.

q: After a reorganization, the security team wants to find S3 buckets and IAM roles unintentionally shared outside the organization. Which tool identifies unintended external access?
options: AWS Cost Explorer
IAM Access Analyzer — analyzes resource policies to flag access granted to external principals
Amazon Inspector
AWS Trusted Advisor cost checks
explain: Access Analyzer evaluates resource-based policies and reports findings when external principals can access resources. Cost Explorer tracks spend, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor cost checks optimize billing.

q: A company keeps 7 years of compliance logs in S3 Standard. The logs are retrieved once or twice a year. Which change gives the BIGGEST cost reduction?
options: Enable S3 server access logging
Move the logs to S3 Standard-IA
Add a lifecycle policy transitioning objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive — the lowest-cost storage for rarely retrieved archives
Replicate the logs to a second Region
explain: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 storage class, designed for data retrieved a couple of times per year. Standard-IA is far pricier for archival data, access logging adds cost, and replication doubles storage spend.

q: A dataset has unpredictable access patterns — some objects stay hot while others go cold without warning. Which storage class optimizes cost automatically?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering — monitors access and moves objects between frequent and infrequent tiers automatically
S3 Standard for everything
S3 One Zone-IA for everything
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for everything
explain: Intelligent-Tiering automatically shifts objects between access tiers based on changing patterns, with no operational effort. Standard overpays for cold data, One Zone-IA penalizes objects accessed too soon, and Glacier retrieval latency breaks hot access.

q: A nightly batch rendering job is fault-tolerant and can handle interruptions. How can compute costs be reduced by up to 90%?
options: Use On-Demand instances
Buy Dedicated Hosts
Use larger instances
Run the job on EC2 Spot Instances — spare capacity at steep discounts for interruptible workloads
explain: Spot Instances offer up to 90% discounts for workloads that tolerate interruption, which fits a fault-tolerant batch job. On-Demand is full price, Dedicated Hosts are premium-priced, and larger instances increase cost without addressing the pricing model.

q: A company runs steady-state EC2 workloads 24/7 for the next 2 years across multiple instance families. Which pricing model gives the LOWEST cost with flexibility across instance types?
options: On-Demand
Compute Savings Plans — commit to a usage level for 1 or 3 years for deep discounts that apply across instance families and Regions
Spot Instances
Dedicated Hosts
explain: Compute Savings Plans discount steady usage up to 66% while remaining flexible across instance families, sizes, and Regions. On-Demand is full price, Spot doesn't suit steady-state needs, and Dedicated Hosts add premium cost.

q: A company wants better price-performance for its Linux-based EC2 and RDS workloads without rewriting code. Which option typically delivers this?
options: Switch to larger x86 instances
Move to Dedicated Hosts
Adopt AWS Graviton-based instances, which offer better price-performance for many Linux workloads
Disable EBS optimization
explain: Graviton processors deliver materially better price-performance for Linux workloads with no code changes in most cases. Larger x86 instances cost more, Dedicated Hosts add licensing-driven cost, and disabling EBS optimization hurts performance.

q: A company uses gp2 volumes and pays for IOPS by over-provisioning volume size. Which volume type lets them provision IOPS independently at lower cost?
options: gp3 — provision IOPS and throughput independently of volume size, at a lower price point than gp2
io2 — always cheaper than gp3
st1
Standard magnetic volumes
explain: gp3 decouples IOPS and throughput from capacity at about 20% lower cost than gp2, ending the over-provisioning practice. io2 is pricier and meant for higher IOPS or durability needs, while HDD types can't deliver provisioned IOPS.

q: A team wants an alert when forecasted monthly spend exceeds $10,000. Which service provides this?
options: AWS CloudTrail
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
AWS Budgets with forecasted spend alerts
explain: AWS Budgets tracks actual and forecasted spend against thresholds and sends alerts. CloudTrail audits API calls, GuardDuty detects threats, and Config evaluates compliance — none monitor spend.

q: A company suspects many EC2 instances are over-provisioned but doesn't know which ones. Which service uses machine learning on CloudWatch metrics to recommend optimal instance types?
options: AWS Artifact
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Systems Manager
Amazon Macie
explain: Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch utilization with ML to recommend rightsized instance types. Artifact hosts compliance reports, Systems Manager manages operations, and Macie finds sensitive data — none recommend instance sizing.

q: An internal tool runs a few times per day for under a minute each time, currently on an always-on EC2 instance. Which change is MOST cost-effective?
options: Buy a Reserved Instance for the EC2 host
Add an Application Load Balancer
Replatform to AWS Lambda — pay per invocation instead of paying for idle EC2 hours
Use a larger EC2 instance
explain: Lambda's per-invocation pricing eliminates paying for ~23 idle hours a day, which dwarfs any Reserved Instance discount on a mostly-idle host. A load balancer adds cost, and a larger instance makes the waste worse.

q: A development environment is only used 8 hours a day on weekdays. How can its cost be minimized with the LEAST effort?
options: Use scheduled scaling or Instance Scheduler to stop resources nights and weekends — stopped EC2 instances incur no compute charges
Run it 24/7 on Spot Instances
Buy 3-year Reserved Instances
Move the workloads to larger instances
explain: Stopping instances nights and weekends eliminates roughly 75% of compute hours with minimal setup. Spot still runs 24/7, Reserved Instances commit to full-time usage, and larger instances increase the hourly rate.

q: A database is idle most of the day with brief peaks. Which option eliminates paying for idle database capacity?
options: Aurora provisioned with Multi-AZ
RDS with a large instance
DynamoDB provisioned mode
Aurora Serverless v2 — scales capacity down automatically during idle periods and you pay for the capacity used
explain: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity down to a small minimum when idle and up instantly for peaks, so idle time costs almost nothing. Provisioned options charge for the instance around the clock regardless of use.

q: A new application's DynamoDB traffic is unpredictable — quiet for days, then viral spikes. Which capacity mode avoids both throttling and paying for unused capacity?
options: Provisioned mode with high fixed capacity
On-demand mode — pay per request with automatic scaling to any spike
Provisioned mode with auto scaling disabled
DAX with provisioned mode
explain: On-demand scales instantly to spikes and drops to near-zero cost when idle, with no throttling from under-provisioning. Fixed provisioned capacity either throttles or wastes money, and DAX is a cache rather than a capacity mode.

q: Backups are retrieved about once per quarter and need millisecond access when requested. Which is the MOST cost-effective storage class?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval — low-cost archive storage with millisecond retrieval for quarterly access
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
explain: Glacier Instant Retrieval is priced for archives accessed quarterly with millisecond retrieval needs. Standard overpays for archive data, Flexible Retrieval takes minutes to hours, and Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring fees better suited to unpredictable patterns.

q: Private EC2 instances transfer large volumes of data to S3 and DynamoDB through a NAT gateway, incurring data processing charges. How can these charges be eliminated?
options: Use VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB — traffic stays on the private AWS network with no data processing charges
Add more NAT gateways
Assign Elastic IPs to the instances
Enable VPC Flow Logs
explain: Gateway endpoints route S3 and DynamoDB traffic privately with no hourly or data processing charges. More NAT gateways multiply the charges, Elastic IPs don't change the data path, and Flow Logs only record traffic.

q: EBS snapshots are accumulating and the storage bill keeps growing. Which approach controls snapshot costs automatically?
options: Delete all snapshots
Copy snapshots to more Regions
Take snapshots more frequently
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM) to enforce retention policies that expire old snapshots
explain: DLM lifecycle policies automatically expire snapshots past their retention period, controlling growth with no manual work. Deleting everything destroys recovery points, more copies and more frequent snapshots increase cost.

q: Containerized batch jobs on Fargate are fault-tolerant. Which Fargate capacity provider reduces cost for interruptible work?
options: Fargate On-Demand
Fargate Spot — discounted spare capacity for fault-tolerant containers
EC2 Dedicated Hosts
Larger task sizes
explain: Fargate Spot offers deep discounts on spare capacity for containers that tolerate interruption. On-Demand is full price, Dedicated Hosts are premium-priced, and larger tasks increase resource consumption.

q: A company stores infrequently accessed thumbnails that are easily regenerated if lost. Which is the MOST cost-effective sufficiently durable option?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 One Zone-IA — the lowest-cost infrequent-access storage for reproducible data that doesn't need multi-AZ resilience
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
explain: One Zone-IA is the cheapest infrequent-access class and fits reproducible data where an AZ loss is acceptable. Standard overpays, Deep Archive retrieval is too slow for thumbnails, and Intelligent-Tiering adds fees for a predictable pattern.

q: A finance team wants to identify the top cost drivers by service and find rightsizing opportunities across accounts. Which tool provides interactive cost analysis?
options: AWS Cost Explorer — visualizes spend by service, account, and tags, with rightsizing recommendations
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon Inspector
VPC Reachability Analyzer
explain: Cost Explorer breaks down spend by service, account, and tags with built-in rightsizing recommendations. CloudTrail audits API calls, Inspector scans vulnerabilities, and Reachability Analyzer troubleshoots network paths — none analyze cost.

q: A development team accidentally ran a destructive UPDATE against the production Aurora MySQL cluster 20 minutes ago. They need to rewind the cluster to just before the bad transaction without restoring from a snapshot and without changing the cluster endpoint. Which feature meets this requirement?
options: Perform a point-in-time restore to a brand-new cluster
Use Aurora Backtrack to rewind the DB cluster in place to a specific point in time
Enable Multi-AZ deployment on the cluster
Restore the cluster from the most recent automated snapshot
explain: Aurora Backtrack rewinds a cluster in place to a point within the backtrack window (up to 72 hours) with no new cluster and no endpoint change. Point-in-time restore and snapshot restore both create a new cluster with a new endpoint, and Multi-AZ handles AZ failover, not rewinding bad transactions.

q: A company runs stateful workers on EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. When instances are terminated during scale-in, in-flight jobs are killed abruptly and customers see errors. The team needs instances to finish their current jobs and deregister cleanly before termination completes. Which feature should they use?
options: Lifecycle hooks that pause termination until a custom action (such as draining in-flight jobs) signals completion
Increase the desired capacity of the group permanently
Disable all health checks on the Auto Scaling group
Migrate the workers to larger instance types
explain: Lifecycle hooks put the instance in a wait state (Terminating:Wait) so a script or Lambda can drain jobs and deregister the worker before termination proceeds. More capacity doesn't make termination graceful, disabling health checks removes protection, and larger instances still get terminated mid-job.

q: A company operates its application in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. The us-east-1 deployment is much larger, so the team wants roughly 80% of global traffic served from us-east-1 and 20% from eu-west-1, shifting traffic by configurable bias rather than by user geography. Which Route 53 routing policy supports this?
options: Failover routing
Geolocation routing
Geoproximity routing with bias values
Multivalue answer routing
explain: Geoproximity routing steers traffic based on the geographic distance to resources plus an adjustable bias that expands or shrinks a Region's catchment area. Failover is strictly primary/secondary, geolocation routes purely by user location with no bias control, and multivalue answer routing returns multiple healthy records without distance awareness.

q: A single EC2 instance hosts a legacy application that cannot run on multiple instances. The instance must recover automatically if the underlying host hardware fails, with minimal administrative effort. Which solution provides this?
options: Place the instance in an Auto Scaling group with a minimum of one
Create AMIs of the instance every night
Replatform the application to Lambda
Configure a CloudWatch alarm on the StatusCheckFailed_System metric to trigger EC2 automatic recovery of the instance
explain: EC2 automatic recovery migrates the instance to healthy hardware when system status checks fail, which is exactly the host-failure scenario, and it works for single instances. An Auto Scaling group replaces rather than recovers the instance (new instance ID, new data unless scripted), AMIs require manual restore, and Lambda requires replatforming.

q: A team must upgrade its production RDS for PostgreSQL engine version with near-zero downtime and a fast rollback path if the new version misbehaves. Which approach is BEST?
options: Run an in-place major version upgrade during the maintenance window
Use RDS Blue/Green Deployments — build a green environment with the new engine version, switch over when validated, and keep the blue environment for fast rollback
Restore the latest snapshot into a new instance running the new engine version
Create a read replica and promote it during the upgrade
explain: Blue/Green Deployments create a synchronized staging (green) environment for the upgrade, switchover takes about a minute, and the original blue environment remains available for instant rollback. In-place upgrades cause longer downtime and risky rollbacks, snapshot restores lose data written after the snapshot, and a read replica promotion doesn't test the new engine version.

q: An order workflow orchestrated by Step Functions calls a payment API that occasionally returns throttling errors. The workflow must retry the call with exponential backoff and, after repeated failures, route the order to a manual review queue instead of failing silently. Which design meets this requirement?
options: Configure Retry with exponential backoff on the task state, plus a Catch block that sends the order to an SQS queue for manual review
Remove the payment step from the workflow
Increase the memory of the Lambda functions in the workflow
Run the workflow synchronously inside the web tier
explain: Retry with backoff handles transient throttling automatically, and Catch routes exhausted failures to a review queue so no order is lost silently. Removing the payment step breaks the business flow, memory doesn't fix throttling, and synchronous web-tier execution loses the orchestration's durability.

q: A company uses Amazon EFS for shared content in us-east-1 and needs a continuously updated copy in eu-west-1 for disaster recovery, with automatic failover of mount targets. Which solution provides this with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Run rsync between EC2 instances on a cron schedule
Take EBS snapshots and copy them across Regions
Enable EFS replication to the second Region
Write scripts that sync files to S3 and back
explain: EFS replication continuously replicates the file system to another Region as a managed feature with no scripts to maintain. rsync and S3-sync scripts are fragile and operationally heavy, and EBS snapshots don't replicate a live shared file system.

q: A global company runs active-active across two Regions. During an incident it needs a single control to instantly shift 100% of traffic away from a Region, plus pre-deployment checks verifying that scaling limits, health checks, and IAM permissions are correctly configured before failover is ever needed. Which service provides these capabilities?
options: Route 53 weighted routing records
CloudWatch alarms alone
ELB target group health checks
Route 53 Application Recovery Controller, with routing controls for instant traffic shifts and readiness checks for pre-deployment validation
explain: Application Recovery Controller provides routing controls (highly available on/off switches for traffic shifting) and readiness checks that audit recovery prerequisites across Regions. Weighted routing changes DNS gradually rather than instantly, and CloudWatch or ELB checks alone don't provide the traffic-shift control plane or readiness auditing.

q: A company runs a large Spot-based batch fleet. When EC2 issues a Spot interruption notice, running jobs are killed abruptly and must restart from scratch. Which feature proactively replaces Spot Instances that are at elevated risk of interruption?
options: On-Demand Capacity Reservations
EC2 Auto Scaling capacity rebalance — launches replacement Spot Instances when existing ones are flagged at elevated interruption risk
Disabling Spot Instances entirely
Moving the fleet to larger instance types
explain: Capacity rebalance monitors the EC2 Spot rebalance recommendation signal and proactively launches replacements before interruption, so jobs can drain gracefully. Capacity Reservations are for On-Demand, disabling Spot abandons the discount, and larger instances are interrupted just the same.

q: An Aurora MySQL cluster has five read replicas. During a failover, the company wants a specific replica — the one in the same AZ as the application tier — to be promoted first to minimize latency after failover. How can this be controlled?
options: Assign promotion priority tiers to the Aurora Replicas so the preferred replica is chosen first
Enable Multi-AZ deployment on the cluster
Increase the instance size of the preferred replica
Convert the cluster to an Aurora Global Database
explain: Aurora lets each replica carry a promotion priority tier (0-15); the lowest-numbered healthy tier is promoted first, giving deterministic failover order. Multi-AZ doesn't control which replica wins, instance size doesn't affect promotion order, and Global Database addresses cross-region rather than failover priority.

q: A company replicates critical data cross-region with S3 replication and has a compliance requirement that replication complete within 15 minutes, with visibility into whether objects actually replicated on time. Which feature meets this requirement?
options: Standard S3 cross-region replication, which offers no time SLA
S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket
S3 Batch Replication for existing objects
S3 Replication Time Control (RTC), which backs replication with a 15-minute SLA and CloudWatch metrics
explain: RTC provides a 15-minute replication SLA with metrics (and S3 event notifications on SLA breach) for compliance reporting. Standard replication is best-effort with no time guarantee, Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than replication, and Batch Replication is a one-time backfill job, not ongoing SLA-backed replication.

q: An application experiences sudden traffic surges, and new EC2 instances take 4 minutes to initialize, causing latency spikes during every scale-out event. Which Auto Scaling feature keeps pre-initialized instances ready so scale-out is nearly instant?
options: Scheduled scaling actions
Warm pools — maintain pre-initialized stopped or running instances that join the group immediately on scale-out
Building larger AMIs
Step scaling policies
explain: Warm pools keep instances initialized (and optionally stopped to save cost) so scale-out adds ready capacity in seconds instead of minutes. Scheduled scaling handles predictable patterns but not initialization time, larger AMIs don't shorten boot, and step scaling still launches cold instances.

q: A stateful application on EC2 takes 10 minutes to warm its in-memory cache after every reboot. The instance is stopped overnight to save cost, but the RAM contents must survive stop/start cycles. Which feature preserves memory across a stop and start?
options: Instance store volumes
EBS snapshots taken before each stop
EC2 hibernation — saves RAM contents to the EBS root volume and restores them on start
An Auto Scaling group with a minimum of one
explain: Hibernation persists in-memory state to the root EBS volume on stop and restores it on start, so the cache survives. Instance store data is lost on stop, snapshots require manual restore steps, and Auto Scaling replaces instances rather than preserving their RAM.

q: A company runs active-passive application servers in private subnets across two VPCs connected by Transit Gateway, and wants Route 53 to fail over DNS between them based on health checks. Route 53 health checkers on the public internet cannot reach the private endpoints. Which approach enables health-based failover for these private resources?
options: Create standard HTTP health checks against the private IP addresses
Use weighted routing with manual weight changes
Use geolocation routing
Create CloudWatch alarms on metrics from the private endpoints and base Route 53 health checks on the alarm state
explain: Route 53 supports health checks based on CloudWatch alarm state, which bridges the gap for resources its internet-based checkers can't reach directly. Standard health checks against private IPs will always fail, and weighted or geolocation routing without health awareness can't fail over automatically.

q: An RDS database grows unpredictably, and the team fears an outage caused by the storage filling up completely. Which feature automatically increases allocated storage before it runs out?
options: RDS storage autoscaling — automatically scales storage when free space drops below a threshold
Taking manual snapshots more frequently
Adding read replicas
Enabling Multi-AZ deployment
explain: Storage autoscaling monitors free space and grows the volume automatically within a configured maximum, preventing full-disk outages. Snapshots don't free or add space, read replicas don't add primary storage, and Multi-AZ is about failover, not capacity.

q: An ALB spans three AZs, but 90% of the registered targets are in one AZ, and that AZ's instances are overloaded while the others sit idle. Which ALB setting distributes incoming traffic evenly across all registered targets regardless of which AZ they are in?
options: Sticky sessions
Cross-zone load balancing
Connection draining
Slow start mode
explain: Cross-zone load balancing spreads each AZ's traffic across targets in all enabled AZs instead of only local targets. Sticky sessions pin users to specific targets, connection draining only affects deregistration timing, and slow start ramps traffic to new targets — none rebalance across AZs.

q: A company processes order events through EventBridge to a Lambda consumer. A bug in the consumer caused two hours of failed processing, and the team needs to reprocess exactly the events from that window. Which EventBridge feature enables this?
options: Configuring a dead-letter queue on the event bus
EventBridge Scheduler
EventBridge archives with event replay — re-send the archived events from the time window back to the bus
Increasing the Lambda function's reserved concurrency
explain: Archives store events durably and replay re-sends a filtered time range to the event bus or another target, which is exactly the recovery pattern. A DLQ only captures failed deliveries rather than the full event history, Scheduler triggers new events on a timetable, and concurrency doesn't recover lost processing.

q: A company's primary site runs on EC2 behind an ALB in us-east-1. For regional disaster recovery on a tight budget, the team wants Route 53 to fail over to a static maintenance page hosted in a second Region. Which is the MOST cost-effective secondary target?
options: A full replica of the application stack in the second Region
S3 static website hosting in the second Region serving the maintenance page
A second ALB with no registered targets
A CloudFront distribution with no origin configured
explain: S3 static website hosting costs pennies and serves the maintenance page with high durability, making it the cheapest viable failover target. A full replica stack is the most expensive option, an ALB with no targets serves nothing, and a CloudFront distribution without an origin can't serve content.

q: An application uses Aurora Global Database with the primary cluster in us-east-1. Application servers in eu-west-1 suffer high write latency because every write round-trips to the primary Region. Which feature lets the secondary cluster accept writes locally and forward them to the primary without application changes?
options: Write forwarding — the secondary cluster accepts writes and forwards them to the primary cluster
Adding cross-region read replicas
Enabling Aurora Backtrack
Cloning the primary cluster into eu-west-1
explain: Write forwarding lets applications in a secondary Region issue writes against the local cluster endpoint, which forwards them to the primary — cutting an application round trip. Read replicas don't accept writes, Backtrack rewinds data changes, and cloning creates a point-in-time copy, not a live write path.

q: An e-commerce site has predictable traffic spikes every weekday at 9 AM plus unpredictable flash-sale spikes throughout the day. Which Auto Scaling combination handles both patterns?
options: Manual scaling by an operator each morning
Step scaling policies alone
Scheduled scaling actions alone
Scheduled scaling for the predictable 9 AM spike plus target tracking policies for unpredictable demand
explain: Scheduled scaling pre-provisions capacity for the known 9 AM spike, while target tracking reacts to the unpredictable flash-sale demand in real time. Manual scaling is slow and error-prone, step scaling alone can't pre-warm for the predictable spike, and scheduled scaling alone can't react to surprises.

q: A company has Transit Gateways in three Regions and needs resilient, encrypted inter-region connectivity between its VPCs without managing VPN appliances. Which solution connects the Transit Gateways?
options: VPC peering between Regions
Routing inter-region traffic over the public internet
Transit Gateway inter-region peering
Direct Connect gateways only
explain: Transit Gateway peering connects Transit Gateways across Regions over the AWS backbone with built-in encryption and no appliances to manage. Inter-region VPC peering doesn't exist as a peering primitive for Transit Gateways, public internet routing is insecure, and Direct Connect gateways connect on-premises networks rather than Transit Gateways to each other.

q: A company needs its RDS automated backups copied to a second Region daily for disaster recovery, managed centrally with consistent retention across multiple accounts. Which solution provides this with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: AWS Backup with backup plans that include cross-region copy rules and cross-account management
Manually copying snapshots to the second Region each day
AWS DMS ongoing replication to the second Region
Creating cross-region read replicas and snapshotting those
explain: AWS Backup centralizes backup scheduling, retention, cross-region copies, and cross-account management in backup plans. Manual snapshot copies are toil-prone, DMS is a migration/replication engine rather than a backup service, and snapshotting read replicas adds unnecessary moving parts.

q: A company pages on-call engineers whenever any single EC2 CPU alarm fires, causing alert fatigue from false positives during deployments. Which CloudWatch feature reduces noise by requiring a combination of conditions before alerting?
options: Detailed monitoring on all instances
Composite alarms — combine multiple alarms with boolean logic so the alert fires only when the real failure condition holds
Creating even more granular alarms
Streaming metrics to CloudWatch Logs
explain: Composite alarms evaluate expressions like ALARM(cpu_high) AND ALARM(error_rate_high), suppressing pages from single-metric blips during deployments. Detailed monitoring increases metric frequency rather than reducing noise, more alarms multiply the pages, and Logs streaming is for analysis rather than alerting logic.

q: A company replicates objects to S3 buckets in three Regions and wants applications to use a single global endpoint that automatically routes each request to the closest healthy bucket copy. Which feature provides this?
options: Cross-region replication alone, which does not provide a unified endpoint
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Select
S3 Multi-Region Access Points — a global endpoint that routes to the lowest-latency healthy replica
explain: Multi-Region Access Points provide one global endpoint backed by active-active bucket replicas, with automatic routing to the lowest-latency healthy copy. Replication alone leaves applications to pick buckets themselves, Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to one bucket, and S3 Select filters object content.
