explain: Neptune supports up to 15 read replicas including cross-Region replicas, placing read capacity near analysts to cut latency. Streams capture change data rather than serving reads, vertical scaling has hard limits, and DynamoDB is a key-value/document store rather than a graph engine.

q: A document database workload on Amazon DocumentDB has unpredictable read/write spikes and the team wants the cluster to scale throughput automatically without manual instance changes. Which DocumentDB deployment option provides elastic scaling?
options: Fixed db.r6g.large instances
Read replicas added manually
Sharding the application across collections
DocumentDB elastic clusters, which automatically scale compute and storage with workload demand
explain: DocumentDB elastic clusters automatically scale compute capacity with demand, removing manual instance resizing for spiky workloads. Fixed instances require manual changes, manual replicas don't scale writes, and application-level sharding adds complexity the managed elastic option avoids.

q: A real-time bidding platform needs sub-millisecond data access with strong durability guarantees — data loss on failover is unacceptable. Which in-memory service provides both speed and Multi-AZ durability?
options: ElastiCache for Redis with cluster mode
Amazon MemoryDB for Redis, which provides sub-millisecond reads with a durable transaction log and Multi-AZ failover
DynamoDB with DAX
An EC2-hosted Redis with RDB snapshots
explain: MemoryDB combines in-memory sub-millisecond performance with a durable transaction log and Multi-AZ failover, so no committed data is lost. ElastiCache is primarily a cache with weaker durability guarantees, DAX accelerates DynamoDB rather than providing Redis semantics, and EC2-hosted Redis snapshots risk data loss between snapshots.

q: A global video platform's origin is overwhelmed by cache misses: many CloudFront edge locations each fetch the same objects from the origin independently. Which feature collapses those requests into a single origin fetch per Region?
options: CloudFront Origin Shield, which adds a regional caching layer so edges fetch from Shield instead of hammering the origin
Increasing the TTL on all cache behaviors
Adding more origin servers
Enabling CloudFront signed URLs
explain: Origin Shield inserts a regional mid-tier cache so all edges in a Region collapse to one origin request, dramatically cutting origin load. Longer TTLs don't help uncacheable or first-fetch misses, more origins add cost without collapsing requests, and signed URLs control access rather than reducing origin fetches.

q: A hybrid application replicates large datasets between an on-premises data center and VPCs in three AWS Regions. The team wants private, consistent-throughput connectivity to all three Regions over a single connection. Which Direct Connect topology fits?
options: Three separate Direct Connect connections, one per Region
A Site-to-Site VPN to each Region
A Direct Connect gateway, which attaches one connection to VPCs in multiple Regions over private VIFs
Public VIFs with IPsec to each Region
explain: A Direct Connect gateway associates a single connection with VPCs across multiple Regions via private virtual interfaces, giving consistent private throughput everywhere. Separate connections triple cost and complexity, VPNs lack consistent throughput, and public VIFs traverse public paths rather than private ones.

q: An EMR Spark cluster is manually sized for peak load and sits idle 70% of the time, yet jobs occasionally need far more capacity than the fixed cluster provides. Which EMR feature automatically resizes the cluster to the workload?
options: EMR managed scaling, which automatically adds or removes instances based on workload demand
Fixed instance fleets with Spot only
Running all jobs on the master node
Disabling YARN dynamic allocation
explain: EMR managed scaling automatically adjusts cluster size to workload demand, cutting idle cost while handling bursts. Fixed Spot fleets still require manual sizing, running jobs on the master node risks cluster stability, and disabling YARN dynamic allocation reduces elasticity rather than adding it.

q: An IoT platform ingests millions of timestamped sensor readings per day and needs fast time-range queries with automatic data lifecycle management. Which purpose-built AWS database fits best?
options: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with table partitioning
Amazon Timestream, a serverless time-series database with built-in tiered storage for hot and historical data
Amazon Neptune for sensor relationships
DynamoDB with a composite sort key
explain: Timestream is purpose-built for time-series ingestion with automatic tiering between in-memory and magnetic stores and SQL time-range queries. RDS partitioning requires manual management, Neptune models graphs rather than time series, and DynamoDB needs significant custom design for time-range efficiency.

q: A company runs 20 microservices as ECS tasks and wants a single ALB to route to each service by URL path, with services discovering each other without hardcoded endpoints. Which ECS networking feature provides service-to-service discovery and routing?
options: ECS Service Connect, which provides service discovery, load balancing, and observability between ECS services
Assigning public IPs to every task
Hardcoding task IPs in environment variables
Running all services in one task definition
explain: ECS Service Connect gives ECS services automatic discovery, traffic routing, and health-aware load balancing between services without hardcoded addresses. Public IPs expose services unnecessarily, hardcoded IPs break on redeploys, and cramming services into one task definition destroys independent scaling.

q: A SaaS API serves users on five continents from a single Region, and distant users complain about latency. The team wants DNS to route each user to the lowest-latency of three regional deployments. Which Route 53 policy optimizes for latency?
options: Weighted routing with manual weights
Geolocation routing by continent
Latency-based routing, which directs users to the Region with the lowest measured latency from their location
Failover routing with health checks
explain: Latency-based routing measures network latency from the user to each Region and returns the fastest endpoint, directly addressing the complaint. Weighted routing splits traffic arbitrarily, geolocation routes by geography which doesn't equal lowest latency, and failover routing is active-passive rather than performance-based.

q: A database volume is running out of space during business hours. The team believes resizing requires downtime and a maintenance window. Which EBS capability allows changing volume type and size live?
options: Creating a new volume from a snapshot during off-hours
Detaching the volume, resizing, and reattaching
Stopping the instance before any modification
EBS elastic volumes, which allow modifying size, IOPS, and volume type while the volume stays attached and in service
explain: EBS elastic volumes support live modification of size, provisioned IOPS, and volume type with no downtime or detachment. Snapshot-based replacement requires cutover downtime, detach/reattach interrupts the workload, and stopping the instance is exactly the downtime the team wants to avoid.

q: A company replicates encrypted EBS snapshots to a second Region for DR. The secondary Region's applications need to decrypt the data, but the KMS key exists only in the primary Region. Which KMS feature provides a usable key in both Regions under one key ID?
options: Exporting the key material to a file
Multi-Region KMS keys, which replicate key material across Regions so the same key ID decrypts in either Region
Sharing the snapshot without re-encryption
Using the AWS-managed EBS default key in both Regions
explain: Multi-Region keys replicate the same key material to other Regions under a shared key ID, so data encrypted in one Region decrypts in another. Exported key material can't be imported into KMS for EBS use, unshared snapshots aren't accessible cross-account, and the AWS-managed default key is Region-scoped and can't decrypt the primary's ciphertext.

q: Three teams share one S3 bucket holding a common dataset, but each team must only access its own prefix, and access is granted through the corporate identity provider. Which S3 feature maps IdP identities directly to prefix-level permissions at scale?
options: One bucket policy with hardcoded team ARNs
Separate buckets per team with full replication
S3 Block Public Access at the account level
S3 Access Grants, which map corporate identities to S3 prefixes with least-privilege permissions
explain: S3 Access Grants map IdP users and groups directly to specific bucket prefixes, scaling least-privilege access without giant bucket policies. Hardcoded bucket policies become unmanageable, separate buckets duplicate the dataset, and Block Public Access controls public exposure rather than granting team access.

q: Account A needs read access to an S3 bucket in Account B. The bucket policy must allow the access only when the request comes from within the company's AWS Organization, guarding against the confused-deputy problem. Which IAM condition key enforces this?
options: aws:PrincipalOrgID, which restricts access to principals belonging to the specified AWS Organization
aws:SourceIp with the corporate office range
aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent
s3:ExistingObjectTag with a team tag
explain: aws:PrincipalOrgID in the bucket policy ensures only principals from your Organization can assume the access, blocking external confused-deputy misuse. SourceIp doesn't cover remote or VPC-based callers, MFA presence doesn't prove organizational membership, and object tags don't identify the calling principal's organization.

q: A payment service must decrypt cardholder data on EC2, but compliance forbids the decryption keys and plaintext from being accessible to the host OS, administrators, or other processes on the instance. Which EC2 capability provides an isolated execution environment for this?
options: EC2 Instance Connect
Encrypted EBS volumes
AWS Nitro Enclaves, which provide isolated compute with no persistent storage, no administrator access, and no networking to the parent instance
Security groups restricting SSH
explain: Nitro Enclaves create a hardened, isolated enclave alongside the EC2 instance with no persistent storage, no admin access, and no inbound networking — designed exactly for sensitive processing like decryption. Instance Connect manages SSH access, EBS encryption protects data at rest rather than in use, and security groups only filter network traffic.

q: A bank must manage its own encryption keys in dedicated, single-tenant hardware outside of AWS's shared infrastructure, while still using them with AWS services. Which KMS option keeps key material in an external key manager under the bank's control?
options: AWS-managed KMS keys
KMS External Key Store (XKS), which lets KMS use keys stored in an external hardware security module outside AWS
S3-managed SSE-S3 encryption
Storing keys in Secrets Manager
explain: External Key Store integrates KMS with keys held in the customer's own external HSM, so AWS never stores the key material. AWS-managed keys live in shared KMS infrastructure, SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys, and Secrets Manager stores secrets rather than providing external key custody.

q: An audit found unencrypted EBS volumes launched by developers who forgot to enable encryption. The team wants encryption enforced automatically for all new volumes and snapshots in the account. Which setting provides this guardrail?
options: An SCP denying ec2:RunInstances
A CloudWatch alarm on volume creation
Enabling EBS Snapshot Block Public Access
EBS encryption by default, which automatically encrypts all new EBS volumes and snapshots in the Region
explain: EBS encryption by default automatically encrypts every new volume and snapshot in the Region, removing reliance on developers remembering the checkbox. Denying RunInstances blocks launches entirely, alarms only notify after the fact, and snapshot block-public-access controls sharing rather than encryption.

q: A company suspects compromised credentials are being used to list and exfiltrate data from S3, and needs automated discovery of sensitive data across hundreds of buckets to scope the exposure. Which service uses machine learning to find PII in S3?
options: Amazon Macie, which uses ML to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII across S3 buckets
AWS Config rules for bucket policies
Amazon Inspector for S3
VPC Flow Logs for S3 endpoints
explain: Macie applies machine learning to discover, classify, and alert on sensitive data like PII and credentials across S3 at scale. Config evaluates configuration compliance rather than content, Inspector scans compute and images rather than bucket contents, and Flow Logs capture network metadata rather than data classification.

q: After a GuardDuty finding flags suspicious behavior on an EC2 instance, responders need a visual timeline of related API calls, logins, and network connections to determine blast radius. Which service builds investigation graphs from the findings?
options: AWS CloudTrail Lake queries
AWS Security Hub custom insights
Amazon Detective, which correlates GuardDuty, CloudTrail, and VPC Flow Logs into visual investigation graphs
AWS Config timeline views
explain: Detective automatically builds entity graphs linking findings to related API activity, authentications, and network flows for rapid scoping. CloudTrail Lake requires manual SQL investigation, Security Hub aggregates findings without behavioral graphs, and Config tracks resource configuration history rather than attack timelines.

q: A gaming company is launching a popular title and expects large volumetric DDoS attacks against its ALBs. They need automatic Layer 3/4 mitigation plus access to a 24/7 response team and cost protection against scaling during attacks. Which service provides all three?
options: AWS WAF with managed rules
AWS Shield Advanced, which adds automatic DDoS mitigation, the Shield Response Team (SRT), and cost protection
Security groups with rate limiting
CloudFront signed URLs
explain: Shield Advanced provides always-on L3/L4 DDoS detection and mitigation, 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team, and cost protection against usage spikes during attacks. WAF handles Layer 7 rules rather than volumetric absorption, security groups can't absorb DDoS scale, and signed URLs control content access rather than mitigating attacks.

q: A security team needs to guarantee DNS responses for their domain haven't been tampered with in transit, protecting users from DNS spoofing and cache poisoning. Which Route 53 feature provides cryptographic DNS integrity?
options: Route 53 health checks
Private hosted zones
Route 53 Resolver query logging
DNSSEC signing in Route 53, which cryptographically signs DNS responses so resolvers can validate authenticity
explain: DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures to DNS records so validating resolvers can detect spoofed or tampered responses. Health checks monitor endpoint availability, private hosted zones serve internal names, and query logging records lookups without authenticating responses.

q: A checkout form collects credit card numbers that must be encrypted at the CloudFront edge before the origin ever sees plaintext, so a compromised origin can't leak card data. Which CloudFront feature encrypts specific form fields at the edge?
options: CloudFront field-level encryption, which encrypts designated sensitive fields at edge locations using the origin's public key
Origin Access Control for S3
CloudFront Functions for header rewrites
Signed cookies for premium content
explain: Field-level encryption encrypts specified form fields at the edge with the customer's public key, so only the holder of the private key can decrypt — the origin never sees plaintext. Origin Access Control secures S3 origins, Functions transform requests rather than encrypting fields, and signed cookies authorize content access.

q: A company runs dozens of microservices on ECS and EKS and needs fine-grained, identity-based authorization between services without managing mutual TLS certificates everywhere. Which AWS service provides service-to-service auth policies?
options: AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints
Security groups referencing other security groups
Amazon VPC Lattice, which provides auth policies for service-to-service access based on IAM identities
Route 53 private hosted zones
explain: VPC Lattice applies IAM-based auth policies to service network traffic, giving identity-aware service-to-service authorization without certificate management. PrivateLink exposes services privately but doesn't authorize between them, security groups filter by network rather than identity, and private DNS only resolves names.

q: Remote employees need secure access to private resources in a VPC from their laptops, with authentication tied to client certificates issued by the company CA. Which Client VPN authentication option uses company-issued certificates?
options: Active Directory authentication only
Mutual authentication with client certificates, where the VPN endpoint validates certificates issued by the company's CA
SAML federation without certificates
Security group rules on the VPN endpoint
explain: Client VPN mutual authentication validates client certificates against the company's CA, binding access to issued device certificates. AD authentication uses directory credentials rather than certificates, SAML federates web identity without client certs, and security groups filter traffic rather than authenticating users.

q: A financial firm runs production workloads that depend on a Direct Connect connection and must encrypt all traffic on the dedicated connection at line rate to meet compliance. Which Direct Connect security feature provides MAC-layer encryption?
options: IPsec VPN over the public VIF
Security groups on the Direct Connect gateway
Enabling jumbo frames on the VIF
MACsec on dedicated 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps connections, encrypting traffic at the link layer
explain: MACsec provides line-rate Layer 2 encryption on supported dedicated Direct Connect connections, meeting compliance without VPN overhead. IPsec over a public VIF adds tunneling complexity and throughput limits, security groups don't apply to Direct Connect, and jumbo frames affect MTU rather than encryption.

q: A company keeps database backups in an S3 bucket in its production account. An attacker who compromises an admin could delete the backups, so the team wants version-level protection requiring an additional authentication factor for deletions. Which S3 feature requires MFA to delete object versions?
options: S3 MFA Delete, which requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete object versions in a versioned bucket
S3 Versioning alone
S3 Object Lock in governance mode
Cross-region replication of the bucket
explain: MFA Delete requires an MFA code to delete object versions or suspend versioning, so a compromised admin credential alone can't destroy backups. Versioning alone still allows deletion of versions, governance-mode Object Lock can be overridden by privileged users, and replication copies data without blocking deletes.

q: A platform team manages hundreds of EC2 instances and wants to eliminate SSH bastion hosts and long-lived key pairs, while keeping full audit logs of every administrative session. Which Systems Manager capability replaces SSH with audited browser/CLI sessions?
options: Systems Manager Patch Manager
Systems Manager Inventory
Session Manager, which provides audited shell access through IAM authentication with every command logged to S3 or CloudWatch
Systems Manager Parameter Store
explain: Session Manager grants shell access authenticated via IAM with no open inbound ports or SSH keys, logging all session activity to S3 or CloudWatch Logs. Patch Manager handles OS patching, Inventory collects software metadata, and Parameter Store holds configuration — none replace interactive SSH access.

q: A support engineer occasionally needs SSH access to EC2 instances, but the security team forbids distributing long-lived private keys. Which EC2 feature issues short-lived SSH keys tied to IAM permissions?
options: Storing private keys in Secrets Manager
EC2 Instance Connect, which pushes ephemeral SSH public keys authorized by IAM policy for one-time use
Opening port 22 to the corporate office
Using the EC2 key pair with a passphrase
explain: EC2 Instance Connect issues short-lived SSH keys authorized through IAM policies, eliminating long-lived key distribution. Secrets Manager still distributes persistent keys, opening port 22 broadens attack surface, and passphrases don't expire the underlying key.

q: After a security incident, responders need full packet captures from specific EC2 instances to analyze attacker traffic, without installing agents. Which VPC feature mirrors instance traffic to an analysis appliance?
options: VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch
Security group logging
CloudTrail data events
VPC Traffic Mirroring, which copies network traffic from ENIs to a target for inspection
explain: Traffic Mirroring replicates raw packets from elastic network interfaces to a monitoring target for deep inspection with IDS or forensic tools. Flow Logs capture only metadata summaries, security groups don't log, and CloudTrail records API calls rather than network packets.

q: EC2 instances must resolve external domains for updates, but the security team wants to block DNS queries to known malware and data-exfiltration domains at the resolver level. Which Route 53 Resolver feature enforces domain blocklists?
options: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, which filters outbound DNS queries against managed and custom domain lists
Route 53 public hosted zones
VPC DHCP option sets
Enabling DNS hostnames on subnets
explain: Resolver DNS Firewall inspects outbound DNS queries and blocks those matching threat or custom blocklists, stopping malware callbacks and DNS tunneling. Public hosted zones serve authoritative records, DHCP option sets configure resolvers rather than filtering, and DNS hostnames only affect internal naming.

q: A company stores API keys for a third-party SaaS product in Secrets Manager in us-east-1, but its DR region eu-west-1 also needs those secrets available during a regional failover. How should the team make secrets available in both Regions?
options: Copying secret values into Parameter Store manually
Hardcoding fallback values in application config
Replicating the secret to eu-west-1 with Secrets Manager multi-Region replication
Sharing the secret via a public S3 bucket
explain: Secrets Manager supports replicating secrets to additional Regions, keeping values synchronized and available for DR failover. Manual Parameter Store copies drift out of sync, hardcoded fallbacks expose secrets and go stale, and a public S3 bucket destroys confidentiality.

q: An EKS application needs to read objects from S3, but the team refuses to embed long-lived AWS credentials in pods. Which IAM mechanism gives each pod short-lived, scoped credentials?
options: EC2 instance profiles shared by all pods
IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA), which uses OIDC federation to grant pods temporary credentials for a specific IAM role
Hardcoded access keys in Kubernetes secrets
A single IAM user for the whole cluster
explain: IRSA federates the cluster's OIDC provider with IAM so each service account assumes its own role with temporary credentials — no long-lived keys in pods. Shared instance profiles over-permit every pod, hardcoded keys risk exposure, and one IAM user for the cluster violates least privilege.

q: A SaaS vendor needs read-only access to a customer's S3 bucket. The customer wants to grant access that automatically expires and can be revoked centrally without touching the bucket policy each time. Which KMS-adjacent IAM mechanism provides temporary delegated permissions?
options: IAM permission boundaries
Cross-account IAM roles with sts:AssumeRole and time-limited sessions, revocable centrally
Sharing the root access keys
S3 ACLs with the vendor's canonical ID
explain: Cross-account IAM roles with AssumeRole provide temporary, centrally revocable, time-limited access without sharing long-term credentials. Permission boundaries limit maximum permissions rather than granting access, root keys must never be shared, and S3 ACLs are legacy and harder to revoke centrally.

q: Users upload files to an S3 bucket that are later processed by backend systems. The team wants browsers to upload directly to S3 with enforced file-size limits and key prefixes, without routing bytes through the application. Which mechanism supports constrained direct uploads?
options: S3 pre-signed POSTs with policy conditions enforcing content-length-range and key prefixes
Public write access on the bucket
Proxying uploads through an EC2 fleet
S3 Transfer Acceleration alone
explain: Pre-signed POST policies enforce conditions like content-length-range and starts-with key prefixes, letting browsers upload directly while the app never handles the bytes. Public write access invites abuse, proxying through EC2 adds cost and latency, and Transfer Acceleration only speeds transfers without constraining them.

q: A company deploys dozens of Lambda functions and wants to ensure OS patches are applied fleet-wide with compliance reporting, without SSHing into anything. Which Systems Manager capability automates patch compliance?
options: Session Manager port forwarding
Systems Manager State Manager associations
Patch Manager, which automates patching with baselines and produces compliance reports across the fleet
EC2 Image Builder pipelines
explain: Patch Manager applies patches per defined baselines on schedule and reports compliance per instance, covering the fleet without manual access. Session Manager provides shell access rather than patching, State Manager enforces configuration state rather than OS patches, and Image Builder builds AMIs rather than patching running instances.

q: A company with 50 accounts wants GuardDuty threat detection active in every current and future account with findings centralized, and no per-account manual setup. Which organization-level feature enables this?
options: Enabling GuardDuty manually in each account
GuardDuty delegated administrator with auto-enable for the organization, centrally managing detectors and findings
CloudTrail organization trails only
Security Hub in one account without aggregation
explain: A GuardDuty delegated administrator with auto-enable turns on detectors in all current and future organization accounts and centralizes findings. Manual per-account setup doesn't cover new accounts, CloudTrail trails log activity without threat detection, and Security Hub without aggregation leaves findings scattered.

q: A company will run steady EC2 workloads for 3 years but expects to change instance families as new generations launch. They also run Fargate containers and want one commitment covering both. Which pricing model fits?
options: Standard Reserved Instances for EC2 only
On-Demand with Auto Scaling
Spot Instances for the steady workloads
Compute Savings Plans, which apply to EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage regardless of instance family or Region
explain: Compute Savings Plans offer up to 72% off and automatically apply across EC2 instance families, Regions, Fargate, and Lambda — ideal when flexibility matters. Standard RIs lock to instance family and don't cover Fargate, On-Demand forfeits the discount, and Spot is interruptible and unsuitable for steady workloads.

q: A company buys Compute Savings Plans expecting guaranteed EC2 capacity during a peak event, but instances fail to launch in the needed AZ. What is the misunderstanding?
options: Savings Plans are only valid in us-east-1
Savings Plans provide billing discounts only — capacity reservations are a separate feature (On-Demand Capacity Reservations)
Savings Plans require 3-year terms for any discount
Savings Plans don't apply to Auto Scaling groups
explain: Savings Plans are purely a billing discount with no capacity guarantee; reserving capacity requires On-Demand Capacity Reservations. Savings Plans work in all Regions, offer 1- and 3-year terms, and apply to Auto Scaling usage normally.

q: A finance team cannot attribute its EC2 and RDS spend to individual product teams and suspects widespread overprovisioning. Which AWS service generates rightsizing recommendations for EC2, EBS, and RDS?
options: AWS Compute Optimizer, which analyzes utilization metrics and recommends optimal instance types and volume configurations
AWS Budgets with forecasted alerts
Cost Explorer's monthly reports
AWS Price List API queries
explain: Compute Optimizer uses machine learning on CloudWatch metrics to recommend rightsized EC2 instance types, EBS volumes, and RDS instances. Budgets alert on spend thresholds, Cost Explorer visualizes historical spend without recommendations, and the Price List API only provides pricing data.

q: Quarterly reports are archived to S3 and accessed a few times per year, but when accessed they must be retrieved in milliseconds. Which S3 storage class offers millisecond retrieval at archive pricing?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, which provides millisecond access for quarterly-accessed data at lower cost than Standard-IA
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access
explain: Glacier Instant Retrieval delivers millisecond retrieval for data accessed quarterly at lower storage cost than Standard-IA. Deep Archive takes hours to retrieve, Standard-IA costs more for rarely accessed data, and One Zone-IA sacrifices AZ redundancy without archive pricing.

q: A database team provisioned io1 volumes with 10,000 IOPS two years ago, but actual usage never exceeds 4,000 IOPS. They want to cut cost without a migration project. Which volume change lowers the bill with no downtime?
options: Migrating to instance store volumes
Converting io1 to gp3 with 4,000 provisioned IOPS, which costs significantly less per IOPS and modifies live via elastic volumes
Deleting the volumes and restoring from snapshots
Switching to sc1 cold HDD
explain: gp3 allows provisioning 4,000 IOPS independent of size at a lower price per IOPS than io1, and elastic volumes apply the change live. Instance store is ephemeral and loses data on stop, snapshot restore requires downtime, and sc1 is a throughput HDD unsuitable for database IOPS.

q: An application serves 100 TB/month of downloads directly from S3 in us-east-1 to global users, and data transfer dominates the bill. Which architecture change most reduces transfer cost while improving performance?
options: Moving the bucket to a cheaper Region
Enabling S3 Transfer Acceleration
Compressing objects with gzip only
Serving downloads through CloudFront, which cuts S3 origin transfer costs and caches content at edge locations
explain: CloudFront caches content at edges so repeat downloads don't incur S3 origin transfer, and CloudFront-to-internet rates undercut direct S3 transfer pricing. Moving Regions doesn't change internet transfer rates, Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than cutting download cost, and compression helps only marginally on already-compressed media.

q: Applications in private subnets call DynamoDB and Amazon SQS through a NAT gateway, and NAT data-processing charges are climbing. Which change eliminates the NAT charges for these two services?
options: VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB plus an interface endpoint for SQS, keeping traffic off the NAT gateway
A larger NAT gateway instance
Moving the applications to public subnets
Enabling IPv6 on the VPC
explain: Gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB are free and interface endpoints bill far less than NAT data-processing, removing those flows from the NAT gateway. A bigger NAT gateway doesn't reduce per-GB charges, public subnets expose the apps, and IPv6 still routes through NAT-equivalent egress for these services.

q: A security team enabled VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs in all VPCs and was surprised by the ingestion and storage bill. Which destination change typically lowers flow-log costs at scale?
options: Disabling flow logs entirely
Increasing the log retention to one year
Publishing flow logs to S3, which has far lower ingestion and storage costs than CloudWatch Logs
Enabling detailed EC2 monitoring
explain: S3 as a flow-log destination avoids CloudWatch Logs ingestion charges and offers cheaper long-term storage, the standard cost optimization at scale. Disabling logs blinds security monitoring, longer retention increases cost, and detailed monitoring is unrelated to log ingestion pricing.

q: Athena queries against 10 TB of S3 log data are slow and expensive because each query scans terabytes of raw JSON. Which one-time data preparation step permanently cuts both query cost and time?
options: Creating more Athena workgroups
Converting the logs to columnar Parquet with partitioning (via CTAS), so queries scan only relevant columns and partitions
Increasing the Athena result-set limit
Running queries during off-peak hours
explain: Parquet's columnar format plus partitioning means Athena scans only needed columns and partitions, cutting the $5/TB scanned cost dramatically and speeding queries. Workgroups manage access rather than scan size, result limits don't reduce scanned bytes, and Athena pricing is identical regardless of hour.

q: A nightly Spark ETL job runs on a long-running EMR cluster that sits idle 20 hours a day. The job itself takes 90 minutes. Which EMR deployment pattern eliminates the idle cost?
options: Reserving the cluster with 3-year RIs
Adding more core nodes permanently
Switching the cluster to Graviton instances
Transient EMR clusters that launch on schedule, run the job, and terminate — optionally on Spot with managed scaling
explain: Transient clusters exist only for the 90-minute job window, eliminating 20 hours of idle spend; Spot and managed scaling cut the job cost further. RIs discount but don't remove idle hours, more nodes increase idle cost, and Graviton improves price-performance without addressing idleness.

q: A company with 15 AWS accounts wants a single bill, automatic volume discounts, and the ability to block expensive services in development accounts. Which combination delivers consolidated billing plus guardrails?
options: AWS Organizations with consolidated billing and SCPs restricting costly services in dev OUs
Separate bills paid by one credit card
IAM users in a single account for everyone
Cost Explorer without Organizations
explain: Organizations consolidates billing across accounts to unlock volume discounts, while SCPs on development OUs block expensive instance types and services. Separate bills forfeit discounts, one shared account destroys isolation, and Cost Explorer alone provides neither consolidated billing nor guardrails.

q: A startup serves 90% of its users from North America and Europe and wants to cut CloudFront costs without hurting those users' experience. Which price class limits edge locations to the cheapest regions covering their audience?
options: Price Class All
Price Class 200
Price Class 100, which uses only North American and European edge locations at the lowest price
Disabling CloudFront and serving from S3
explain: Price Class 100 restricts delivery to North America and Europe edge locations — exactly the startup's audience — at the lowest CloudFront pricing. Price Class All and 200 include pricier regions their users don't need, and dropping CloudFront entirely sacrifices caching and performance.

q: A company enables S3 same-region replication for operational resilience. How does SRR affect the data transfer portion of the bill compared to cross-region replication?
options: SRR and CRR have identical transfer charges
Same-region replication incurs no inter-region data transfer charge; only replication PUT request charges apply
SRR doubles the storage cost
SRR requires Transfer Acceleration fees
explain: Same-region replication stays within the Region so no inter-region transfer fee applies — costs are the replication PUT requests and the destination storage. Cross-region replication adds per-GB transfer charges, SRR doesn't double storage beyond the replica copy itself, and Transfer Acceleration is unrelated to replication.

q: A company transfers 100 TB/month between its data center and AWS over a Site-to-Site VPN and the data transfer bill is enormous. Which connectivity change most reduces per-GB transfer cost at this volume?
options: Adding a second VPN tunnel for redundancy
Enabling VPN acceleration
Moving to Direct Connect, which offers significantly lower per-GB data transfer rates than VPN at high volumes
Compressing traffic with gzip
explain: Direct Connect provides much lower per-GB transfer pricing than internet-based VPN at 100 TB/month scale, plus consistent throughput. A second tunnel adds redundancy not savings, acceleration improves performance rather than pricing, and compression can't shrink already-compressed or encrypted payloads enough to matter.

q: An ECR repository accumulates thousands of old container images from every CI build, and storage costs grow monthly. Which ECR feature automatically prunes stale images?
options: ECR lifecycle policies, which automatically delete images by age or count thresholds
ECR image scanning on push
Tag immutability alone
Replicating the repository to another Region
explain: Lifecycle policies automatically expire images older than N days or beyond a count limit, stopping the storage growth from CI builds. Image scanning finds vulnerabilities rather than deleting, tag immutability prevents overwrites without pruning, and replication duplicates the bloat elsewhere.

q: A team runs scheduled cron jobs on EC2 instances that sit idle between runs, paying for 24/7 instances to execute a few minutes of work daily. Which serverless scheduler eliminates the idle instances?
options: Larger EC2 instances to finish faster
Auto Scaling scheduled actions keeping one instance warm
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler invoking Lambda on the cron expression, so compute exists only during execution
Running cron on the RDS instance
explain: EventBridge Scheduler triggers Lambda directly on schedule, so the team pays only for execution time instead of idle EC2 hours. Bigger instances still idle, scheduled Auto Scaling still runs instances between jobs, and RDS instances aren't job runners.

q: A company runs steady ElastiCache Redis clusters 24/7 in one Region for a year and wants a commitment discount similar to EC2 Reserved Instances. Which ElastiCache pricing option provides it?
options: ElastiCache Spot nodes
ElastiCache Reserved Nodes with 1- or 3-year terms, offering significant discounts for steady-state cache workloads
On-Demand with cluster mode
ElastiCache Serverless only
explain: Reserved Nodes commit to 1- or 3-year terms for steady ElastiCache usage at a steep discount, mirroring the RI model. ElastiCache has no Spot offering, On-Demand forfeits the discount, and Serverless suits variable rather than steady workloads.

q: A team is buying Savings Plans and wants the maximum possible discount, with cash available upfront. Which payment option yields the highest Savings Plans discount?
options: No Upfront monthly payments
Partial Upfront
Splitting across multiple 1-year plans
All Upfront, which provides the largest discount in exchange for full prepayment
explain: All Upfront prepayment earns the highest Savings Plans discount rate, followed by Partial Upfront, then No Upfront. Splitting into multiple smaller plans doesn't change the rate structure, and monthly payments trade discount for cash-flow flexibility.

q: A company with 200 S3 buckets needs organization-wide visibility into storage growth and cost anomalies, plus recommendations on which buckets to optimize first. Which S3 analytics feature provides fleet-wide storage insights?
options: S3 Storage Lens, which aggregates storage metrics and cost-optimization recommendations across accounts and buckets
S3 Inventory per bucket
CloudWatch per-bucket metrics only
AWS Config rules for bucket encryption
explain: Storage Lens provides organization-wide dashboards of storage usage, growth trends, and cost-optimization recommendations across all buckets. S3 Inventory lists objects per bucket without analytics, per-bucket CloudWatch metrics lack aggregation, and Config checks compliance rather than cost.

q: A team invalidates their entire CloudFront distribution (/*) on every deployment and the invalidation charges are adding up. Which deployment practice avoids invalidation costs entirely?
options: Invalidating more frequently in smaller batches
Switching to Price Class 100
Versioned file names (e.g., app-v2.js), so new deployments are new objects and no invalidation is needed
Increasing the default TTL to one year
explain: Versioned filenames make each deployment a new cache object, so the 1,000 free monthly invalidation paths are never consumed. Smaller batches still incur charges past the free tier, price class affects delivery cost rather than invalidations, and long TTLs make stale content worse without versioning.

q: The monthly bill shows charges for load balancers that no longer receive traffic after a migration. The team assumed idle load balancers are free. What is the cost reality?
options: Idle ALBs/NLBs are free after 30 days
ALBs and NLBs incur hourly charges plus LCU usage fees regardless of traffic, so unused ones should be deleted
Only data transfer is billed for load balancers
Charges stop automatically when target groups are empty
explain: Load balancers bill hourly plus Load Balancer Capacity Units even with zero traffic, so orphaned LBs from migrations must be deleted to stop charges. There is no free idle period, the hourly/LCU fees apply without traffic, and empty target groups don't pause billing.

q: A machine learning team runs training jobs on FSx for Lustre. The training datasets are regenerated from S3 for each run, so the file system only needs to exist during training. Which FSx for Lustre deployment type fits this ephemeral pattern cheapest?
options: Persistent SSD deployment running 24/7
FSx for Windows File Server
EFS with lifecycle management
Scratch deployment, designed for temporary high-performance workloads and deleted after the job completes
explain: Scratch file systems provide the same high throughput for temporary workloads at lower cost and are meant to be deleted after use, matching regenerated training data perfectly. Persistent deployments charge for 24/7 durability the team doesn't need, FSx for Windows serves SMB, and EFS can't match Lustre throughput for training.

q: A company records AWS Config configuration items across 40 accounts in all Regions and the Config bill is surprisingly large. Which change most reduces Config costs while keeping compliance coverage?
options: Recording all resource types in all Regions with daily snapshots
Using Config aggregators without recording
Enabling Config in only one Region per account
Scoping recording to specific resource types needed for compliance instead of recording everything
explain: Config charges per configuration item recorded, so limiting recording to the resource types compliance actually requires cuts the bill while keeping coverage. Recording everything maximizes cost, aggregators collect without reducing recording, and single-Region recording blinds multi-Region compliance.

q: A high-traffic Lambda function is invoked millions of times per month, and each invocation calls DynamoDB for the same slowly-changing reference data. Which change cuts both Lambda duration cost and DynamoDB read cost?
options: Increasing Lambda memory for faster execution
Adding DynamoDB Auto Scaling
Caching the reference data with ElastiCache or DAX, so invocations avoid repeated DynamoDB reads and finish faster
Switching DynamoDB to on-demand mode
explain: Caching reference data in ElastiCache or DAX eliminates repeated DynamoDB reads (cutting RCU cost) and shortens Lambda execution (cutting duration GB-second cost). More memory doesn't remove the read, Auto Scaling doesn't reduce read volume, and on-demand pricing doesn't cut the number of reads.

q: A low-traffic internal web app averages 8% CPU with occasional spikes to 70%, running on a general-purpose instance 24/7. Which instance choice best matches this burstable pattern at lowest cost?
options: A compute-optimized instance sized for the 70% spikes
T-series burstable instances, which provide baseline CPU with burst credits for spikes at the lowest cost for low-average utilization
A memory-optimized instance
Two instances behind a load balancer for redundancy
explain: T-series burstable instances are priced for low baseline utilization and accrue CPU credits for the occasional 70% spikes — the cheapest fit for this pattern. Compute-optimized instances overpay for unused capacity, memory-optimized targets the wrong resource, and two instances double the bill for an internal low-traffic app.

q: An RDS for MySQL database suffered data corruption from a bad deployment three days ago, but the corruption was only discovered this morning. The team needs the database restored to its state five minutes before the corruption occurred. Which recovery option provides this granularity?
options: Restore the most recent automated snapshot
Point-in-time recovery to five minutes before the corruption
Promote a read replica to a standalone instance
Fail over to the Multi-AZ standby
explain: Point-in-time recovery replays transaction logs against a snapshot, restoring to any second within the backup retention window. The latest snapshot only goes back to snapshot time, a read replica contains the same corruption as the primary, and Multi-AZ failover mirrors the corrupted primary rather than rewinding it.

q: A company runs active-passive across two Regions with Route 53 failover. A recent drill revealed the recovery Region was missing EC2 capacity quota and its health checks pointed at decommissioned endpoints, so failover would have failed. Which Application Recovery Controller capability continuously validates that the recovery environment is actually ready to take over?
options: Routing controls
Zonal autoshift
Readiness checks
CloudWatch composite alarms
explain: Readiness checks continuously audit recovery resources — capacity, quotas, routing, and DNS targets — and surface misconfigurations before a disaster. Routing controls only shift traffic, zonal autoshift handles AZ-level shifts rather than Regional recovery validation, and composite alarms aggregate alarms without assessing recovery readiness.

q: An event-driven order system publishes order events to Amazon EventBridge in us-east-1. The company needs those events to be processed in eu-west-1 if us-east-1 becomes unavailable, with automatic failover and no custom replication code in the producer. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: EventBridge global endpoints with us-east-1 as primary and eu-west-1 as secondary
An EventBridge event bus in each Region with the producer publishing to both
EventBridge archive and replay from us-east-1 to eu-west-1
A Lambda function that forwards each event to eu-west-1
explain: Global endpoints route events to the secondary Region automatically when health checks detect the primary is impaired, with no producer changes. Dual publishing burdens the producer with failover logic, archive and replay is a manual recovery operation rather than automatic failover, and a Lambda forwarder is custom code that itself becomes a single point of failure.

q: A news site behind CloudFront shows origin errors to readers whenever the origin is briefly unhealthy during deployments. The team wants CloudFront to keep serving cached content when the origin errors, instead of passing the error to users. Which caching configuration achieves this?
options: Increase the default TTL on all cache behaviors
Configure an origin group with a failover origin
Disable caching so every request reaches the origin
Use stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error cache directives
explain: These directives let CloudFront serve stale cached content while revalidating in the background, or when the origin returns an error. Longer TTLs alone do not permit serving stale content on error, origin groups require provisioning a second origin, and disabling caching makes every request depend on the origin.

q: An operator accidentally dropped a production DocumentDB collection 45 minutes ago. The team needs the collection restored to its state 10 minutes before the drop, without losing the writes that happened since on other collections. Which DocumentDB feature enables this?
options: Restoring the latest manual snapshot
Point-in-time recovery to 10 minutes before the drop
Promoting a read replica
Replaying the oplog manually
explain: DocumentDB continuous backups support point-in-time recovery to any second within the backup window, restoring to just before the drop. Manual snapshots only go back to snapshot time, replicas contain the same dropped state as the primary, and manual oplog replay is not a supported restore path.

q: A log analytics platform runs Amazon OpenSearch Service in one Region. For regional disaster recovery, the team needs a continuously replicated, ready-to-query copy of its indexes in a second Region. Which feature provides this?
options: Cross-cluster replication between the primary domain and a follower domain in the second Region
Automated snapshots copied to the second Region every hour
UltraWarm storage on the primary domain
EBS snapshot schedules on the domain's data nodes
explain: Cross-cluster replication keeps a live follower index in the second Region that can serve queries immediately. Hourly snapshots have an RPO of up to an hour and require a restore before querying, UltraWarm is a cheaper storage tier rather than disaster recovery, and managed OpenSearch domains do not expose EBS-level snapshots.

q: A Kinesis data stream feeds a fraud-detection consumer. A 30-hour consumer outage caused permanent data loss because records aged out of the stream before processing resumed. Which change prevents this data loss for future multi-day outages?
options: Double the number of shards in the stream
Enable enhanced fan-out on the consumer
Increase the stream's data retention period to 7 days
Replace the consumer with a Lambda event source mapping
explain: Kinesis Data Streams defaults to 24-hour retention but supports extended retention up to 365 days, so a 7-day window survives multi-day consumer outages. More shards add throughput rather than retention, enhanced fan-out adds per-consumer throughput rather than retention, and a Lambda consumer reads from the same stream with the same retention limit.

q: A disaster recovery runbook for a multi-tier application has 40 manual console steps, and the last drill took three hours with two human errors. Which approach makes failover repeatable and less error-prone?
options: Keep the printed runbook but assign more engineers to the drill
Write a single Lambda function that performs all 40 steps
Document the steps in a wiki with screenshots
Implement the runbook as a Systems Manager Automation document with approval steps
explain: SSM Automation codifies multi-step runbooks with branching, approvals, and rate controls, making drills repeatable and auditable. More engineers do not remove human error, a monolithic Lambda lacks approval gates and safe rollout controls, and a wiki still requires manual execution of every step.

q: A REST API runs on API Gateway with a Regional endpoint in us-east-1. The company needs automatic failover to a standby copy of the API in eu-west-1 during a regional impairment. Which design provides this?
options: Change the endpoint type to edge-optimized
Deploy the API in eu-west-1 and use Route 53 failover routing with health checks against both Regional endpoints
Enable API Gateway caching on the production stage
Add a second stage to the same API in us-east-1
explain: Route 53 failover routing with health checks against each Regional endpoint shifts DNS to eu-west-1 when us-east-1 is unhealthy. Edge-optimized endpoints improve latency rather than providing failover, caching cannot serve a Region-wide outage, and a second stage lives in the same Region and fails with it.

q: A company deploys its application with AWS CloudFormation in us-east-1. For disaster recovery it needs the identical infrastructure in eu-west-1, and both Regions must be updated together on every change with minimal operational overhead. Which approach meets this requirement?
options: Recreate the resources manually in eu-west-1 from the console
Maintain a second copy of the template and update each Region's stack by hand
Deploy the stack to both Regions with CloudFormation StackSets
Rely on CloudFormation drift detection to keep the Regions in sync
explain: StackSets deploy and update a common template across accounts and Regions from one operation, keeping the DR environment identical. Manual recreation and hand-maintained duplicate stacks inevitably drift, and drift detection only reports differences without deploying anything.

q: An Amazon DocumentDB cluster has a primary instance and two replicas spread across three Availability Zones. If the primary fails, the application needs automatic promotion of a replica with minimal downtime. Which statement is correct?
options: DocumentDB automatically fails over to a replica, typically within 30 seconds, with no manual intervention
An operator must promote a replica manually through the console
The application must implement its own leader election to pick a new primary
Automatic failover requires provisioning a separate Multi-AZ standby instance
explain: DocumentDB replicates storage across AZs and automatically promotes a replica on primary failure, usually in under 30 seconds. No manual promotion, application-level election, or separate standby instance is required — unlike RDS database instances, the replicas themselves serve as the failover targets.

q: An analytics team runs Amazon Redshift in us-east-1. For disaster recovery, it needs automated daily copies of its cluster snapshots stored in eu-west-1. Which feature meets this requirement?
options: Redshift concurrency scaling
AWS Backup EBS volume copies of the cluster nodes
A daily UNLOAD of all tables to S3 in eu-west-1
Cross-Region snapshot copy configured on the Redshift cluster
explain: Redshift supports automated cross-Region snapshot copy, delivering daily cluster snapshots to the second Region. Concurrency scaling addresses query performance rather than backup, EBS-level copies do not capture the managed cluster state, and unloading tables is a partial, labor-intensive substitute for a full cluster snapshot.

q: A legacy application runs on a single EC2 instance and cannot be clustered. If its Availability Zone fails, the application must resume quickly in another AZ while keeping the same public IP address that customers have whitelisted. Which design provides the fastest recovery?
options: Enable EC2 auto recovery on the instance
Maintain a stopped standby instance from a current AMI in a second AZ and reassociate the Elastic IP to it on failure
Take hourly AMIs so a replacement can be launched quickly
Attach a second elastic network interface to the instance
explain: A warm standby plus Elastic IP reassociation restores service in another AZ while preserving the whitelisted public IP. EC2 auto recovery only recovers within the same AZ, AMIs alone still require launch and configuration steps, and an extra ENI does nothing when the whole AZ is impaired.

q: An Amazon Neptune cluster has a primary DB instance and read replicas in other Availability Zones. The team assumes it must provision a separate standby instance, like RDS Multi-AZ, to get automatic failover. What should they understand?
options: Failover requires restoring the cluster from the latest snapshot
A separate Multi-AZ standby instance must be provisioned for automatic failover
Neptune automatically fails over to a read replica with no separate standby to provision
Replicas can only be promoted manually, followed by an application restart
explain: Neptune uses a shared cluster volume, so any read replica can be promoted automatically on primary failure with no separate standby. Snapshot restores are for point-in-time recovery rather than failover, and promotion is automatic rather than manual.

q: A company protects EC2, RDS, and EFS with AWS Backup, including cross-Region copies. Auditors want proof that the backups are actually restorable, but restore drills must not touch production. Which AWS Backup feature validates recoverability safely?
options: Restore testing, which restores recovery points into an isolated test environment on a schedule
Backup vault lock on the recovery points
Cross-account backup copies
Legal holds on the recovery points
explain: Restore testing automatically restores recovery points in an isolated environment and reports success, proving recoverability without production impact. Vault lock provides immutability against deletion, cross-account copies provide disaster recovery isolation, and legal holds prevent deletion — none of them verify that a restore actually works.

q: A company connects its data center to AWS with a Site-to-Site VPN. During maintenance on the customer gateway device, the single VPN tunnel in use dropped and connectivity was lost for an hour. Which design keeps the VPN highly available?
options: Increase the MTU on the VPN tunnel
Enable Dead Peer Detection on the customer gateway
Create a second VPN connection that shares the same tunnel
Use both tunnels that AWS provisions for the Site-to-Site VPN connection, terminating on redundant customer gateway devices
explain: Every Site-to-Site VPN connection includes two tunnels in separate AZs; using both, ideally on redundant customer gateways, removes the single-tunnel single point of failure. MTU tuning does not add redundancy, Dead Peer Detection only detects failure faster, and a connection cannot share tunnels — the redundancy comes from using both provided tunnels.

q: A company uses Direct Connect as its primary hybrid link and wants automatic failover to a Site-to-Site VPN if Direct Connect fails, with Direct Connect preferred whenever it is healthy. Which design achieves this?
options: Configure static routes and switch them manually during outages
Advertise the same on-premises routes over both links via BGP, with AS path prepending on the VPN so Direct Connect is preferred
Give the VPN higher bandwidth so it is always the preferred path
Order a second Direct Connect and skip the VPN entirely
explain: BGP selects the Direct Connect path normally, while AS path prepending makes the VPN routes less preferred so they take over automatically on DX failure. Manual static route changes are slow and error-prone, preferring the VPN defeats the purpose of the DX investment, and a second DX adds resilience but provides no automatic VPN backup.

q: An application mounts an EFS file system from EC2 instances in three Availability Zones, but mounts intermittently fail for instances in one AZ. Investigation shows the file system has mount targets in only two AZs. What is the correct fix?
options: Enable EFS replication to the third AZ
Switch the file system to Max I/O performance mode
Create a mount target in each AZ where clients mount the file system
Place the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group
explain: EC2 instances must mount EFS through a mount target in their own AZ, so every AZ with clients needs one. EFS replication is for cross-Region disaster recovery rather than AZ-level mounting, performance mode affects throughput rather than connectivity, and placement groups address network latency rather than mount availability.

q: A Route 53 health check polls an application's /health endpoint and reports healthy, but during partial outages the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a body of 'DEGRADED', so failover never triggers. Which health check improvement detects this condition?
options: Decrease the health check interval to 10 seconds
Add more health checker locations
Switch to a TCP health check on port 443
Enable string matching on the health check for the expected response body
explain: String matching fails the health check when the response body does not contain the expected string, catching degraded-but-200 responses. A shorter interval only checks the same flawed condition faster, more checkers do not change what is evaluated, and a TCP check only verifies the port is open.

q: A DynamoDB table holds several terabytes of critical data. The team needs a full point-in-time copy in S3 in another Region for disaster recovery and analytics, without consuming the table's read capacity. Which feature provides this?
options: DynamoDB export to S3, which uses point-in-time recovery snapshots without consuming provisioned read capacity
A full table Scan that writes items to S3
DynamoDB Streams feeding a Lambda function that writes to S3
An on-demand backup replicated with S3 cross-Region replication
explain: Export to S3 reads from PITR snapshots rather than the live table, so it consumes no provisioned read capacity and produces a full copy. A Scan consumes RCUs and takes a long time on terabytes, Streams only capture changes from enablement forward, and on-demand backups live in DynamoDB rather than S3 so S3 replication does not apply.

q: An engineer accidentally deleted a production RDS instance. The team had automated backups, but recovery still took hours and caused an outage. Which combination prevents accidental deletion and guarantees a final backup is captured?
options: Enable Multi-AZ deployment
Enable deletion protection and retain a final snapshot when the instance is deleted
Increase the automated backup retention period to 35 days
Enable storage autoscaling on the instance
explain: Deletion protection blocks delete API calls, and the final snapshot option captures the data as of deletion for any authorized delete. Multi-AZ protects against AZ failure rather than human error, longer retention does not stop deletion, and storage autoscaling addresses capacity rather than deletion safety.

q: Applications in private subnets use a VPC interface endpoint for Secrets Manager. During an AZ impairment, applications in that AZ lose access to secrets while instances in other AZs are unaffected. What is the most likely cause?
options: The endpoint policy denies requests from the impaired AZ
Secrets Manager experienced a Regional outage
The interface endpoint has subnets in only some AZs
The private route tables are missing a NAT gateway route
explain: Interface endpoints place an ENI in each selected subnet, and clients should resolve to an endpoint ENI in their own AZ — AZs without one lose access during an impairment. Endpoint policies do not filter by AZ, a Regional Secrets Manager outage would affect all AZs, and interface endpoints do not use NAT gateways.

q: A company runs a multi-tier application across EC2, RDS, and S3 and wants a single assessment of whether the architecture meets its RTO and RPO targets, with prioritized improvement recommendations. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Config
AWS Trusted Advisor
CloudWatch Application Insights
AWS Resilience Hub
explain: Resilience Hub evaluates the application against defined RTO/RPO objectives and produces prioritized resilience recommendations. Config checks resource configuration compliance, Trusted Advisor gives general best-practice checks, and Application Insights focuses on observability rather than resilience assessment.

q: A company enables S3 cross-Region replication on a bucket holding 50 million existing objects. New uploads replicate, but the pre-existing objects do not. Which feature replicates the existing objects?
options: An S3 Batch Replication job
S3 Replication Time Control
Re-uploading all 50 million objects
S3 Inventory with Athena queries
explain: Cross-Region replication only applies to new objects; S3 Batch Replication replicates existing objects. Replication Time Control adds an SLA to replication of new objects, re-uploading is wasteful and slow, and S3 Inventory only reports on objects without replicating them.

q: A genomics team runs batch analysis on a fixed fleet of EC2 instances, manually submitting jobs and babysitting capacity. They want managed job scheduling with automatic provisioning, Spot usage, and retries for failed jobs. Which service fits best?
options: AWS Lambda with maximum memory
AWS Batch with a managed compute environment
EC2 Auto Scaling with scheduled actions
Amazon EMR
explain: AWS Batch provides managed job queues, scheduling, dynamic provisioning including Spot, and automatic retries. Lambda has a 15-minute execution limit unsuited to genomics jobs, Auto Scaling does not schedule or retry jobs, and EMR is for big-data frameworks rather than general batch jobs.

q: A real-time bidding application stores session state in S3 Standard and needs single-digit millisecond data access for frequently accessed objects in one Region. The data is easily re-created if lost. Which S3 storage class delivers the lowest latency?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Express One Zone
S3 Standard-IA
explain: S3 Express One Zone is purpose-built for single-digit millisecond access, storing data in a single AZ. S3 Standard offers tens of milliseconds, Intelligent-Tiering optimizes cost rather than latency, and Standard-IA adds retrieval fees with the same latency as Standard.

q: A Java-based Lambda function suffers multi-second cold starts after idle periods because JVM initialization is slow. The team wants faster cold starts without keeping functions warm. Which feature addresses this?
options: Lambda provisioned concurrency
Lambda SnapStart
Increasing the function's memory to 10 GB
Lambda reserved concurrency
explain: SnapStart initializes the execution environment ahead of time and snapshots it, cutting Java cold starts dramatically. Provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm at extra cost, more memory speeds execution but does not eliminate JVM initialization, and reserved concurrency only caps concurrency rather than warming.

q: A Kinesis data stream has one shard receiving 80% of all writes because the partition key has low cardinality. That shard's writes are throttled while other shards sit idle. Which approach fixes the hot-shard problem?
options: Redesign the partition key for higher cardinality and split the hot shard
Enable enhanced fan-out on the consumers
Increase the stream's retention period
Switch the stream to on-demand capacity mode
explain: Enhanced fan-out adds read throughput rather than fixing write imbalance, retention affects replay windows rather than throughput, and while on-demand mode can absorb spikes, the durable fix for a hot shard is a well-distributed partition key plus splitting. A low-cardinality partition key concentrates writes on one shard; neither read-side features nor retention address that.

q: An MSK cluster must sustain much higher per-broker throughput for a growing event backbone, and the team prefers fewer, more powerful brokers over managing many smaller ones. Which broker type fits?
options: MSK Serverless
Kafka brokers with tiered storage
Standard MSK provisioned brokers with more partitions
MSK Express brokers
explain: Express brokers are purpose-built for significantly higher per-broker throughput, reducing the broker count needed. MSK Serverless auto-scales but does not maximize per-broker throughput, tiered storage addresses retention cost rather than throughput, and adding partitions does not raise the per-broker ceiling.

q: A Redshift query joining two large fact tables on customer ID runs slowly, and EXPLAIN shows most of the time spent redistributing rows across nodes. Which table design change minimizes redistribution for this join?
options: Add more nodes to the cluster
Set DISTKEY to customer ID on both tables so matching rows are co-located
Enable concurrency scaling
Use EVEN distribution for all tables
explain: KEY distribution on the join column co-locates matching rows on the same node slice, eliminating redistribution. More nodes add capacity without fixing the data layout, concurrency scaling adds burst query capacity rather than fixing joins, and EVEN distribution scatters rows randomly which forces redistribution on every join.

q: A dashboard runs the same Athena queries over slowly changing S3 data every few minutes, and each run scans terabytes. Which Athena feature avoids rescanning unchanged data?
options: Athena workgroup query limits
Partition projection
Athena result reuse
Athena engine version 2
explain: Result reuse returns cached results for identical queries when the underlying data has not changed, skipping the scan. Workgroup limits cap cost rather than avoiding rescans, partition projection helps partition discovery, and engine version 2 is an older engine generation rather than a caching feature.

q: A document database workload on Amazon DocumentDB is outgrowing the write capacity of a single primary instance, and the team needs to scale writes horizontally by sharding. Which DocumentDB deployment supports this?
options: DocumentDB elastic clusters
Adding more read replicas to the instance-based cluster
Enabling DocumentDB global clusters
Increasing the primary instance class
explain: Elastic clusters shard data across multiple shards for horizontal write scaling. Read replicas scale reads rather than writes, DocumentDB has no global cluster offering, and a larger instance only scales vertically.

q: Analysts need near-real-time Aurora MySQL data in Redshift, but the current nightly ETL pipeline is complex and the data is stale by morning. Which integration provides near-real-time analytics with no ETL pipeline to manage?
options: Aurora read replicas in the analytics account
AWS DMS full load plus CDC to Redshift
Nightly snapshots exported to S3 and loaded with COPY
Aurora zero-ETL integration with Amazon Redshift
explain: Zero-ETL continuously replicates Aurora data into Redshift with no pipeline to build or maintain. Read replicas serve transactional reads rather than warehousing, DMS requires managing replication instances and tasks, and snapshot exports are batch-based and stale.

q: A company runs its application in three Regions and wants to route users to the nearest Region, but also bias some traffic toward the Region with the most spare capacity. Which Route 53 routing policy supports distance-based routing with adjustable bias?
options: Latency-based routing
Weighted routing
Geoproximity routing
Multivalue answer routing
explain: Geoproximity routes based on geographic distance with an optional bias to shift traffic between Regions. Latency-based routing uses measured latency without bias control, weighted routing splits by fixed ratios without geography, and multivalue answer routing returns multiple healthy records rather than choosing by location.

q: A hybrid application uses a Site-to-Site VPN over the public internet, but throughput varies and latency is high for distant branch offices. The company wants to accelerate the VPN without laying new private connectivity. Which feature improves VPN performance over long distances?
options: Enabling Dead Peer Detection on the customer gateway
AWS Site-to-Site VPN acceleration using AWS Global Accelerator
Increasing the VPN tunnel MTU to 9001
Adding a second VPN connection in the same Region
explain: VPN acceleration routes traffic through the AWS global network via Global Accelerator, improving long-distance throughput and reliability. Dead Peer Detection only detects dead peers, MTU tuning does not fix internet variability, and a second connection adds redundancy rather than performance.

q: A media rendering farm mounts EFS from thousands of EC2 instances with highly parallel I/O, and the General Purpose performance mode is throttling throughput. Which EFS performance mode is designed for highly parallelized workloads?
options: Max I/O
General Purpose
Elastic throughput
Provisioned throughput at 1 MB/s
explain: Max I/O is built for highly parallel workloads across thousands of clients, trading slightly higher latencies for aggregate throughput. General Purpose is already the bottleneck, and Elastic and Provisioned are throughput modes rather than performance modes that address parallel-client scaling.

q: An event-processing workflow runs millions of short executions per day, each lasting under a second. Standard Step Functions workflows are becoming expensive at this volume. Which workflow type is designed for high-event-rate, short-duration workloads?
options: Step Functions Standard workflows with more retries
AWS Batch jobs
Lambda destinations
Step Functions Express Workflows
explain: Express Workflows are designed for high-volume, short-duration executions with pricing to match. Standard workflows suit long-running orchestrations, Batch is for long-running jobs rather than sub-second events, and Lambda destinations only handle async invocation results rather than orchestration.

q: A SaaS platform needs to trigger millions of one-time and recurring customer schedules — reminders, report runs, subscription renewals — with per-schedule time zones. Managing this with cron on EC2 is collapsing. Which service is purpose-built for schedules at this scale?
options: EventBridge rules with cron expressions
Step Functions wait states
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
SQS delay queues
explain: EventBridge Scheduler is built for millions of one-time and recurring schedules with time zone support. EventBridge rules are limited in schedule count and flexibility, Step Functions wait states tie up executions for the wait duration, and SQS delay queues cap at 15 minutes per message.

q: An application issues thousands of individual DynamoDB GetItem calls per second to fetch related items, and the per-request overhead is hurting latency. The items are frequently requested together. Which approach reduces request overhead?
options: Place DAX in front of the table
Use BatchGetItem to retrieve up to 100 items per call
Double the table's provisioned read capacity
Enable DynamoDB Streams on the table
explain: BatchGetItem fetches many items in one call, cutting per-request overhead for items fetched together. DAX caches reads but does not batch requests, more RCUs add throughput without reducing call count, and Streams capture changes rather than serving reads.

q: An order pipeline uses an SQS FIFO queue for exactly-once, ordered processing, but throughput is capped and batching alone is not enough during flash sales. Which FIFO feature raises the throughput ceiling?
options: High throughput mode for FIFO queues
Switching to a standard queue
Increasing the visibility timeout
Enabling long polling
explain: FIFO high throughput mode raises the per-queue throughput limits while preserving ordering and deduplication. A standard queue drops ordering guarantees, visibility timeout controls reprocessing rather than throughput, and long polling reduces empty receives rather than raising throughput.

q: A Redis workload holds 500 GB of data on ElastiCache, but only about 20% is accessed frequently. Keeping everything in RAM is expensive. Which ElastiCache feature keeps hot data in memory and colder data on SSD at lower cost?
options: Redis Cluster mode with more shards
ElastiCache Serverless
Read replicas in every AZ
Data tiering with r6gd nodes
explain: Data tiering stores infrequently accessed data on local NVMe SSDs while hot data stays in memory, cutting cost for large datasets. More shards add memory rather than tiering, Serverless auto-scales but does not tier to SSD, and read replicas add memory copies rather than reducing cost.

q: A website serves large text-based assets (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) through CloudFront, and transfer size is hurting load times on slow connections. Which CloudFront feature reduces transfer size with no origin changes?
options: Signed URLs
Origin shield
Automatic object compression
Real-time logs
explain: CloudFront can compress cacheable text content with gzip or Brotli at the edge, shrinking transfers without origin changes. Signed URLs control access, origin shield reduces origin load rather than transfer size, and real-time logs are observability.

q: A DynamoDB table on provisioned capacity handles a steady baseline, but a weekly flash sale needs 10x write throughput for one hour. Scaling up in advance wastes money and sudden spikes throttle. Which feature pre-warms burst capacity for a known event?
options: DynamoDB auto scaling
Warm throughput for the table
DAX in front of the table
Global secondary index overloading
explain: Warm throughput lets you declare upcoming throughput needs so DynamoDB pre-warms capacity for the burst. Auto scaling reacts to traffic rather than preparing for it, DAX caches reads rather than absorbing write bursts, and GSIs do not add write capacity to the base table.

q: An Aurora MySQL workload runs complex queries with heavy temporary table usage, and the team wants faster queries without changing SQL or adding read replicas. Which instance-level feature accelerates temporary object processing?
options: Aurora optimized reads using instances with local NVMe SSD storage
Aurora parallel query
Enabling the query cache
Aurora Serverless v2 scaling
explain: Optimized reads place temporary tables and files on fast local NVMe storage, speeding queries with heavy temp usage. Parallel query is a deprecated feature, the query cache was removed in MySQL 8.0 and does not help temp tables, and Serverless v2 scales compute rather than accelerating temp I/O.

q: A multi-tenant SaaS database on Aurora has outgrown the write throughput of a single writer instance, and tenants need isolation from noisy-neighbor writes. Which Aurora capability provides horizontal write scaling through sharding?
options: Aurora Global Database
Adding Aurora read replicas
Aurora cloning
Aurora Limitless Database
explain: Limitless Database shards the cluster across multiple writers for horizontal write scale-out. Global Database replicates across Regions for reads and DR rather than sharding writes, read replicas scale reads only, and cloning creates copy-on-write copies for testing rather than scaling.

q: A mobile team is building a collaborative app needing a GraphQL API with real-time updates pushed to clients and offline sync for mobile devices. Building this on API Gateway plus custom WebSocket handling is proving complex. Which managed service fits best?
options: API Gateway REST APIs with usage plans
Application Load Balancer with WebSocket stickiness
AWS AppSync
Amazon SNS topics per client
explain: AppSync provides managed GraphQL with real-time subscriptions and built-in offline synchronization. REST APIs do not push real-time updates, ALB stickiness does not provide a GraphQL or sync layer, and SNS is pub/sub messaging rather than a data API.

q: A marketing team wants A/B testing on a CloudFront-served site: users must be assigned to a variant at the edge on first request, with assignment logic that calls an external feature-flag API. Which edge compute option supports network calls for this logic?
options: Lambda@Edge
CloudFront Functions
S3 Object Lambda
