API Gateway caching
explain: Lambda@Edge supports network access and longer runtimes, so it can call external APIs for variant assignment. CloudFront Functions cannot make network calls, S3 Object Lambda transforms S3 retrievals rather than viewer requests, and API Gateway caching does not run edge logic.

q: An RDS for MySQL workload is bottlenecked on temporary table I/O, and the team wants instances with local NVMe SSDs for faster temporary object processing without changing the engine. Which RDS feature provides this?
options: RDS Performance Insights
RDS Proxy
RDS Optimized Reads and Optimized Writes
Enabling Multi-AZ
explain: Optimized Reads and Optimized Writes use instance types with local NVMe SSDs to accelerate temporary tables and transaction processing. Performance Insights is observability, RDS Proxy pools connections rather than accelerating I/O, and Multi-AZ addresses availability rather than performance.

q: A multiplayer game backend runs in two Regions behind AWS Global Accelerator. Partners must whitelist fixed entry IP addresses, and players should reach the nearest healthy Region with minimal latency. Which combination meets these requirements?
options: Route 53 latency-based routing with Elastic IPs
An ALB in each Region with cross-zone load balancing
CloudFront with static IP allowlisting
Global Accelerator with Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP)
explain: Global Accelerator provides fixed anycast entry IPs — including BYOIP addresses partners can whitelist — and routes players to the optimal healthy endpoint. Route 53 latency routing resolves to changing IPs, ALBs are Regional, and CloudFront is for HTTP content rather than game traffic.

q: A company uses AWS Global Accelerator with endpoints in two Regions and wants to send 80% of traffic to the primary Region and 20% to the secondary for a gradual migration. Which Global Accelerator setting controls this distribution?
options: Client affinity settings
Endpoint weights
Health check intervals
Cross-Region failover thresholds
explain: Endpoint weights dial the proportion of traffic each endpoint group receives, enabling gradual shifts. Client affinity pins users to endpoints rather than distributing by ratio, health check intervals only affect failure detection speed, and there is no failover threshold setting that splits traffic by percentage.

q: A data processing service needs temporary permission to use a KMS key owned by another team, without the key owner editing the key policy for each short-lived workload. Which KMS mechanism delegates key usage without key policy changes?
options: KMS key rotation
A new customer managed key per workload
IAM permission boundaries
KMS grants
explain: Grants delegate specific key operations to a principal programmatically, without modifying the key policy each time. Key rotation changes key material rather than delegating access, per-workload keys multiply management overhead, and permission boundaries only limit maximum permissions rather than granting key use.

q: A bank must keep its encryption keys in an on-premises hardware security module outside of AWS infrastructure for regulatory reasons, while still using those keys to encrypt AWS workloads. Which KMS feature supports this?
options: KMS multi-Region keys
KMS External Key Store (XKS)
AWS CloudHSM with manual key sync
S3 server-side encryption with S3-managed keys
explain: External Key Store lets KMS use keys held in an external HSM outside AWS. Multi-Region keys replicate within AWS, CloudHSM is AWS-hosted hardware rather than external, and SSE-S3 uses AWS-managed keys that never leave AWS.

q: A government workload requires two independent layers of encryption applied to S3 objects, both managed through KMS. Which S3 encryption option applies dual-layer server-side encryption?
options: Dual-layer server-side encryption with KMS keys (DSSE-KMS)
SSE-S3 with bucket keys
SSE-C with customer-provided keys
Client-side encryption with the S3 Encryption Client
explain: DSSE-KMS applies two independent encryption layers, both under KMS control. SSE-S3 applies a single AES-256 layer, SSE-C uses customer-supplied keys rather than KMS, and client-side encryption happens before upload rather than as S3 server-side dual layers.

q: A data lake bucket serves thousands of users with different prefix-level permissions, and managing individual bucket policies has become unmanageable. Which S3 feature maps corporate identities to fine-grained S3 permissions at scale?
options: S3 Block Public Access
S3 Object Ownership
S3 Access Grants
S3 Inventory
explain: Access Grants map identities from IAM Identity Center or IAM to S3 prefixes with least-privilege permissions at scale. Block Public Access is a guardrail rather than an authorization system, Object Ownership controls ACL behavior rather than granting access, and Inventory only reports on objects.

q: A company wants to ensure that content processed by AWS AI services is never stored or used for service improvement, enforced centrally so no account can opt back in. Which Organizations policy type enforces this?
options: Service control policies (SCPs)
Tag policies
Backup policies
AI services opt-out policies
explain: AI services opt-out policies centrally control whether AWS may store content for service improvement. SCPs restrict API actions rather than data-use preferences, tag policies standardize tags, and backup policies manage AWS Backup plans.

q: A company with 60 AWS accounts wants centrally managed preventive and detective guardrails — for example, blocking public S3 buckets while also detecting unencrypted volumes — applied automatically to every account including new ones. Which service provides this landing-zone governance?
options: AWS Config conformance packs alone
AWS Control Tower
AWS Systems Manager Automation
IAM Access Analyzer
explain: Control Tower applies preventive, detective, and proactive guardrails across all accounts in the landing zone automatically. Config conformance packs only assess and optionally remediate without preventive enforcement, Systems Manager Automation runs tasks rather than governing, and Access Analyzer focuses on access findings rather than broad guardrails.

q: A finance team cannot allocate costs because product teams tag resources inconsistently — some use 'Team', others 'team', others nothing at all. Which Organizations feature enforces standardized tag keys and allowed values across accounts?
options: Tag policies
Service control policies
Cost allocation tags activation
AWS Budgets
explain: Tag policies enforce tag key casing and allowed values on resources across the organization. SCPs restrict actions rather than tag formats, activating cost allocation tags only enables billing reports for existing tags, and Budgets track spend rather than enforcing tagging.

q: A platform team wants every EC2 instance in the organization to carry a mandatory baseline security group, with automatic remediation when instances launch without it. Which Firewall Manager policy type enforces this?
options: WAF policies
Network Firewall policies
Security group policies
Shield Advanced policies
explain: Firewall Manager security group policies enforce common or audited security groups across accounts and auto-remediate drift. WAF policies manage web ACLs, Network Firewall policies manage firewall rules, and Shield Advanced policies handle DDoS protection — none manage security group attachment.

q: A company must inspect HTTPS traffic leaving its VPCs for malware and data exfiltration, but TLS encryption blinds its current Network Firewall rules. Which Network Firewall capability decrypts and inspects TLS traffic?
options: Stateful domain list rule groups
Suricata IPS rules
AWS-managed threat signature rule groups
TLS inspection configuration
explain: TLS inspection terminates and re-encrypts traffic so firewall rules can inspect the plaintext. Domain lists filter by domain without seeing content, IPS rules match patterns in visible traffic, and managed threat signatures also cannot see inside encrypted sessions.

q: A security team runs production workloads on EKS and wants runtime threat detection for container-level attacks — such as crypto mining inside pods — without deploying agents themselves. Which GuardDuty protection plan provides this?
options: GuardDuty S3 Protection
GuardDuty EKS Runtime Monitoring
GuardDuty RDS Protection
GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2
explain: EKS Runtime Monitoring uses AWS-managed sensors to detect container runtime threats. S3 Protection monitors bucket threats, RDS Protection watches database login anomalies, and Malware Protection scans EBS volumes — none monitor container runtime behavior.

q: A compliance audit requires a software bill of materials (SBOM) listing packages and vulnerabilities for every container image in ECR. Which Inspector capability produces this inventory?
options: Inspector SBOM export for scanned resources
ECR image scanning on push
AWS Config resource inventory
Security Hub finding aggregation
explain: Inspector can export SBOMs detailing packages and CVEs for scanned images and instances. ECR on-push scanning finds vulnerabilities without producing an SBOM, Config inventories resource configuration rather than software packages, and Security Hub aggregates findings rather than generating SBOMs.

q: A B2B API on API Gateway must reject all traffic except requests from two partner corporate IP ranges. The team wants this enforced at the API entry point rather than in application code. Which feature implements IP-based access control?
options: Lambda authorizers
API Gateway usage plans with throttling
API Gateway resource policies with IP condition keys
WAF rate-based rules
explain: Resource policies attach to the API and can allow or deny based on source IP via aws:SourceIp conditions. Lambda authorizers validate tokens rather than enforcing network policy, usage plans throttle rather than IP-filter, and WAF rate rules limit request rates rather than allowlisting IPs.

q: A WAF rate-based rule blocks legitimate users behind corporate NAT gateways because thousands of users share a few IP addresses. The team wants rate limiting applied per session cookie rather than per IP. Which rate-based rule feature enables this?
options: WAF Bot Control managed rule group
WAF CAPTCHA action
Increasing the rule's rate limit threshold
Scope-down statements on the rate-based rule
explain: Scope-down statements narrow the aggregation key — for example, counting requests per cookie or header instead of per IP. Bot Control targets bot behavior rather than keying, CAPTCHA challenges users rather than changing aggregation, and raising the threshold weakens protection for everyone.

q: A fleet of EC2 instances connects to RDS for MySQL with a shared database password in config files, and rotating it requires coordinated deployments. Which authentication method eliminates stored database passwords?
options: Secrets Manager rotation with a Lambda function
RDS IAM database authentication with short-lived auth tokens
Longer, more complex shared passwords
Storing the password in Systems Manager Parameter Store
explain: IAM database authentication issues short-lived tokens, so no password is stored or rotated. Secrets Manager rotation still stores a password between rotations, longer passwords do not remove the shared-secret problem, and Parameter Store still holds a static secret.

q: A company runs Amazon MSK and wants Kafka clients to authenticate with certificates issued by its private CA, with no passwords or long-lived secrets to rotate. Which MSK authentication method fits?
options: Mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication
SASL/SCRAM with Secrets Manager rotation
IAM access control for MSK
Unauthenticated access inside the VPC
explain: mTLS authenticates clients with client certificates from the company's CA, eliminating shared secrets. SASL/SCRAM still uses passwords, IAM auth uses signatures rather than the private CA certificates, and unauthenticated access provides no authentication at all.

q: Engineers assume project-scoped roles, and the security team wants S3 and DynamoDB policies to automatically grant access to resources tagged with the engineer's project — without updating policies for each new project. Which IAM pattern enables this?
options: A separate IAM role per project
IAM permission boundaries on every role
ABAC with STS session tags passed at role assumption
Resource-based policies on every S3 object
explain: Session tags passed via sts:TagSession let policies compare the principal's project tag against resource tags, scaling to new projects automatically. Per-project roles multiply management overhead, permission boundaries only cap permissions, and per-object policies do not scale.

q: A company must continuously collect evidence for SOC 2 and PCI DSS audits across 40 AWS accounts — configuration snapshots, user activity, and compliance check results — without manual screenshots and spreadsheets. Which service automates evidence collection mapped to control frameworks?
options: AWS Artifact
AWS Config rules
CloudTrail Lake
AWS Audit Manager
explain: Audit Manager continuously gathers evidence and maps it to controls in frameworks like SOC 2 and PCI DSS. Artifact provides on-demand compliance reports rather than collecting evidence, Config rules check configuration without framework mapping, and CloudTrail Lake stores API activity without audit-framework organization.

q: A prospect's security questionnaire asks for AWS's current SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. Where can the company download these on demand?
options: AWS Service Health Dashboard
AWS Artifact
AWS Support Center
The AWS Trust & Safety contact form
explain: Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS compliance reports and certifications. The Health Dashboard shows service status, the Support Center handles cases, and Trust & Safety handles abuse reports — none distribute compliance documents.

q: After a security incident, responders need a record of which internal hosts queried a suspicious domain. VPC DNS queries currently leave no audit trail. Which feature logs DNS queries made by resources in the VPC?
options: Route 53 Resolver query logging
VPC Flow Logs
Route 53 health checks
AWS Network Firewall flow logs
explain: Resolver query logging records DNS queries from VPC resources for forensic analysis. Flow Logs capture IP traffic without DNS names, health checks monitor endpoint availability, and Network Firewall logs show allowed or denied traffic rather than DNS query history.

q: An analytics application reads objects from a shared S3 bucket, but privacy rules require Social Security numbers to be masked before the application ever sees them. The stored objects must remain unchanged. Which S3 feature transforms objects on retrieval?
options: S3 Select
S3 Batch Operations
S3 Object Lock
S3 Object Lambda
explain: Object Lambda invokes a Lambda function to transform objects — such as masking PII — as they are retrieved, leaving stored objects intact. S3 Select filters rows and columns but cannot mask patterns generically, Batch Operations transform stored copies rather than retrieval-time views, and Object Lock provides immutability rather than transformation.

q: A team stores API tokens in Systems Manager Parameter Store and needs tokens to automatically expire with a notification before expiry, so stale credentials are never used silently. Which Parameter Store capability supports expiration with notification?
options: Standard parameters with tags
Secrets Manager rotation schedules
Advanced parameters with parameter policies
Parameter Store change notifications via SNS alone
explain: Advanced parameters support parameter policies for expiration and no-change notifications. Standard parameters lack policies, Secrets Manager is a different service for secrets rotation, and SNS notifications alone cannot enforce expiration.

q: A security team is drowning in Security Hub findings — informational items from trusted accounts clutter the queue and slow response to critical findings. Which Security Hub feature automatically archives or escalates findings based on criteria?
options: Security Hub custom insights
GuardDuty suppression rules
Security Hub automation rules
Config conformance packs
explain: Automation rules automatically update finding fields — such as archiving informational findings or raising severity — when criteria match. Custom insights only filter views without changing findings, GuardDuty suppression rules apply to GuardDuty rather than Security Hub, and conformance packs assess configuration rather than triaging findings.

q: A central logging bucket must accept writes from every account in the AWS Organization, including accounts created next month, while rejecting requests from outside the organization. Which bucket policy condition implements this?
options: aws:PrincipalOrgID matching the organization ID
aws:SourceIp matching the corporate range
aws:PrincipalArn listing each account's role
aws:SecureTransport set to true
explain: The aws:PrincipalOrgID condition grants access to any principal in the organization, automatically covering new accounts. IP conditions do not identify organization membership, listing ARNs requires updates for every new account, and SecureTransport only enforces TLS.

q: After a penetration test exploited IMDSv1 via SSRF, the security team wants to guarantee that no new EC2 instance in the organization can launch without requiring IMDSv2. Which control enforces this organization-wide?
options: A security group rule blocking port 80
An IAM policy attached to developers
Enabling IMDSv2 on existing instances
An SCP denying ec2:RunInstances unless IMDSv2 is required
explain: An SCP with a condition on IMDSv2 token requirements blocks instance launches across all accounts unless IMDSv2 is enforced. Security groups cannot control metadata service versions, IAM policies on developers do not cover all launch paths such as Auto Scaling, and fixing existing instances does not prevent new vulnerable launches.

q: A GuardDuty finding flags an EC2 instance communicating with a known malicious domain. The team wants the instance automatically isolated — all traffic blocked — within seconds, without waiting for a human. Which automation achieves this?
options: A CloudWatch alarm on CPU utilization
An EventBridge rule matching the GuardDuty finding that triggers a Lambda function to revoke the instance's security groups
Inspector rescanning the instance
A Config rule marking the instance noncompliant
explain: EventBridge captures the GuardDuty finding in real time and Lambda revokes security group rules to quarantine the instance immediately. CPU alarms do not detect compromise, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities rather than responding to active threats, and Config rules only flag noncompliance without isolating the host.

q: A Spot-based Auto Scaling group loses instances to interruptions faster than replacements launch, causing capacity dips. Which Auto Scaling feature proactively replaces Spot Instances when EC2 signals elevated interruption risk?
options: Scheduled scaling actions
Capacity Rebalancing
Predictive scaling
Instance refresh
explain: Capacity Rebalancing launches replacements when the Spot rebalance recommendation signals elevated interruption risk. Scheduled scaling follows timetables rather than risk signals, predictive scaling forecasts load rather than Spot risk, and instance refresh rolls out configuration changes.

q: A site uses Lambda@Edge on every viewer request for simple URL rewrites and header normalization, and the per-request charges are adding up at high traffic. The logic needs no network calls and runs in under a millisecond. Which change cuts edge compute cost?
options: Move the logic to CloudFront Functions, which cost less per invocation than Lambda@Edge
Increase the Lambda@Edge memory allocation
Add more CloudFront edge locations
Disable CloudFront caching
explain: CloudFront Functions are priced far lower per invocation and suit lightweight edge logic without network access. More memory raises Lambda@Edge cost, edge locations do not change compute pricing, and disabling caching increases origin load and cost.

q: An RDS database is sized up mainly to handle thousands of idle application connections rather than actual query load. Which change could allow a smaller, cheaper instance without hurting performance?
options: Enable Multi-AZ for connection failover
Increase the max_connections parameter
Add read replicas for the idle connections
Place RDS Proxy in front of the database to pool connections
explain: RDS Proxy multiplexes thousands of application connections into a small pool of database connections, removing the need to oversize the instance for connection count. Multi-AZ addresses availability, raising max_connections on an oversized instance keeps the oversizing, and read replicas add cost rather than reducing it.

q: An application logs verbosely to CloudWatch Logs, but most log groups are only queried during rare incidents. Ingestion and 1-year Standard retention dominate the observability bill. Which log class cuts storage cost for rarely accessed logs?
options: CloudWatch Logs Standard with shorter retention
Exporting logs to EBS volumes
The CloudWatch Logs Infrequent Access log class
Disabling CloudWatch Logs encryption
explain: The Infrequent Access log class offers cheaper storage for logs queried rarely, with a per-GB ingestion fee suited to this pattern. Shorter retention loses the 1-year history, EBS is not a log store, and encryption has no meaningful cost impact.

q: A high-traffic API Gateway REST API has full request/response data logging enabled to CloudWatch Logs, and log ingestion dominates the API's cost. The team only needs error visibility, not full payloads. Which change cuts logging cost?
options: Enable API Gateway caching
Reduce execution logging to ERROR level and disable full request/response data tracing
Switch the API to a private endpoint
Increase the throttling limits
explain: ERROR-level logging without data tracing keeps failure visibility while eliminating the bulk of ingestion volume. Caching does not reduce logging volume, private endpoints change network access rather than logging, and higher throttling permits more traffic and more logs.

q: A company spends heavily on CloudFront data transfer and request fees each month with steady, predictable traffic for the next year. Which commitment option discounts CloudFront usage?
options: The CloudFront security savings bundle
EC2 Reserved Instances
A Compute Savings Plan
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
explain: The CloudFront savings bundle commits to monthly usage for a discounted rate. EC2 RIs and Compute Savings Plans cover compute rather than CloudFront, and Intelligent-Tiering is S3 storage rather than CDN pricing.

q: Development RDS instances have the default 7-day automated backup retention, and backup storage is a noticeable cost for environments that are rebuilt from code weekly. Which change cuts backup cost for these dev databases?
options: Enable Multi-AZ on the dev instances
Increase backup retention to 35 days for safety
Take manual snapshots daily in addition to automated backups
Reduce automated backup retention to 1 day (or 0) on the dev instances
explain: Shorter retention keeps fewer automated backups, directly cutting backup storage for disposable dev databases. Multi-AZ doubles instance cost, longer retention increases backup storage, and extra manual snapshots add storage rather than reducing it.

q: Analysts run ad-hoc Athena queries, and occasional runaway queries scan tens of terabytes, blowing the monthly budget. Which Athena feature caps how much data a query can scan?
options: Athena engine version 3
Partition projection
Workgroup settings for per-query data usage controls
Athena result reuse
explain: Workgroups enforce per-query and per-workgroup data-scanned limits that cancel runaway queries. Engine v3 improves performance rather than capping cost, partition projection speeds partition pruning, and result reuse avoids rescans but does not cap a novel runaway query.

q: After several projects shut down, the team suspects idle load balancers, unattached EBS volumes, and idle RDS instances are still billing. Which service automatically flags these specific waste categories?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks
AWS Budgets forecasts
CloudWatch anomaly detection
AWS Pricing Calculator
explain: Trusted Advisor's cost optimization checks specifically identify idle load balancers, unattached volumes, and idle RDS instances. Budgets alert on spend without identifying the resources, anomaly detection flags metric deviations rather than waste categories, and the Pricing Calculator estimates future cost rather than finding waste.

q: A CI pipeline uploads build artifacts to S3 on every commit, and the bucket grows unboundedly with artifacts nobody ever downloads after a week. Which approach automatically controls this storage growth?
options: Enabling S3 versioning on the bucket
Moving all artifacts to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Increasing the bucket's request rate limits
A lifecycle rule expiring objects after 30 days
explain: A lifecycle expiration rule automatically deletes aging artifacts. Versioning increases storage, Intelligent-Tiering only optimizes class without deleting, and request rate limits do not affect stored volume.

q: A development Aurora cluster has three read replicas that were provisioned 'just in case' but serve no read traffic. The cluster's compute bill is dominated by these idle replicas. Which change cuts cost with no impact on the dev workload?
options: Enabling Aurora Serverless v2
Deleting the unused read replicas
Enabling backtrack on the cluster
Switching to provisioned IOPS storage
explain: Read replicas bill for compute whether or not they serve traffic, so removing idle ones directly cuts cost. Serverless v2 is a larger migration, backtrack adds cost for rewind capability, and provisioned IOPS increases storage cost.

q: A DocumentDB cluster supports a development environment used only on weekdays. The cluster bills for compute around the clock. Which action eliminates compute charges nights and weekends?
options: Enabling DocumentDB elastic clusters
Removing all read replicas each evening
Stopping the DocumentDB cluster when not in use
Switching to on-demand backups
explain: DocumentDB supports stopping clusters, which halts compute billing while preserving data. Elastic clusters scale writes rather than pausing, removing replicas leaves the primary billing, and on-demand backups do not affect compute charges.

q: Two VPCs exchange 30 TB/month through a Transit Gateway, and the bill shows large Transit Gateway hourly and data-processing charges. Only these two VPCs need to communicate. Which change reduces this connectivity cost?
options: Replace the Transit Gateway attachment with VPC peering between the two VPCs
Add a second Transit Gateway for redundancy
Enable Transit Gateway multicast
Move both workloads into a single subnet
explain: VPC peering has no hourly charge and no per-GB processing fee, making it cheaper for simple two-VPC connectivity. A second Transit Gateway doubles the hourly cost, multicast adds features rather than cutting cost, and merging subnets across VPCs is not possible.

q: An application sends millions of SNS notifications per month, mostly as SMS messages to mobile users, and messaging is now a top cost driver. Users already have the company's mobile app installed. Which change dramatically cuts notification cost?
options: Batching SMS messages into fewer sends
Switching to SNS FIFO topics
Increasing the SMS spending quota
Switching from SMS to mobile push notifications
explain: Mobile push notifications cost a fraction of SMS per message for users with the app installed. Batching does not change per-message SMS pricing, FIFO topics add ordering rather than lowering SMS rates, and raising the quota only permits more spending.

q: A finance team needs line-item detail of every AWS charge — down to individual resources and hours — to build custom chargeback reports that Cost Explorer cannot produce. Which combination provides the most granular billing data?
options: AWS Budgets with forecasted alerts
AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) queried with Athena
The monthly PDF invoice
Cost Anomaly Detection alerts
explain: CUR delivers the most detailed billing dataset, and Athena enables custom SQL analysis for chargeback. Budgets track thresholds rather than line items, the PDF invoice lacks resource-level detail, and anomaly detection alerts on spikes without granular data.

q: CloudTrail delivers management events to both S3 and CloudWatch Logs, and the CloudWatch Logs ingestion charges are enormous because every API call is logged. The team rarely queries recent events in CloudWatch but must retain the audit trail. Which change cuts cost while keeping the audit trail?
options: Disabling CloudTrail in all Regions
Increasing the CloudWatch Logs retention period
Keep CloudTrail delivery to S3 and remove the CloudWatch Logs delivery
Enabling CloudTrail Insights on all trails
explain: S3 is far cheaper than CloudWatch Logs for storing the full audit trail that is rarely queried. Disabling CloudTrail loses auditing, longer retention increases cost, and Insights adds event types rather than reducing ingestion.

q: An e-commerce application has predictable daily traffic waves, but target-tracking scaling reacts after load arrives, causing latency during ramp-up, while scheduled scaling needs constant retuning. Which Auto Scaling policy forecasts demand and provisions capacity ahead of the wave?
options: Predictive scaling
Simple scaling with large step adjustments
Manual scaling each morning
Spot Fleet diversification
explain: Predictive scaling uses machine learning on historical patterns to provision capacity before demand arrives. Simple scaling still reacts to alarms, manual scaling is operationally heavy, and Spot diversification addresses interruption risk rather than forecast-based provisioning.

q: A company cannot attribute shared AWS costs — such as data transfer and support charges — to product teams using only resource tags, since these charges carry no tags. Which billing feature creates custom cost groupings with rules that include untagged charges?
options: AWS Budgets
Linked account consolidated billing
Tag-based cost allocation reports
AWS Cost Categories
explain: Cost Categories define custom groupings with rules that can allocate untagged and shared costs to teams. Budgets monitor spend rather than grouping it, consolidated billing aggregates accounts without team attribution, and tag-based allocation only works where tags exist.

q: An analytics pipeline copies 50 TB/month from S3 in us-east-1 to process in eu-west-1, incurring large inter-Region data transfer charges. The processed results are consumed back in us-east-1. Which change eliminates the transfer cost?
options: Enabling S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket
Running the processing in us-east-1 where the data already lives
Replicating the bucket with S3 Batch Replication
Compressing the data before transfer
explain: Processing data in the same Region as the source avoids inter-Region transfer charges entirely. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than cutting transfer fees, Batch Replication copies data across Regions which still incurs transfer, and compression reduces but does not eliminate the charge.

q: A Lambda function was configured with high provisioned concurrency for a launch event, but traffic never materialized and the concurrency sits unused, billing every hour. Which change stops this waste while keeping the function available?
options: Remove the unused provisioned concurrency so the function scales on demand
Increase the function's memory allocation
Enable Lambda SnapStart
Add reserved concurrency to the function
explain: Provisioned concurrency bills whether or not it is used, so removing it returns the function to pay-per-invocation scaling. More memory raises per-invocation cost, SnapStart addresses cold starts rather than unused concurrency, and reserved concurrency caps invocations rather than removing the provisioned-concurrency charge.

q: A bucket replicates all objects cross-Region for disaster recovery, but only objects under the /critical/ prefix actually need a second copy. Replicating everything doubles storage and transfer costs unnecessarily. Which change limits replication cost?
options: Disabling versioning on the source bucket
Switching to S3 Batch Replication
Adding a prefix filter to the replication rule so only /critical/ objects replicate
Enabling Replication Time Control
explain: Replication rules support prefix filters, so only the critical prefix replicates and the rest stays single-copy. Disabling versioning breaks replication prerequisites, Batch Replication is for existing objects rather than filtering, and RTC adds an SLA rather than reducing scope.

q: A WAF web ACL logs every request to CloudWatch Logs, and log ingestion plus long retention has become a major cost line. The team rarely queries the logs but must retain them for audits. Which change cuts logging cost?
options: Disabling WAF logging entirely
Increasing the WAF rate limit
Sampling fewer requests with CloudWatch Logs
Sending WAF logs to S3 instead of CloudWatch Logs
explain: WAF can deliver full logs to S3, where storage is far cheaper than CloudWatch Logs ingestion for rarely queried audit data. Disabling logging loses audit evidence, rate limits do not affect logging cost, and CloudWatch Logs sampling is not a WAF logging option.

q: An Amazon OpenSearch Service domain runs on x86 instances with steady search traffic. The team wants better price-performance without changing queries or capacity. Which change delivers this?
options: Moving all indexes to UltraWarm storage
Migrating the domain to Graviton instance types
Enabling cross-cluster replication
Increasing the shard count
explain: Graviton instances offer better price-performance for OpenSearch with no application changes. UltraWarm suits rarely queried data rather than steady search traffic, cross-cluster replication adds a second domain's cost, and more shards increase overhead rather than cutting cost.

q: A team created hundreds of individual CloudWatch metric alarms — one per EC2 instance — and alarm charges are significant. They still need to know when any instance in a fleet is unhealthy. Which approach reduces alarm cost?
options: Replace per-instance alarms with metric math expressions and composite alarms
Enable detailed monitoring on every instance
Create more granular per-process alarms
Export metrics to S3 and delete the alarms
explain: Metric math and composite alarms evaluate fleet health with far fewer alarm objects, cutting alarm charges. Detailed monitoring adds cost, more granular alarms increase cost, and deleting alarms removes the alerting the team still needs.

q: Development RDS databases run 24/7 with Multi-AZ enabled, doubling instance cost for environments where brief downtime is acceptable. Which change cuts dev database cost with minimal effort?
options: Enabling Performance Insights
Switching to provisioned IOPS storage
Running dev databases as Single-AZ deployments
Increasing the backup retention period
explain: Single-AZ removes the standby instance cost, which is acceptable for dev environments tolerating brief downtime. Performance Insights adds cost, provisioned IOPS increases cost, and longer retention increases storage cost.

q: A company runs its order database on an Aurora MySQL cluster in us-east-1 and must survive a full Regional outage with recovery in under one minute and minimal data loss. Which solution meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?
options: Create a cross-Region Aurora read replica and promote it manually during an outage
Deploy an Aurora Global Database and use managed failover to the secondary Region
Enable Multi-AZ on the Aurora cluster
Copy automated snapshots to a second Region and restore them after an outage
explain: Aurora Global Database replicates with a typical 1-second RPO, and managed failover to the secondary Region typically completes in under a minute with no manual steps. Manual replica promotion is slower and error-prone, Multi-AZ protects against AZ failure rather than a Regional outage, and snapshot restore has the highest RTO of all options.

q: A streaming platform runs Amazon MSK with brokers spread across three AZs. A broker failure recently caused permanent data loss for partitions whose messages had not yet been consumed. Which configuration prevents data loss when a broker fails?
options: Set the topic replication factor to 3 with min.insync.replicas=2 so every acknowledged write exists on multiple brokers
Run all brokers in a single AZ to reduce replication lag
Set the replication factor to 1 to simplify partition leader election
Increase the retention period on the topics
explain: Replication factor 3 with min.insync.replicas=2 guarantees each acknowledged write is stored on at least two brokers, so one broker loss never destroys the only copy. A single AZ concentrates failure risk, replication factor 1 means the only copy dies with its broker, and longer retention creates no additional copies.

q: An order system must hold each new order message for 15 minutes before any consumer can process it, giving customers a cancellation window. Which SQS feature provides this?
options: A FIFO queue with message group IDs
A delay queue using DelaySeconds, which keeps messages invisible to consumers until the delay expires
A redrive policy with maxReceiveCount
Long polling with a 20-second wait time
explain: Delay queues keep each message invisible for the configured delay of up to 15 minutes, exactly matching the cancellation window. FIFO ordering does not delay delivery, redrive policies isolate poison messages rather than delaying them, and long polling only reduces empty receives.

q: A public API backed by Lambda experiences traffic surges that overwhelm a downstream legacy system, causing cascading failures. The team must cap the request rate reaching the backend while keeping the API available. Which approach meets this requirement?
options: Increase the Lambda function memory allocation
Disable API Gateway caching
Add additional deployment stages to the API
Configure throttling limits and usage plans on API Gateway to cap requests per second
explain: Throttling and usage plans shed excess load at the API edge so the backend never receives more than it can handle. More memory does not limit request rate, disabling caching increases backend load, and extra deployment stages provide no rate limiting.

q: A company runs a critical database on a single EC2 instance with EBS volumes and needs automated point-in-time backups with cross-Region copies for disaster recovery. Which solution provides this with the least operational overhead?
options: Use AWS Backup with a backup plan that snapshots the volumes on a schedule and copies backups to a second Region
Configure the volumes in a RAID 0 stripe for faster recovery
Store the database files on instance store volumes
Manually create EBS snapshots before each deployment
explain: AWS Backup automates scheduled snapshots and cross-Region copies in one policy. RAID 0 increases failure risk and is not a backup, instance store volumes are ephemeral and lose data on stop, and manual snapshots are error-prone with no cross-Region copies.

q: A company serves a latency-sensitive trading API from two Regions. Client firewalls only allow traffic to fixed IP addresses, and failover between Regions must occur in under a minute when health checks fail. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Route 53 failover routing with health checks
AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups in both Regions and health checks
A single Application Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing
CloudFront with an origin group
explain: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs that satisfy firewall allowlists and performs health-checked failover typically in under a minute. Route 53 failover is DNS-based, so client caching delays failover and it provides no static IPs; a single ALB is Regional; CloudFront is an HTTP cache, not a fixed-IP TCP failover solution.

q: An ECS service behind an ALB deploys new task versions that fail health checks, causing user-facing errors until the team rolls back manually. The team needs deployments that shift traffic only after new tasks pass health checks, with automatic rollback on failure. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Permanently double the service desired task count
Disable ALB health checks during deployments
Use CodeDeploy blue/green deployments for the ECS service with a test listener and automatic rollback on failed health checks
Increase the task definition CPU and memory
explain: CodeDeploy blue/green validates the new task set behind a test listener, shifts production traffic only after health checks pass, and rolls back automatically on failure. Doubling tasks wastes capacity without safe shifting, disabling health checks hides failures, and more CPU does not fix broken deployments.

q: A company wants its AWS Backup copies isolated in a separate security account so that a compromise of the production account cannot delete or alter them. Which design provides this isolation?
options: Keep all backups in the production account vault
Manually share snapshots with the security account each week
Enable S3 Versioning on the backup bucket
Use AWS Backup cross-account copy to a vault in the security account, protected by vault access policies
explain: Cross-account copy places recovery points in a separate account vault where production credentials have no delete rights. Same-account backups share the blast radius, manual sharing is operationally fragile, and versioning does not isolate across accounts.

q: During an AZ impairment, a company running a multi-AZ application needs traffic shifted away from the impaired AZ within minutes, without DNS changes or new deployments. Which capability provides this?
options: Use Amazon Application Recovery Controller zonal shift to move traffic away from the impaired AZ
Update Route 53 weighted records manually
Terminate all instances in the impaired AZ
Deploy a second copy of the application in another Region
explain: ARC zonal shift moves traffic off an impaired AZ quickly through load balancer integration, with no DNS propagation delay. Manual DNS edits are slow and error-prone, terminating instances does not reroute traffic, and a second Region is excessive for an AZ-level event.

q: A serverless application uses DynamoDB in us-east-1 and must keep serving reads and writes from eu-west-1 during a Regional outage, with data replicated in near real time. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
Use DynamoDB global tables with replicas in both Regions
Export the table to S3 daily with DynamoDB export
Create a read replica of the DynamoDB table
explain: Global tables provide active-active multi-Region replication, typically under a second, with local reads and writes in each Region. Point-in-time recovery restores to a moment in time but does not serve multi-Region traffic, S3 exports are batch-based and slow, and DynamoDB has no read-replica feature.

q: A company keeps EBS snapshots for compliance: recent snapshots must restore in minutes, but snapshots older than 90 days are almost never restored. Engineers keep forgetting to move old snapshots to the Archive tier manually. How can the tiering be automated?
options: An Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policy that automatically transitions snapshots older than 90 days to the Archive tier
Deleting snapshots older than 90 days
Enabling Fast Snapshot Restore on every snapshot
Copying every snapshot to a second Region
explain: Data Lifecycle Manager policies can automatically archive snapshots past a set age, keeping recent snapshots in the standard tier for fast restores while cutting storage cost on old ones. Deleting snapshots violates retention, Fast Snapshot Restore speeds restores without reducing storage cost, and cross-region copies multiply cost.

q: A team deploys application updates with Elastic Beanstalk, but failed deployments leave the environment in a partially updated state that takes hours to repair. They need deployments where a failure leaves the previous version fully intact. Which deployment policy meets this requirement?
options: All at once
Rolling
Rolling with additional batch
Immutable
explain: Immutable deployments launch a full new fleet and swap traffic only on success, so a failed deployment leaves the old fleet untouched. All-at-once causes downtime, while rolling and rolling-with-additional-batch update instances in place, so failures strand mixed versions.

q: After an RDS Multi-AZ failover, thousands of application connections reconnect at once and overwhelm the new primary, causing a second outage. Which solution reduces failover disruption and absorbs the connection surge?
options: Place RDS Proxy in front of the database to pool connections and fail over faster than direct application reconnects
Add RDS read replicas to handle writes during failover
Increase the DB instance class
Disable automated backups during failover
explain: RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool and fails over more quickly, shielding the new primary from a reconnect storm. Read replicas cannot accept writes, a larger instance does not fix connection churn, and disabling backups harms durability without helping connections.

q: A Lambda function reads from an SQS queue through an event source mapping. A poison message exhausts all retries, and the team wants the failed batch captured in a dead-letter queue without writing custom DLQ polling code. Where should the on-failure destination be configured?
options: On the Lambda function's asynchronous invocation settings
As a Lambda destination on the function's $LATEST version
On the event source mapping, which sends failed batches to the configured SQS queue or SNS topic after retries are exhausted
Only on the SQS queue's redrive policy
explain: For poll-based event source mappings, the on-failure destination is configured on the mapping itself, which routes failed batches to SQS or SNS after retries are exhausted. Asynchronous invocation destinations apply to direct async invokes rather than poll-based mappings, and a redrive policy alone moves messages without capturing the failed batch for analysis.

q: An Auto Scaling group takes several minutes to bring new instances into service because each instance runs a long initialization script, causing dropped requests during sudden spikes. Which feature shortens the time to serve traffic?
options: Increase the maximum size of the group
Switch to a larger instance type
Configure an Auto Scaling warm pool of pre-initialized stopped instances
Disable health checks so instances register faster
explain: Warm pools keep pre-initialized instances in a stopped state ready to start quickly, cutting scale-out time dramatically. A higher maximum does not speed initialization, larger instances still run the script, and disabling health checks risks sending traffic to unready instances.

q: A healthcare company needs database backups to be immutable for 7 years, but legal requires a break-glass path: designated compliance officers must be able to delete recovery points in rare, audited scenarios. Compliance mode is too strict. Which Vault Lock mode fits?
options: Vault Lock in Governance mode, which keeps recovery points immutable except to users granted specific IAM permissions for audited deletion
Vault Lock in Compliance mode
S3 Versioning on the backup bucket
Manual monthly copies to a second account
explain: Governance mode enforces immutability while still allowing specifically permissioned users to delete recovery points, providing the audited break-glass path legal requires. Compliance mode blocks deletion by everyone including the root user, versioning does not stop privileged deletes, and manual copies are operationally fragile.

q: A website serves dynamic content from an ALB origin. When the primary Region ALB becomes unhealthy, visitors see errors until engineers intervene. Which CloudFront configuration provides automatic failover to a standby origin?
options: Configure a CloudFront origin group with the primary ALB and a secondary origin, failing over on configured HTTP error status codes
Increase the CloudFront default TTL
Add more edge locations
Enable CloudFront signed URLs
explain: Origin groups automatically fail over to the secondary origin when the primary returns configured error codes. TTL changes affect caching rather than failover, edge locations do not add origin redundancy, and signed URLs control access rather than availability.

q: A company runs workloads in 20 member accounts and needs all EC2 state-change events collected on a central security account's event bus for monitoring. Which configuration enables this?
options: A resource-based policy on the central event bus allowing PutEvents from the member accounts, with rules in each account forwarding matching events to the central bus
VPC peering between all accounts
Enabling CloudTrail data events in each account
Creating one event bus shared across all accounts
explain: Event buses accept cross-account PutEvents when their resource policy allows it, so member-account rules can forward events to the central bus. VPC peering carries network traffic rather than events, CloudTrail records API calls instead of routing bus events, and event buses are account-scoped resources that cannot be shared directly.

q: A company needs disaster recovery for EC2 workloads to a second Region with recovery point objectives measured in seconds and minimal operational overhead. Which service provides this?
options: Copy AMIs to the second Region weekly
Restore from manual snapshots during an outage
Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery with continuous block-level replication to the second Region
Sync data disks to S3 with a cron job
explain: Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates block-level changes, delivering RPOs measured in seconds with fast failover. Weekly AMIs and manual snapshot restores have large RPOs and slow RTOs, and cron-based S3 sync is fragile and crash-inconsistent.

q: A company connects its data center to AWS with a single Direct Connect connection. A failure of that connection would halt replication to the cloud. Which design provides resilient connectivity with automatic failover?
options: Add a second virtual interface on the same connection
Order a second Direct Connect connection at the same location terminating on the same router
Replace Direct Connect with a Site-to-Site VPN only
Provision a second Direct Connect connection at a different location, or a Site-to-Site VPN backup, with BGP failover
explain: A second connection at a separate location, or a VPN backup, with BGP provides automatic path failover. A second VIF on the same physical connection shares its fate, the same location and router risk correlated failure, and VPN-only is lower bandwidth and less consistent than Direct Connect.

q: A team runs an active-passive application across two Regions and needs a single audited control to shift traffic during disaster-recovery drills, with safety rules that prevent accidentally taking both Regions offline. Which Application Recovery Controller feature provides this?
options: ARC routing controls with safety rules that block unsafe traffic shifts
Manually editing Route 53 weighted records
Changing ALB listeners by runbook
Creating CloudFront invalidations
explain: Routing controls provide a single audited switch for traffic shifting, and safety rules prevent states such as zero healthy Regions. Manual DNS edits are slow and error-prone, runbook listener changes lack guardrails, and invalidations only clear caches.

q: A company must protect critical S3 data against accidental deletion and Regional outages, keeping a recoverable copy in a second Region. Which combination meets both requirements?
options: Enable MFA Delete only
Enable S3 Versioning and configure Cross-Region Replication to a bucket in a second Region
Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Configure a lifecycle rule to expire objects after 30 days
explain: Versioning protects against overwrites and deletes while Cross-Region Replication maintains a second-Regional copy. MFA Delete alone does not replicate data, Intelligent-Tiering is a cost optimization, and expiration deletes data, which is the opposite of protection.

q: A company runs a multi-Region active-passive application and discovered during a real outage that the standby Region lacked sufficient capacity. How can they continuously validate disaster-recovery readiness before an actual failover?
options: Run the failover procedure manually once a year
Disable health checks in the standby Region
Use Route 53 Application Recovery Controller readiness checks to continuously audit quotas, capacity, and routing configuration
Keep both Regions active-active at all times
explain: ARC readiness checks continuously monitor recovery preparedness including capacity, limits, and routing. Annual manual tests go stale between runs, disabling health checks blinds monitoring, and active-active doubles cost for a passive design.

q: A clustered database requires two EC2 instances in the same AZ to have concurrent read/write access to a shared block volume for its active-active configuration. Which storage option supports this?
options: EBS gp3 volume attached to both instances
EFS file system mounted on both instances
Instance store volumes on each instance
EBS io2 volume with Multi-Attach enabled
explain: EBS Multi-Attach on io1/io2 volumes allows concurrent block-level access from multiple Nitro instances in the same AZ. gp3 does not support Multi-Attach, EFS is NFS file storage rather than block storage, and instance store volumes cannot be shared between instances.

q: A team designed Multi-AZ failover for their application but has never tested it under real failure conditions. They want to safely simulate an AZ impairment in a controlled experiment with automatic rollback. Which service supports this?
options: AWS Config conformance packs
AWS Fault Injection Simulator (FIS) with experiment templates and stop conditions
CloudWatch Synthetics canaries
AWS Trusted Advisor
explain: FIS runs controlled failure-injection experiments with guardrails and stop conditions that halt the experiment if impact exceeds thresholds. Config checks configuration compliance, Synthetics monitor endpoints, and Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, but none inject faults.

q: A CloudFront distribution runs a URL-rewrite function on viewer request for every request, but the rewrite is only needed when CloudFront actually fetches from the origin — cache hits do not need it. Which change cuts edge compute invocations?
options: Move the function to the origin request trigger so it runs only on cache misses
Increase the function memory allocation
Disable caching so every request reaches the origin
Run the rewrite on viewer response instead
explain: Origin request triggers fire only when CloudFront forwards a request to the origin, so cache hits skip the function entirely. Viewer request runs on every request including hits, function memory is fixed for CloudFront Functions, disabling caching destroys the hit ratio, and viewer response also runs on every request.

q: A company must migrate 50 TB from on-premises NAS to S3 within two weeks over good network connectivity, with minimal operational effort and automatic retry of failures. Which service fits?
options: rsync over a Site-to-Site VPN
AWS DataSync with parallelized transfers, scheduling, and built-in retry
Mailing hard drives to AWS
Manually uploading with the S3 console
explain: DataSync parallelizes transfers, schedules the migration, and retries failures automatically. rsync over VPN is single-threaded and fragile, mailing drives is slow and manual, and console uploads do not scale to 50 TB.

q: An Aurora MySQL cluster writer instance is CPU-saturated by reporting queries, slowing down order writes. Reporting can tolerate slightly stale data. Which change offloads the reporting load with minimal changes?
options: Enable Multi-AZ on the cluster
Increase the writer instance class
Add Aurora Replicas and point reporting queries at the cluster reader endpoint
Enable Aurora Backtrack
explain: The reader endpoint load-balances reads across Aurora Replicas, removing reporting load from the writer. Multi-AZ adds a standby for failover rather than read capacity, a larger writer is costly and keeps workloads mixed, and Backtrack rewinds data rather than scaling reads.

q: A global user base uploads large video files to S3 in us-east-1, and users in distant Regions report slow uploads. The company needs faster uploads without changing the application endpoint. Which solution helps?
options: Enable S3 Versioning
Move the bucket to each user Region
Use S3 multipart upload only
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to route uploads through nearby CloudFront edge locations
explain: Transfer Acceleration uses the edge network for the long-haul portion of the upload, speeding distant uploads with only an endpoint change. Versioning does not speed transfers, per-Region buckets fragment data, and multipart upload helps large files but not geographic latency.

q: A video-rendering workload needs 2,500 MiB/s of sustained throughput from EBS, but a single gp3 volume caps throughput at 1,000 MiB/s. Which configuration delivers the required throughput?
options: A single io2 volume with 64,000 provisioned IOPS
A RAID 0 stripe across multiple gp3 volumes to aggregate each volume's throughput
A single Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volume
A larger gp2 volume
explain: Striping gp3 volumes in RAID 0 aggregates each volume's throughput, exceeding the 1,000 MiB/s per-volume cap. A single io2 volume targets extreme IOPS rather than this throughput need and costs more, st1 tops out at 500 MiB/s per volume, and larger gp2 volumes still cap each volume's throughput at 250 MiB/s.

q: A data-science team runs a 6-hour model-training job on EC2 that must survive interruptions without losing in-memory progress, resuming exactly where it left off after a stop and start. Which EC2 feature provides this?
options: Spot Instances with checkpointing to S3
EC2 Hibernate, which persists RAM to the EBS root volume across stop and start cycles
Terminating the instance nightly
A larger instance type
explain: Hibernate saves RAM contents to the encrypted EBS root volume on stop and restores them on start, resuming in-memory work. Checkpointing requires application code, nightly termination destroys progress, and larger instances do not survive stops.

q: A Java-based Lambda function behind an API experiences high cold-start latency during traffic spikes, hurting response times. The team wants lower cold starts without paying for always-on capacity. Which solution fits?
options: Increase the function memory to 10 GB
Enable provisioned concurrency at peak levels permanently
Enable Lambda SnapStart to restore from a pre-initialized snapshot
Convert the function to a container image
explain: SnapStart restores from an initialized snapshot, cutting Java cold starts with no idle-capacity cost. More memory helps only marginally, permanent provisioned concurrency pays for idle capacity, and container images do not fix JVM initialization time.

q: A REST API serves reference data that changes once daily but receives thousands of identical GET requests per minute, overloading the backend. Which change reduces backend load with minimal effort?
options: Increase Lambda reserved concurrency
Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics
Switch to WebSocket APIs
Enable API Gateway caching with a TTL matching the data freshness requirement
explain: API Gateway caching serves repeated GETs without invoking the backend, slashing load. Reserved concurrency caps Lambda throughput rather than reducing calls, metrics do not reduce load, and WebSockets do not cache responses.

q: A DynamoDB table powers an order system, and three downstream services need the stream of item changes with the ability to replay up to 7 days of history after an outage. DynamoDB Streams caps retention at 24 hours. Which configuration meets the replay requirement?
options: Enable Kinesis Data Streams as a destination for DynamoDB change data capture, which retains records for up to 365 days so consumers can replay a week of changes
Increase the DynamoDB Streams retention period to 7 days
Poll the table with a Scan every hour
Export the table to S3 once per day
explain: Kinesis Data Streams can be configured as a destination for DynamoDB change data capture and retains records for up to 365 days, so consumers can replay days of changes after an outage. DynamoDB Streams retention maxes out at 24 hours and cannot be extended, hourly scans miss changes between polls and burn read capacity, and daily S3 exports are far too coarse for change replay.

q: A global application serves personalized, uncacheable dynamic content over HTTPS, and users in distant Regions experience high latency. Which service accelerates this dynamic traffic over the AWS global network?
options: CloudFront
AWS Global Accelerator, which routes dynamic TCP and UDP traffic over the AWS backbone with static entry points
S3 Transfer Acceleration
Route 53 geolocation routing
explain: Global Accelerator proxies dynamic traffic over the AWS backbone, cutting internet latency for uncacheable content. CloudFront caches static content, S3 Transfer Acceleration targets S3 uploads, and geolocation routing is DNS-based without backbone acceleration.

q: An Amazon Redshift cluster handles nightly ETL well, but during month-end reporting, dozens of concurrent analyst queries queue up and time out. Which feature absorbs the burst of concurrent queries automatically?
options: Increase the node type permanently
Enable automated snapshots
Enable concurrency scaling to add transient capacity for query bursts
Move the data to S3 and query with Athena only
explain: Concurrency scaling adds ephemeral clusters for query bursts and removes them afterward. Larger nodes permanently raise cost, snapshots do not add compute, and moving to Athena-only is a replatform rather than a fix.

q: A machine learning team trains models on FSx for Lustre linked to an S3 bucket. Training writes checkpoints and updated datasets that must land back in the S3 bucket automatically, without manual copy jobs. Which FSx for Lustre feature provides this?
options: Manually rsyncing from the file system to S3 after each run
A data repository association with automatic export, which writes new and changed files back to the linked S3 bucket
EBS snapshots of the training instances
S3 Versioning on the bucket
explain: A data repository association with automatic export writes new and changed files back to the linked S3 prefix with no copy jobs. Manual rsync adds operational toil, EBS snapshots capture volumes rather than syncing to S3, and versioning protects objects without moving data.

q: A live dashboard polls a REST API every 2 seconds from 50,000 clients, overloading the backend with mostly unchanged responses. Which architecture delivers real-time updates while reducing backend load?
options: Use an API Gateway WebSocket API that pushes updates to clients only when data changes
Increase the polling frequency
Add more REST API stages
Disable API throttling
explain: WebSockets push changes on events, eliminating tens of thousands of clients polling empty responses. Faster polling worsens load, more stages do not change the pattern, and disabling throttling removes protection.

q: A company runs analytics queries against data in S3 and wants to avoid moving data into a warehouse, querying it in place with standard SQL while keeping costs low. Which service provides this?
options: Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster
Amazon Athena, a serverless interactive query service for data in S3
Amazon EMR long-running cluster
Amazon RDS
explain: Athena queries S3 data in place with pay-per-query pricing and no infrastructure. A Redshift cluster must be loaded and billed around the clock, long-running EMR clusters idle between jobs, and RDS is not an S3 query engine.

q: A team configures a CloudFront distribution with an S3 bucket origin using the bucket's website endpoint, then attaches Origin Access Control — but requests fail and OAC has no effect. What is the correct origin configuration for a private bucket?
options: Keep the website endpoint and make the bucket public
Use the S3 REST API endpoint as the origin with Origin Access Control, and keep the bucket private with a policy granting access only to the distribution
Keep the website endpoint and add signed URLs
Point CloudFront at an EC2-hosted copy of the site
explain: Origin Access Control only works with the S3 REST API endpoint; the website endpoint cannot use OAC and forces the bucket to be public. Making the bucket public defeats the private-origin goal, signed URLs control viewer access rather than origin access, and EC2 hosting adds cost and management for static content.

q: An RDS database slows intermittently, and the team needs to identify which SQL queries consume the most load over time with minimal setup. Which feature provides this?
options: Enable Enhanced Monitoring at 1-second granularity permanently
Export slow query logs to CloudWatch and parse them manually
Increase the instance class until the problem disappears
Enable Performance Insights to visualize top SQL by load
explain: Performance Insights aggregates wait events and top SQL by load out of the box. One-second Enhanced Monitoring adds cost and shows OS metrics rather than query attribution, manual log parsing is heavy operational work, and upsizing masks the root cause.

q: Athena queries over years of S3 log data scan terabytes and run for minutes, though analysts usually query a single day. Which change most reduces scan volume and query time?
options: Partition the data by date so queries scan only the relevant prefixes
Increase the Athena workgroup compute capacity
Convert the data to uncompressed CSV
Enable S3 Versioning on the log bucket
explain: Partitioning prunes irrelevant prefixes so queries scan only the requested days. Athena is serverless with no compute to scale, uncompressed CSV scans more data, and versioning does not reduce scan volume.

q: A Kinesis data stream throughput swings wildly between idle nights and massive daytime peaks, and the team is tired of manually resharding. Which capacity mode adapts automatically?
options: Keep provisioned mode and double the shards
Switch the stream to on-demand capacity mode
Add enhanced fan-out consumers
Reduce the record size
explain: On-demand mode scales shard capacity automatically with throughput. Doubling shards permanently wastes money, enhanced fan-out addresses per-consumer reads rather than stream capacity, and smaller records do not auto-scale shards.

q: A Hadoop cluster on EC2 needs instances spread across distinct hardware racks so a rack failure affects only part of the cluster, while keeping all instances in a single AZ for low latency. Which placement group type provides this?
options: Cluster placement group
Spread placement group
Partition placement group, which isolates instances into partitions across racks
No placement group
explain: Partition placement groups spread instances across logical partitions (racks), limiting the blast radius of hardware failure within one AZ. Cluster packs instances together, spread places at most one instance per rack which does not scale for Hadoop, and no placement group gives no rack awareness.

q: A compute-heavy Lambda function runs slowly at 512 MB. The team wants faster execution without rewriting code. Which tuning step is MOST likely to help?
options: Increase the timeout to 15 minutes
Enable provisioned concurrency
Use a larger deployment package
Increase the function memory, which proportionally increases CPU allocation
explain: Lambda allocates CPU proportionally to memory, so more memory speeds compute-bound code. Timeout does not add CPU, provisioned concurrency fixes cold starts rather than execution speed, and package size does not affect CPU.

q: A database on EBS sees inconsistent throughput on older EC2 instance types because EBS traffic competes with instance network traffic. Which instance capability gives EBS dedicated bandwidth?
options: EBS-optimized instances, which provide dedicated bandwidth for EBS I/O separate from other network traffic
Attaching more EBS volumes
Using instance store volumes
A larger AMI
explain: EBS-optimized instances reserve dedicated bandwidth for EBS traffic so it never contends with regular network traffic. More volumes do not add dedicated bandwidth, instance store is ephemeral, and AMI size is unrelated to network contention.

q: A team wants to canary-test a new API version by sending 5% of production traffic to new targets while 95% stays on the current version, all behind one ALB. Which configuration provides this?
options: Weighted target groups on the ALB listener forwarding 95% and 5% to the two target groups
Two ALBs with DNS-based splitting
A Network Load Balancer
Route 53 failover records
explain: ALB listeners support weighted forwarding across target groups for precise traffic splits. Two ALBs with DNS is coarse and TTL-dependent, NLB does not do layer-7 weighting, and failover records are primary/secondary.

q: A single-AZ analytics job repeatedly reads the same S3 dataset and needs the lowest possible S3 request latency. Which storage class fits?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Express One Zone with directory buckets for single-digit millisecond data access
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard-IA
explain: S3 Express One Zone stores data in a single AZ with directory buckets for consistent single-digit millisecond access. S3 Standard has higher first-byte latency, Glacier Instant Retrieval is for archival access, and Standard-IA targets infrequent access with retrieval fees.

q: A production database on a gp2 volume needs more IOPS immediately, but the team cannot afford downtime. Which approach changes volume performance without stopping the instance?
options: Stop the instance, detach the volume, and create a new one
Add a second instance
Modify the EBS elastic volume to gp3 or io2 while it stays attached and in use
Take a snapshot and restore to a bigger volume during a maintenance window
explain: Elastic volumes allow live changes to type, size, and IOPS without detaching. Stop-and-detach causes downtime, a second instance does not fix the volume, and snapshot restore requires a maintenance window.

q: A read-heavy product catalog on RDS MySQL struggles at peak traffic. Queries are highly repetitive and tolerate 5-minute staleness. Which change reduces database load most effectively?
options: Enable Multi-AZ
Increase the RDS instance class
Add RDS read replicas in the same AZ only
Place ElastiCache for Redis in front of the database and cache query results with a 5-minute TTL
explain: Caching absorbs the repetitive reads that dominate the load, which a TTL matching the staleness tolerance allows. Multi-AZ aids failover rather than read scale, upsizing is costly, and read replicas still execute every query against the database.

q: A company encrypts S3 objects with customer-provided keys (SSE-C) but key management overhead is growing. They want S3 to manage encryption with keys they control in KMS, including per-object data keys for extra protection. Which encryption option meets this requirement?
options: SSE-S3 with Amazon S3 managed keys
Client-side encryption with keys stored in the application
Dual-layer server-side encryption with KMS keys (DSSE-KMS)
Disable encryption and rely on bucket policies
explain: DSSE-KMS applies two layers of encryption using KMS keys the customer controls, removing the per-request key handling of SSE-C. SSE-S3 uses AWS-owned keys, client-side encryption keeps the key management burden, and disabling encryption removes protection entirely.

q: An application in Account A must decrypt data with a KMS key in Account B. The key policy currently allows only Account B principals. What is required to grant Account A role access?
options: Add Account A IAM role to the KMS key policy, because the key policy is the primary authorization for KMS and must permit the external account
Attach an IAM policy in Account A only
Enable automatic key rotation
Create a KMS grant for Account A root user
explain: KMS evaluates the key policy first, and cross-account access requires the key policy to explicitly permit the external principal, so an IAM policy in Account A alone is insufficient. Rotation does not grant access, and grants still require the key policy to allow the external account.

q: A developer in a member account cannot launch EC2 instances even though the IAM user has full EC2 permissions. An SCP attached to the OU denies ec2:RunInstances. Which statement is TRUE?
options: The IAM user policy overrides the SCP
The SCP denial wins, because SCPs set the maximum permissions and an explicit SCP deny cannot be overridden by IAM policies
Moving the user to the management account fixes it
Permission boundaries override SCPs
explain: SCPs define the permission ceiling for an account, and an explicit deny in an SCP blocks the action regardless of IAM allows. IAM policies never override SCPs, the management account is not a workaround, and permission boundaries also only restrict rather than expand.

q: A company uses several gateway VPC endpoints for S3 within one VPC and wants a bucket policy that allows access only from that VPC, regardless of which of the VPC's endpoints a request uses. Which condition key enforces this?
options: aws:SourceVpce with every endpoint ID listed
aws:SourceIp matching the VPC CIDR block
aws:SourceVpc matching the VPC ID, which covers all gateway endpoints in the VPC
s3:x-amz-acl
explain: aws:SourceVpc matches the VPC a request originated from, covering every gateway endpoint in that VPC without enumerating endpoint IDs. aws:SourceVpce requires listing each endpoint, SourceIp cannot reliably identify VPC traffic at the bucket, and s3:x-amz-acl governs canned ACLs on writes rather than request origin.

q: A login API faces credential-stuffing attacks from distributed IPs that rotate frequently, evading simple rate-based rules. Which WAF capability BEST mitigates this?
options: A rate-based rule with a very low threshold
AWS Shield Advanced
The WAF Bot Control managed rule group, which detects automated clients using behavioral signals beyond IP rate
A security group blocking port 443
explain: Bot Control identifies automation through browser fingerprinting and behavioral analysis, catching distributed attacks that IP rate rules miss. Low rate thresholds block legitimate users, Shield Advanced targets DDoS, and blocking port 443 would take the API offline.

q: A security team needs tamper-evident audit logs of all API activity across every account in the organization, stored centrally. Which design meets this requirement?
options: Create an organization CloudTrail trail with log file validation enabled, delivering digest-verified logs to a central S3 bucket
Enable CloudTrail separately in each account with local buckets
Use VPC Flow Logs as the audit source
Enable GuardDuty in each account
explain: An organization trail captures API activity from all accounts centrally, and log file validation with digest files detects tampering. Per-account trails fragment the audit, Flow Logs record network traffic rather than API calls, and GuardDuty detects threats rather than logging API activity.

q: A three-tier application needs its database security group to accept traffic only from the application tier, even as application instances scale in and out with changing IPs. Which rule design provides this?
options: Allow the application subnet CIDR range
Reference the application tier security group ID as the source in the database security group
Allow 0.0.0.0/0 on the database port
Allow the database port in the NACL only
explain: Referencing the source security group ID automatically tracks membership as instances scale. Subnet CIDRs are overly broad, 0.0.0.0/0 exposes the database publicly, and NACLs are stateless subnet filters rather than instance-aware controls.

q: Partner accounts upload files to a central S3 bucket, but the bucket owner cannot manage those partner-uploaded objects, and the bucket must never allow public access. Which configuration enforces both?
options: Enable versioning only
Add a bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject to everyone
Enable access logging
Enable S3 Block Public Access and set Object Ownership to BucketOwnerEnforced
explain: Block Public Access blocks every public ACL and policy path, while BucketOwnerEnforced disables ACLs so the bucket owner owns every object. Versioning does not control access, a public GetObject policy violates the requirement, and access logging is detective rather than preventive.

q: A company consumes a partner API hosted in the partner VPC. Traffic must stay off the public internet in both directions, and the partner must not manage firewall rules for the company dynamic IPs. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Site-to-Site VPN to the partner
VPC peering with the partner VPC
AWS PrivateLink, with the partner exposing an endpoint service and the company creating an interface endpoint in its VPC
Internet gateway with IP allowlisting
explain: PrivateLink provides private, unidirectional connectivity without peering or VPN coordination. VPNs require joint configuration, peering has CIDR constraints and full mesh complexity, and an internet gateway puts traffic on the public internet.

q: An application in Account A must read objects from an S3 bucket in Account B without using long-term credentials. Which combination grants this securely?
options: An IAM role in Account B with a trust policy allowing Account A, assumed via STS for temporary credentials, plus a bucket policy permitting the role
Sharing Account B access keys with the application
Making the bucket public
An IAM user in Account A with S3 permissions
explain: The role trust policy authorizes Account A, STS vends short-lived credentials, and the bucket policy grants the role access, so no long-term keys exist. Shared keys leak, public buckets expose data, and Account A IAM permissions alone cannot reach Account B resources.

q: A GuardDuty finding flags potentially compromised EC2 instances, and the team needs to quickly trace the root cause across VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and DNS logs in one visual timeline. Which service accelerates this investigation?
options: Manually querying CloudWatch Logs Insights
Amazon Detective, which correlates GuardDuty findings with underlying log sources into visual investigation graphs
Amazon Macie
AWS Artifact
explain: Detective automatically builds entity graphs from GuardDuty findings across log sources for fast triage. Manual Log Insights queries are slow to correlate, Macie finds sensitive data, and Artifact hosts compliance reports.
