q: A company must continuously verify that S3 buckets across 40 accounts have encryption and Block Public Access enabled, automatically remediating drift. Which solution provides this at scale?
options: Annual manual audits
Trusted Advisor checks alone
AWS Config aggregator alone
AWS Config conformance packs with managed rules plus automatic remediation through SSM Automation documents
explain: Conformance packs deploy rule bundles across accounts and trigger SSM remediation on noncompliance. Manual audits go stale, Trusted Advisor does not auto-remediate, and an aggregator only centralizes findings.

q: A company migrates SQL Server databases to RDS and requires database administrators to authenticate with their existing Active Directory credentials using single sign-on, with no separate database passwords. Which RDS authentication option provides this?
options: RDS IAM database authentication
Kerberos authentication for RDS integrated with AWS Managed Microsoft AD
Storing database passwords in Secrets Manager with rotation
Enforcing SSL/TLS on database connections
explain: RDS supports Kerberos authentication against AWS Managed Microsoft AD, giving AD users single sign-on to the database with no database passwords. IAM database authentication uses short-lived tokens rather than AD identities, Secrets Manager still relies on passwords, and TLS encrypts connections without authenticating users.

q: A SaaS application must let enterprise customers sign in with their corporate SAML identity provider, without the application managing any passwords. Which Cognito configuration provides this?
options: A Cognito user pool with a SAML identity provider configured for federation
An identity pool alone
IAM users for each customer employee
Storing corporate passwords in the application
explain: User pools federate SAML identity providers so customers authenticate with their own provider while the app manages no passwords. An identity pool alone provides no sign-in directory, per-employee IAM users do not scale, and storing passwords is a severe anti-pattern.

q: A company needs managed VPN-based remote access to its VPC for employees, authenticating against Active Directory with per-connection logging. Which solution provides this?
options: Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Client VPN endpoint with Active Directory authentication and connection logging enabled
Bastion hosts
Direct Connect
explain: Client VPN is the managed OpenVPN-based remote-access service with AD authentication and connection logs. Site-to-Site connects networks rather than users, bastions are SSH jump hosts, and Direct Connect is a dedicated circuit.

q: A stateful application works when its security group allows outbound traffic, but connections fail after the team adds a NACL rule allowing inbound traffic only. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The security group is blocking return traffic
The instance needs a public IP
The route table is missing
NACLs are stateless, so the inbound allow rule is not enough and return traffic on ephemeral ports needs an explicit outbound NACL rule
explain: NACLs evaluate every packet statelessly, so ephemeral-port return traffic requires its own outbound rule. Security groups are stateful and automatically allow return traffic, while public IPs and route tables are unrelated to this symptom.

q: A company needs TLS certificates for internal services that are not reachable from the public internet. Which ACM option issues these certificates?
options: Public ACM certificates
Self-signed certificates uploaded to IAM
ACM Private CA to issue private certificates for internal hosts
CloudFront default certificates
explain: ACM Private CA issues certificates trusted inside the organization for private domains. Public ACM certificates require public domain validation, IAM-uploaded self-signed certificates lack managed trust chains, and CloudFront certificates serve distributions.

q: A security audit found IAM roles with permissions far beyond what they use. The team wants to scope policies down based on actual usage. Which tool identifies the actions each role really used?
options: IAM Access Analyzer unused-access findings and policy generation based on CloudTrail access history
AWS Budgets
GuardDuty findings
Manual review of every CloudTrail event
explain: Access Analyzer flags unused permissions and can generate least-privilege policies from CloudTrail access activity. Budgets track spend, GuardDuty finds threats, and manual review of every event does not scale.

q: A company deploys AWS Managed Microsoft AD to support a lift-and-shift application, but user accounts must remain in the on-premises Active Directory with no password or account sync to AWS. Users need seamless access to resources in both directories. Which configuration provides this?
options: AD Connector pointing at the on-premises AD
A two-way forest trust between AWS Managed Microsoft AD and the on-premises Active Directory
Simple AD with manually duplicated user accounts
IAM Identity Center with local users
explain: A two-way forest trust lets the AWS Managed Microsoft AD forest and the on-premises forest authenticate each other's users with no account synchronization. AD Connector proxies authentication but does not join a managed AD forest to the on-premises forest, Simple AD cannot establish enterprise forest trusts, and Identity Center local users would duplicate identities.

q: A company with 50 AWS accounts needs every web application protected by the same WAF rule set, automatically applied to new accounts. Which solution centrally enforces this?
options: Manually configure WAF in each account
A single SCP
CloudFormation StackSets deploying WAF rules per account
AWS Firewall Manager with a WAF policy applied across the organization and automatic remediation of noncompliant resources
explain: Firewall Manager centrally deploys and continuously enforces WAF, Shield, and security group policies org-wide with auto-remediation. Manual configuration does not scale, SCPs restrict actions rather than deploying WAF, and StackSets deploy resources without continuous compliance enforcement.

q: A data-processing job needs decrypt access to a KMS key for 2 hours during a migration, after which access must disappear automatically. Which mechanism provides this time-bound delegation?
options: Add a permanent key policy statement
Create a new IAM user with the key
Create a KMS grant with appropriate constraints for the job role
Disable key rotation
explain: KMS grants delegate key use temporarily and can be retired when the job ends. Permanent key policy statements do not expire, new IAM users add identity sprawl, and rotation is unrelated to access duration.

q: A company requires MFA for any IAM user performing destructive EC2 actions, even if the user credentials are compromised. Which approach enforces this?
options: An IAM policy condition requiring recent MFA authentication, using temporary credentials from GetSessionToken, on destructive actions
A strong password policy
Rotating access keys weekly
Enabling MFA on the root user only
explain: IAM policies can require recent MFA-authenticated temporary credentials for sensitive actions, so stolen long-term keys alone cannot perform them. Password policies do not add MFA, key rotation does not require MFA, and root MFA does not cover IAM users.

q: A company needs backups in S3 protected from ransomware, including attacks that compromise admin credentials. Objects must be unchangeable for 90 days once written. Which feature provides this?
options: S3 Versioning
S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a 90-day retention period
SSE-KMS encryption
Cross-Region Replication
explain: Object Lock in Compliance mode makes objects immutable for the retention period, even against the root user. Versioning keeps prior versions but they can still be deleted, encryption does not prevent deletion, and replication copies data without locking it.

q: A team deploys container images to ECR and Lambda functions packaged as container images. They need automated scanning for package vulnerabilities before deployment. Which service scans both?
options: GuardDuty
Macie
Security Hub alone
Amazon Inspector, which scans ECR images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities
explain: Inspector assesses ECR container images and Lambda functions for known CVEs. GuardDuty detects runtime threats, Macie finds sensitive data, and Security Hub aggregates findings from other services rather than scanning itself.

q: A bank must use AWS KMS APIs to encrypt EBS volumes and S3 objects, but regulations require the KMS keys to be generated and stored in single-tenant HSMs under the bank's exclusive control rather than in AWS-managed multi-tenant HSMs. Which KMS configuration meets both requirements?
options: KMS with AWS managed keys
A KMS custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster, so applications use standard KMS APIs while key material lives in bank-controlled HSMs
SSE-S3 with Amazon S3 managed keys
Client-side encryption with keys stored in application configuration files
explain: A KMS custom key store backed by CloudHSM lets applications call standard KMS APIs while the key material is generated and stored in single-tenant HSMs the bank exclusively controls. AWS managed keys use multi-tenant AWS HSMs, SSE-S3 uses AWS-owned keys, and configuration-file keys are neither HSM-backed nor centrally manageable.

q: A team runs a cron job on a dedicated EC2 instance that starts and stops dev environments on a schedule. The instance idles most of the day. Which serverless replacement eliminates the idle compute cost?
options: Run the cron on a larger instance to finish faster
Keep the instance but switch it to Spot pricing
Move the cron to an on-premises server
Use EventBridge Scheduler to invoke a Lambda function or Systems Manager Automation on the schedule, paying per invocation
explain: EventBridge Scheduler is serverless with pay-per-invocation pricing, so there is no idle instance to pay for. A larger instance still idles, Spot still runs around the clock, and moving on-premises relocates the cost rather than removing it.

q: A company runs the same m6i instance family 24/7 for the next 3 years in a single Region. Which purchasing option gives the deepest discount for this fixed footprint?
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans with a 3-year all-upfront commitment for that instance family and Region
On-Demand
Spot Instances
1-year Compute Savings Plan with no upfront payment
explain: EC2 Instance Savings Plans with a 3-year all-upfront term give the deepest discount for a fixed family and Region. On-Demand has no discount, Spot does not suit steady-state guarantees, and a 1-year no-upfront Compute plan discounts less.

q: A CI/CD build farm runs fault-tolerant builds and needs the lowest cost while maintaining target capacity across instance types and AZs using Spot. Which fleet configuration fits?
options: On-Demand Auto Scaling group with one instance type
EC2 Fleet with a diversified allocation strategy across instance types, AZs, and Spot pools
Dedicated Hosts
A single Spot instance
explain: A diversified EC2 Fleet spreads across Spot pools so no single interruption breaks target capacity, at the lowest cost. On-Demand costs more, Dedicated Hosts carry a premium, and one Spot instance is a single point of failure.

q: An Application Load Balancer has had no registered targets for months but still incurs hourly charges. Which action stops the charges?
options: Enable deletion protection on the load balancer
Register dummy targets
Delete the unused load balancer
Enable access logging
explain: Load balancers bill per hour regardless of traffic, so deleting the unused ALB stops the charges. Deletion protection prevents deletion, dummy targets add cost, and access logging adds S3 objects.

q: A cost review finds unattached EBS volumes and unassociated Elastic IPs accumulating charges for months. Which approach systematically finds and cleans up this waste?
options: Enable detailed monitoring on all instances
Buy more Reserved Instances
Increase CloudWatch log retention
Use Trusted Advisor cost checks to identify idle resources, then snapshot and delete the unattached volumes and release the unused Elastic IPs
explain: Trusted Advisor flags idle EBS volumes and unassociated Elastic IPs so they can be removed. Detailed monitoring does not find waste, Reserved Instances do not reduce idle-resource spend, and longer log retention increases cost.

q: A fleet of gp2 volumes consistently uses less than 3,000 IOPS. The team wants the same performance for less money. Which change delivers this?
options: Migrate the volumes to gp3, which includes 3,000 baseline IOPS regardless of volume size at a lower price per GB than gp2
Increase every gp2 volume size
Switch to io2 for all volumes
Take more frequent snapshots
explain: gp3 costs less per GB than gp2 and includes 3,000 IOPS baseline, so performance stays the same for less money. Larger gp2 volumes raise cost, io2 is priced for high-IOPS workloads, and snapshots add storage cost.

q: An RDS for MySQL fleet on x86 instances needs lower cost with no application changes. Which option delivers better price-performance?
options: Move to larger x86 instances
Migrate to Graviton-based RDS instance classes
Enable Multi-AZ on every instance
Switch to provisioned IOPS storage
explain: Graviton-based RDS instances offer better price-performance with no code changes. Larger x86 instances raise cost, Multi-AZ doubles instance cost, and provisioned IOPS adds storage cost.

q: A versioned S3 bucket storage keeps growing because noncurrent versions accumulate indefinitely. Which lifecycle configuration controls this cost?
options: Expire current versions after 30 days
Abort incomplete multipart uploads
Expire noncurrent versions after 30 days
Enable S3 access logging
explain: NoncurrentVersionExpiration removes old versions after the set period. Expiring current versions deletes live data, aborting multipart uploads targets a different waste source, and access logging adds objects.

q: CloudWatch Logs storage costs are climbing because log groups retain data indefinitely, though nobody queries logs older than 30 days. Which change cuts this cost?
options: Increase the log retention to 10 years
Enable detailed monitoring
Export logs to CloudWatch Metrics
Set a 30-day retention policy on the log groups, archiving to S3 first if compliance requires longer retention
explain: Retention policies delete log data nobody queries, and S3 archival is far cheaper if compliance demands longer storage. Longer retention raises cost, detailed monitoring adds metrics charges, and logs cannot be exported to metrics.

q: A provisioned Redshift cluster is queried 8 hours a day but billed around the clock. Which approach eliminates compute charges during idle hours?
options: Pause the cluster on a schedule and resume it before business hours
Delete and recreate the cluster daily
Add more nodes
Enable concurrency scaling permanently
explain: Pausing stops compute billing while preserving data, and scheduled resume restores availability. Daily recreation is operationally heavy and slow, more nodes raise cost, and concurrency scaling adds burst capacity rather than idle savings.

q: An Aurora cluster I/O charges exceed its instance charges, and the workload is I/O-heavy with steady high throughput. Which configuration change reduces total cost?
options: Add more reader instances
Switch to Aurora I/O-Optimized, which bundles I/O cost into the instance price and is cheaper for I/O-intensive workloads
Enable Backtrack
Take snapshots more often
explain: I/O-Optimized removes per-request I/O charges, which wins when I/O spending dominates. More readers add instance cost, Backtrack adds storage cost, and frequent snapshots add storage cost.

q: A high-traffic JSON API uses API Gateway REST APIs but needs no usage plans, WAF integration, or request and response transformations. Which change lowers API cost?
options: Add a second REST API
Enable caching on the REST API
Migrate to HTTP APIs, which cost significantly less per million requests for simple proxy workloads
Increase throttling limits
explain: HTTP APIs are priced well below REST APIs for straightforward proxying. More REST APIs add cost, caching adds cost, and throttling limits do not change the per-request price.

q: Multiple teams share one AWS account running ad-hoc Athena queries, and one team unoptimized queries scan huge datasets, spiking the bill. How can costs be controlled per team?
options: Delete the Athena workgroups
Give every user administrator access
Move all data to DynamoDB
Create separate Athena workgroups per team with per-query data usage controls and cost allocation tags
explain: Workgroups enforce bytes-scanned limits per team and tag the spend for accountability. Deleting workgroups removes control, administrator access worsens the problem, and migrating to DynamoDB is a replatform rather than a cost control.

q: A team wants one prioritized view of cost-saving opportunities including idle resources, underutilized instances, and commitment recommendations across all services. Which service consolidates these?
options: Cost Optimization Hub, which aggregates cost recommendations across AWS services
CloudTrail
VPC Flow Logs
AWS Budgets
explain: Cost Optimization Hub centralizes rightsizing, idle-resource, and commitment recommendations. CloudTrail logs API calls, Flow Logs show network traffic, and Budgets track spend against thresholds rather than recommending savings.

q: Engineers have accidentally deleted EBS snapshots and AMIs that were still needed for compliance. The team wants a safety net so deleted snapshots and AMIs remain recoverable for 30 days. Which feature provides this?
options: Moving the snapshots to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier
AWS Backup Vault Lock
Taking snapshots more frequently
Recycle Bin retention rules for EBS snapshots and AMIs, which keep deleted items recoverable until the retention period expires
explain: Recycle Bin holds deleted snapshots and AMIs for a configurable retention period so accidental deletions are recoverable. The Archive tier reduces storage cost rather than preventing deletion loss, Vault Lock makes backups immutable which is a different control, and more frequent snapshots do not recover an already-deleted snapshot.

q: A CloudFront distribution serves a primarily US and European audience, but the default price class uses all edge locations globally, incurring higher costs. Which change aligns cost with the audience?
options: Disable CloudFront and serve from the origin
Increase the TTL to one year
Change to Price Class 100 (US, Canada, and Europe) so other Regions are served from the nearest included edge location
Add more origins
explain: Price Class 100 limits edge usage to the audience Regions while still serving global viewers from the nearest included edge. Disabling CloudFront loses CDN benefits, TTL does not change price class, and more origins add cost.

q: A DynamoDB table has steady, predictable traffic 24/7 and currently uses on-demand mode. Which change reduces cost without affecting performance?
options: Enable DynamoDB Streams
Add a global secondary index
Switch to provisioned capacity mode with auto scaling, and consider reserved capacity for the baseline
Enable point-in-time recovery
explain: Provisioned capacity with auto scaling, plus reserved capacity for the predictable baseline, is far cheaper than on-demand for steady workloads. Streams, GSIs, and point-in-time recovery all add cost rather than reducing it.

q: An ElastiCache for Redis cluster runs steady-state 24/7 and will be needed for at least the next year. Which purchasing option lowers its cost with no architecture changes?
options: ElastiCache reserved nodes with a 1-year commitment
On-Demand nodes
Deleting and recreating the cluster nightly
Moving to larger node types
explain: Reserved nodes discount steady-state ElastiCache usage significantly with no changes. On-Demand has no discount, nightly recreation is operationally heavy and loses cache warmth, and larger nodes raise cost.

q: An application in us-east-1a calls AWS services through an interface VPC endpoint provisioned only in us-east-1b, and the team notices cross-AZ data transfer charges on every API call. Which change eliminates these charges?
options: Route the traffic through a NAT gateway instead
Provision an interface endpoint in each Availability Zone the application uses so traffic stays within its AZ
Add more Availability Zones to the VPC
Use public service endpoints over the internet
explain: Interface endpoints are zonal, so traffic from an instance in one AZ to an endpoint in another AZ incurs cross-AZ data transfer charges; placing an endpoint in each AZ keeps traffic local. A NAT gateway adds its own data processing charges, more AZs multiply cross-AZ paths, and public endpoints expose traffic to the internet.

q: A company cannot tell which of 40 application teams drives its S3 costs. Which approach provides per-team S3 cost visibility?
options: Enable S3 Versioning
Delete old buckets
Tag S3 buckets by team and activate cost allocation tags, supplemented by S3 Storage Lens dashboards for usage trends
Enable MFA Delete
explain: Cost allocation tags attribute spend to each team, and Storage Lens dashboards reveal usage trends behind the charges. Versioning adds cost, deleting buckets blindly risks data loss, and MFA Delete is a security control.

q: Compliance requires retaining audit logs for 7 years. The logs are never accessed after the first 90 days. Which storage class is the lowest cost for this archival requirement?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost storage class for long-term archival
explain: Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 storage for data retained long-term with rare access. S3 Standard and Standard-IA charge far more over 7 years, and Flexible Retrieval costs more than Deep Archive for this access pattern.

q: Dozens of EC2 instances in a development account run around the clock, though developers only work weekdays from 9 to 5. The team wants tag-driven automatic start and stop. Which solution provides this?
options: AWS Instance Scheduler, which starts and stops instances on tag-based schedules
Manually stop instances each evening
Convert all instances to Spot
Enable hibernation permanently
explain: Instance Scheduler automates tag-driven start and stop schedules at fleet scale. Manual stops do not scale, Spot instances still run around the clock, and hibernation preserves memory state rather than scheduling stops.

q: A Lambda-based workload bill is dominated by duration charges. The functions are compatible with ARM. Which change cuts compute cost without code changes?
options: Increase memory to the maximum
Switch the functions to Graviton2 (arm64) architecture, which offers a lower price per millisecond
Enable provisioned concurrency for all functions
Raise the timeout
explain: The arm64 Lambda architecture is priced lower per GB-second with comparable performance and needs no code changes. Maximum memory raises cost, provisioned concurrency adds idle capacity cost, and timeout does not change the unit price.

q: An analytics team queries Redshift for 2 hours each morning while the provisioned cluster idles the other 22 hours. Which option eliminates idle compute cost?
options: Add more nodes for faster queries
Enable concurrency scaling permanently
Take manual snapshots nightly
Migrate to Amazon Redshift Serverless, which scales compute to zero when idle and charges per query
explain: Redshift Serverless pauses compute when idle and charges only for queries actually run. More nodes raise cost, concurrency scaling adds burst capacity rather than idle savings, and snapshots do not reduce compute charges.

q: An application's CloudWatch bill is dominated by custom metrics published from the CloudWatch agent on every EC2 instance at 1-second resolution, though dashboards and alarms only need minute-level data. Which change cuts the metric cost?
options: Publish the custom metrics at standard 60-second resolution instead of high resolution, since high-resolution metrics are billed at a higher rate per metric
Enable detailed monitoring on the instances
Create additional CloudWatch dashboards
Lengthen the alarm evaluation periods
explain: High-resolution (1-second) custom metrics cost more per metric than standard-resolution metrics, so dropping to 60-second resolution cuts the bill when sub-minute granularity is not needed. Detailed monitoring covers EC2 hypervisor metrics rather than custom metrics, dashboards do not change metric pricing, and longer alarm periods do not change the resolution cost.

q: A company is migrating a 4 TB on-premises Oracle database to RDS with minimal downtime. The migration must keep replicating ongoing changes after the initial full load until cutover. AWS SCT converted the schema, but the team is unsure which service handles the data movement. Which approach meets the requirement?
options: Use AWS DMS with ongoing replication (CDC) to capture changes after the full load until cutover
Use AWS DataSync to sync the database files to S3 and import them into RDS
Copy the data with S3 multipart upload and restore it into RDS
Use AWS Backup to copy the on-premises database directly into RDS
explain: DMS performs full load plus ongoing change data capture, keeping source and target in sync until cutover for near-zero-downtime migrations. SCT only converts schema and code, it moves no data. DataSync moves files, not live database transactions; S3 multipart upload handles objects, not CDC; AWS Backup cannot ingest on-premises databases.

q: After a ransomware incident at a peer company, a CTO requires that database backups survive even if an attacker gains administrative credentials. Backups must be immutable for 90 days so no one, including admins, can delete or shorten retention during that window. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Store backups in an S3 bucket with versioning enabled
Use AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode with a 90-day minimum retention
Copy snapshots to a second AWS account owned by the same team
Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket holding the backups
explain: Vault Lock compliance mode makes the vault immutable: no one, including the root user, can delete recovery points or shorten retention before expiry. S3 versioning alone still allows privileged deletion of versions; a second account under the same admins offers no protection from compromised admin credentials; MFA Delete protects only versioned S3 objects and does not cover AWS Backup vaults.

q: A clustered database runs across four EC2 instances in one Availability Zone and needs shared block storage so any node can read and write the same volume concurrently. The team proposes EBS Multi-Attach. Which constraint must their design respect?
options: Multi-Attach works with any EBS volume type across multiple Availability Zones
Multi-Attach requires Provisioned IOPS volumes attached to Nitro-based instances in the same AZ, plus a cluster-aware file system
Multi-Attach provides automatic data replication between the attached instances
Multi-Attach volumes can be attached to instances in different Regions for disaster recovery
explain: EBS Multi-Attach supports only io1/io2 volumes, up to 16 Nitro-based instances, all in the same AZ as the volume, and the application must use a cluster-aware file system since EBS provides no write coordination. It does not work with gp3, does not span AZs or Regions, and provides no replication or locking on its own.

q: An Auto Scaling group runs an application whose instances need 12 minutes of software installation and cache warming before they can serve traffic. During traffic spikes, new instances take too long to become useful and the spike overwhelms the fleet. Which feature shortens the time to serve traffic during scale-out?
options: Enable predictive scaling on the Auto Scaling group
Increase the maximum instance lifetime to keep old instances longer
Use larger instance types so fewer instances are needed
Configure a warm pool of pre-initialized stopped instances that join the group during scale-out
explain: Warm pools keep stopped, pre-initialized instances ready so scale-out skips the 12-minute install and warm-up, putting capacity into service fast. Predictive scaling forecasts demand but new instances still boot slowly; longer max lifetime does not speed up launches; larger instances still pay the same initialization time per instance.

q: A trading platform runs Aurora MySQL in us-east-1 and needs a secondary Region that can take over writes within a minute with minimal data loss if the primary Region fails. A cross-Region read replica shows several seconds of replication lag. Which solution best meets the RPO and RTO targets?
options: Use an Aurora Global Database, which replicates with typical sub-second lag, RPO of 1 second, and managed failover under a minute
Enable Aurora Backtrack on the primary cluster
Add more cross-Region read replicas to reduce lag
Use S3 cross-Region replication of automated snapshots
explain: Aurora Global Database uses storage-layer replication with typical lag under a second, designed for 1-second RPO and sub-minute RTO with managed failover. Backtrack rewinds within one cluster and is not cross-Region; adding read replicas does not reduce async lag; snapshot replication is far too slow and coarse for a 1-minute RTO.

q: A company uses Route 53 failover routing to a disaster-recovery site. The health check must consider the state of application servers that have no public IPs and sit in private subnets. Which health check design works?
options: Create a Route 53 health check against the private IP addresses directly
Publish a CloudWatch alarm reflecting application health and base the Route 53 health check on that alarm
Use a geoproximity routing policy instead of failover routing
Point the health check at the NAT gateway's public IP
explain: Route 53 health checkers are on the public internet and cannot reach private IPs, so the standard pattern is a CloudWatch alarm (fed by internal monitoring) that the Route 53 health check evaluates. Private IPs are unreachable to the checkers; geoproximity changes routing logic rather than enabling private health checks; a NAT gateway IP reflects gateway health, not the application.

q: A media site serves images from an S3 origin through CloudFront. During an S3 outage in the origin Region, the site must automatically serve images from a backup origin without DNS changes. Which CloudFront feature provides this?
options: CloudFront signed URLs to redirect clients to the backup origin
Lambda@Edge to rewrite the origin domain on each request
Configure an origin group with the primary S3 origin and a failover origin so CloudFront fails over automatically
Enable CloudFront origin shield in a second Region
explain: Origin groups define a primary and secondary origin; CloudFront automatically fails over when the primary returns configured error status codes, with no DNS change. Signed URLs control access, not failover; Lambda@Edge rewrites add latency and complexity versus the native feature; Origin Shield is an extra caching layer that still depends on the same origin.

q: An application caches database query results in ElastiCache. The team wants the cache to populate only with data the application actually requests, accepting that the first request for an item will be a cache miss. Which caching strategy matches this behavior?
options: Write-through, because it writes to the cache on every database update
Write-behind, because it asynchronously updates the cache after writes
Refresh-ahead, because it proactively reloads items before expiry
Lazy loading, because the application checks the cache first and loads missed items from the database into the cache
explain: Lazy loading populates the cache on demand: check cache, on miss read the database and write the result to the cache. Write-through and write-behind update the cache on writes rather than reads; refresh-ahead preloads before expiry. The described read-driven, miss-tolerant behavior is exactly lazy loading.

q: A gaming leaderboard backed by DynamoDB sees read latency spikes during tournaments. The data changes frequently, so the team cannot use long TTLs, but they need microsecond read performance for repeated queries of the same items. Which solution fits?
options: Place DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table for microsecond in-memory caching
Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
Export the table to S3 and query it with Athena
Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode
explain: DAX is a write-through in-memory cache for DynamoDB delivering microsecond reads without application changes. Point-in-time recovery aids restore, not latency; Athena over S3 exports adds minutes of staleness; on-demand capacity changes throughput billing, not per-request latency.

q: A data pipeline uploads 50 GB video files to S3 over a high-bandwidth link, but single PUT uploads are slow and any network interruption restarts the whole upload. Which approach improves throughput and resumability?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and keep single PUT uploads
Use S3 multipart upload so parts transfer in parallel and failed parts can be retried independently
Compress the files with gzip before a single PUT
Upload through a NAT gateway instead of a VPC endpoint
explain: Multipart upload splits the object into parts uploaded in parallel for higher throughput, and only failed parts need retrying. Transfer Acceleration speeds the network path but does not parallelize or allow resume; compression helps size, not parallelism; a NAT gateway adds a bottleneck versus a direct S3 path.

q: A database workload on gp2 volumes needs 8,000 provisioned IOPS but not the high throughput or cost of io2. The team wants to keep general-purpose SSD pricing while setting IOPS independently of volume size. Which volume type meets this need?
options: Migrate to io2 Block Express volumes for the provisioned IOPS
Increase the gp2 volume size until its baseline IOPS reach 8,000
Use gp3 volumes and provision 8,000 IOPS independently of volume size
Use Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volumes for the IOPS requirement
explain: gp3 decouples performance from capacity: provision up to 16,000 IOPS and throughput independently at a lower price than gp2. io2 Block Express is far more expensive than needed; growing gp2 to earn baseline IOPS wastes capacity and money; st1 is a throughput HDD unsuitable for an 8,000 IOPS random workload.

q: An HPC fluid-dynamics simulation runs across 40 EC2 instances that exchange large messages constantly. Network latency between instances dominates runtime. Which placement strategy minimizes inter-instance latency?
options: Spread placement group to isolate each instance on distinct hardware
Partition placement group to group instances by workload partition
Use the default placement with instances across three Availability Zones
Cluster placement group packing the instances into a single Availability Zone for low-latency 10 Gbps networking
explain: A cluster placement group packs instances close together in one AZ for single-digit-microsecond latency and full-bisection 10 Gbps bandwidth. Spread maximizes hardware isolation at the cost of latency; partition targets fault isolation for big-data workloads; spanning AZs adds inter-AZ latency that hurts tightly coupled HPC.

q: A Java-based Lambda function behind API Gateway suffers 8-second cold starts on the first invocation after each deploy, breaching the API's latency SLO. The team wants faster cold starts without paying for always-warm capacity. Which feature addresses this?
options: Enable Lambda SnapStart to restore the function from a pre-initialized snapshot
Configure provisioned concurrency at zero and rely on burst scaling
Increase the function memory to 10 GB to speed initialization
Move the function into a VPC to reduce cold start time
explain: SnapStart takes a snapshot of the initialized execution environment (supported runtimes like Java) and restores it at invoke time, cutting cold starts dramatically with no always-warm cost. Provisioned concurrency at zero is just on-demand; more memory helps marginally but does not fix 8-second JVM init; VPC attachment historically worsens cold starts rather than improving them.

q: An application in private subnets reads from S3 and DynamoDB. Traffic currently routes through a NAT gateway, incurring data-processing charges and traversing public infrastructure. The team wants private, low-cost connectivity to both services. Which design is best?
options: Create interface VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB with PrivateLink
Use gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, which are free and keep traffic on the AWS network
Peer the VPC with the S3 service VPC
Assign Elastic IPs to the instances and access S3 over the internet
explain: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free, add no hourly charge, and keep traffic off the internet and off the NAT gateway. Interface endpoints also work but incur hourly plus per-GB charges unnecessarily; VPC peering to AWS services is not possible; Elastic IPs route over the public internet, defeating the goal.

q: A company replicates KMS-encrypted EBS snapshots to a second Region for disaster recovery, but the replica snapshots cannot be decrypted there because the KMS key exists only in the primary Region. Which key design solves this while keeping one logical key?
options: Export the key material and import it into a second single-Region key
Disable encryption on the snapshots before replicating them
Use a KMS multi-Region key so the same key material exists in both Regions under one key ID
Share the primary Region key with the second Region through RAM
explain: Multi-Region keys replicate the same key material across Regions under a shared key ID, so replicas encrypted in one Region decrypt in the other. Imported key material creates a separate key ID requiring manual coordination; disabling encryption violates the security requirement; KMS keys cannot be shared across Regions with RAM.

q: A partner integration calls an internal API behind an ALB. The security team requires each caller to present a client certificate so the load balancer itself verifies caller identity before traffic reaches the targets. Which ALB feature provides this?
options: Security group rules that filter by client certificate thumbprint
WAF managed rules for certificate validation
IAM resource policies attached to the ALB
Mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication on the ALB listener to validate client certificates
explain: ALB supports mutual TLS: the listener validates client certificates against a trust store during the TLS handshake before routing. Security groups filter IPs, not certificates; WAF inspects HTTP content, not TLS client auth; IAM policies authorize AWS API calls, not application clients at the load balancer.

q: A login endpoint faces credential-stuffing attacks from botnets that rotate through thousands of IPs, each staying under simple per-IP thresholds. The team needs to block IPs exceeding 2,000 requests per 5 minutes specifically on the /login path. Which WAF configuration fits?
options: A rate-based rule scoped to the /login path with a 2,000-request limit per 5-minute window
A geo-match rule blocking the countries the attacks originate from
AWS Shield Standard on the CloudFront distribution
A WAF IP set listing the attacker IPs permanently
explain: Rate-based rules count requests per IP over a 5-minute window and can be scoped to a path like /login, automatically blocking abusive IPs. Geo-match blocks whole countries, harming legitimate users; Shield Standard covers L3/L4 DDoS, not application-layer login abuse; static IP sets cannot keep up with rotating botnet IPs.

q: A company with 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations must guarantee that no account can disable CloudTrail or delete flow logs, even if an account administrator tries. Which control enforces this organization-wide?
options: An IAM permissions boundary on every administrator role
A service control policy (SCP) that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging and log-deletion actions for all accounts
AWS Config rules that alert when CloudTrail is disabled
Enabling CloudTrail in each account with separate trails
explain: SCPs set maximum permissions for an organization and apply even to account administrators, so a deny on CloudTrail and log-deletion actions cannot be overridden within member accounts. Permissions boundaries limit individual roles but an admin could create new roles; Config rules only detect after the fact; per-account trails are still stoppable by each account's admin.

q: An application stores database credentials in Systems Manager Parameter Store as SecureString parameters, but auditors require automatic password rotation every 30 days with no application code changes. Which service meets the requirement with the least effort?
options: Keep Parameter Store and write a custom rotation script on EC2
Move the credentials to AWS Secrets Manager and enable automatic rotation on a 30-day schedule
Store the credentials in an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption
Embed the credentials in the application AMI and rebuild the AMI monthly
explain: Secrets Manager natively supports scheduled automatic rotation via Lambda rotation functions, including built-in templates for RDS, with no application changes beyond reading the secret. Parameter Store SecureString has no native rotation; S3 storage adds manual rotation burden; baking credentials into AMIs is operationally heavy and insecure.

q: A data lake bucket holds 200 TB with access patterns that vary unpredictably: some objects are hot for weeks, others go cold immediately, and the team cannot predict which. Retrieval fees must stay at zero and objects must move between access tiers automatically. Which storage class fits?
options: S3 Standard with a lifecycle rule transitioning objects to Glacier after 30 days
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access for all objects
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access with manual tier transitions
S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which monitors access and moves objects between tiers automatically with no retrieval fees
explain: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent, infrequent, archive, and deep-archive tiers based on observed access, with no retrieval fees and no lifecycle rules to maintain. Fixed 30-day Glacier transitions penalize objects that go hot again with retrieval fees; One Zone-IA risks durability and still charges retrievals; S3 Standard-IA requires manual transitions and charges per retrieval.

q: A VPC's NAT gateway bill shows most of the charge is per-GB data processing from EC2 instances pulling large datasets from S3. The instances have no other internet needs. Which change eliminates the NAT data-processing charge for this traffic?
options: Add a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 so instance-to-S3 traffic bypasses the NAT gateway entirely
Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
Move the instances to public subnets with Elastic IPs
explain: A gateway endpoint routes S3 traffic privately with no hourly or per-GB charge, removing the NAT gateway data-processing fee for that traffic. NAT instances still incur EC2 and data costs; Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over the internet but does not avoid NAT; public subnets expose instances directly and still traverse the internet gateway.

q: An EC2 fleet runs at 15% average CPU and the finance team suspects over-provisioning, but no one knows which instance types the workloads actually need. Which service provides data-driven rightsizing recommendations?
options: AWS Cost Explorer with manual instance-type comparisons
AWS Compute Optimizer, which analyzes CloudWatch metrics and recommends optimal instance types
AWS Budgets with alerts at 80% of forecasted spend
AWS Trusted Advisor's service-limits check
explain: Compute Optimizer uses machine learning on CloudWatch utilization history to recommend rightsized EC2 instance types, including Graviton options. Cost Explorer shows spend but does not recommend types; Budgets alerts on spend without diagnosing cause; the Trusted Advisor service-limits check is unrelated to rightsizing.

q: An Aurora MySQL cluster serving an analytics workload has unpredictable I/O spikes, and the I/O portion of the bill now exceeds compute costs. The team wants predictable database costs without throttling I/O. Which configuration addresses this?
options: Switch to Aurora Serverless v1 to pay per second of compute
Add cross-Region read replicas to spread the I/O load
Enable Aurora I/O-Optimized cluster storage configuration to eliminate per-request I/O charges
Reduce the backup retention period to lower I/O
explain: Aurora I/O-Optimized removes per-million-request I/O charges in favor of higher compute/storage rates, making costs predictable for I/O-heavy workloads. Serverless v1 still bills I/O; read replicas add cost and do not change the primary's I/O billing; backup retention affects storage, not I/O request charges.

q: A fleet of gp2 volumes needs more IOPS during month-end processing but sits idle the rest of the month. Resizing gp2 volumes upward permanently would waste money. Which change gives provisioned IOPS only when needed at the lowest cost?
options: Convert the volumes to io2 with provisioned IOPS permanently
Take snapshots and restore larger gp2 volumes each month-end
Enable EBS Elastic Volumes to grow gp2 sizes temporarily
Migrate the volumes to gp3 and provision IOPS independently, scaling IOPS up for month-end and down after
explain: gp3 lets IOPS be provisioned independently from 3,000 to 16,000 and adjusted at any time, so the team pays for high IOPS only during month-end at gp3's lower base price. io2 is permanently expensive; snapshot restore cycles cause downtime; Elastic Volumes can grow gp2 but cannot shrink it back, leaving the higher cost in place.

q: A compliance archive is stored in S3 Glacier Deep Archive. Finance notices early-deletion fees on objects removed after 100 days. Which rule explains the charge?
options: Glacier Deep Archive bills a minimum 180-day storage duration, so deletions before 180 days incur a prorated charge for the remainder
Deep Archive charges a per-request fee higher than the storage fee
Objects under 128 KB are billed at the full 180 days regardless
Lifecycle transitions to Deep Archive carry a per-object transition fee exceeding storage costs
explain: S3 Glacier Deep Archive has a 180-day minimum storage duration; deleting earlier triggers a prorated charge for the remaining days. Per-request fees are small relative to storage; the 128 KB minimum applies to S3 Standard-IA and One Zone-IA, not Deep Archive; transition fees are one-time per object and do not explain deletion charges.

q: A financial firm replicates trade records to a second Region with S3 cross-Region replication. Compliance requires 99.99% of objects to replicate within 15 minutes, backed by an SLA with visibility into replication status. Standard replication cannot guarantee this. Which option meets the requirement?
options: Enable S3 Versioning on both buckets to speed up replication
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket
Enable S3 Replication Time Control (RTC), which provides a 15-minute SLA backed by CloudWatch metrics
Copy objects with S3 Batch Operations on a 15-minute schedule
explain: Replication Time Control replicates 99.99% of objects within 15 minutes with an SLA and exposes replication metrics and event notifications. Versioning is a prerequisite, not a speed guarantee; Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads to S3, not replication between buckets; Batch Operations on a schedule cannot provide continuous SLA-backed replication.

q: A company stores shared project files on EFS in us-east-1. A Regional outage would halt work for a globally distributed team, and they need a continuously updated copy in eu-west-1 with minimal RPO. Which EFS feature provides this?
options: EFS lifecycle management to move files to Infrequent Access
EFS access points to isolate each team's files
EFS throughput bursting to handle replication traffic
EFS replication, which continuously replicates the file system to a destination Region
explain: EFS replication creates and continuously updates a replica file system in another Region (or same-Region AZ) with RPO measured in minutes. Lifecycle management only changes storage classes; access points manage permissions, not replication; throughput bursting affects performance, not disaster recovery.

q: A team must roll out a new AMI across an Auto Scaling group of 60 instances without dropping below 80% healthy capacity, and they want the ability to pause the rollout between batches to run smoke tests. Which approach provides controlled, pausable rolling updates?
options: Use an instance refresh with a minimum healthy percentage of 80 and checkpoints that pause between batches
Terminate all instances at once and let the group relaunch them
Detach every instance, update them manually, and reattach them
Set the group's desired capacity to zero and then back to 60
explain: Instance refresh replaces instances in rolling batches honoring the minimum healthy percentage, and checkpoints pause the refresh for validation between phases. Terminating all at once causes full outage; manual detach/update is error-prone and slow; scaling to zero and back is also a full outage.

q: A Lambda function processes S3 events asynchronously. When processing fails after all retries, the team needs the failed event payload routed to an SQS queue for analysis and to a second Lambda for alerting, with successful invocations also recorded. Which feature handles both outcomes natively?
options: Configure a Lambda dead-letter queue, which handles both success and failure destinations
Configure Lambda destinations on the function for both OnSuccess and OnFailure asynchronous results
Increase the function's retry attempts to a very high number
Poll CloudWatch Logs for errors and forward them manually
explain: Lambda destinations route asynchronous invocation records to SQS, SNS, Lambda, or EventBridge separately for success and failure, which DLQs cannot do since they only capture failed events. Raising retries delays but does not route failures; manual log polling is fragile and misses payload context.

q: An application writes to a DynamoDB global table from both us-east-1 and eu-west-1. During a network partition, the same item is updated in both Regions with different values. How does DynamoDB resolve the conflict when connectivity returns?
options: Both versions are kept and the application must merge them manually
The write from the primary Region always wins over the secondary Region
Last-writer-wins reconciliation: the item version with the latest timestamp prevails
The conflicting writes are rolled back and retried by the client
explain: DynamoDB global tables use last-writer-wins conflict resolution based on timestamps, so the most recent write prevails without application intervention. There is no versioning kept for manual merge, no primary/secondary hierarchy in global tables, and no automatic rollback of conflicting writes.

q: A company runs mission-critical replication over a single Direct Connect connection. They need automatic failover to a backup path without manual intervention if the connection or its location fails. Which design provides resilient hybrid connectivity?
options: Add a second virtual interface on the same Direct Connect connection
Order a second connection at the same Direct Connect location on the same router
Replace Direct Connect with a single Site-to-Site VPN connection
Provision a second Direct Connect connection at a different location, or run a Site-to-Site VPN as a BGP-advertised backup path
explain: Resilience requires independent failure domains: a second connection at a different location, or a VPN backup with BGP so routes fail over automatically. A second VIF shares the same physical connection; a second connection at the same location on the same router shares location and device risk; a lone VPN is less consistent than DX and adds no redundancy by itself.

q: An Aurora MySQL cluster's read traffic spikes unpredictably during business hours and drops at night. Manually adding and removing read replicas is too slow and the team over-provisions for the peak. Which feature matches read capacity to demand automatically?
options: Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for read replicas to add or remove replicas based on CPU or connection metrics
Enable Aurora Backtrack to handle traffic spikes
Switch the cluster to provisioned IOPS storage
Place an RDS Proxy in front of the writer to absorb reads
explain: Aurora Auto Scaling adjusts the read-replica count on a schedule or metric thresholds, matching capacity to demand. Backtrack rewinds data, not scaling; provisioned IOPS addresses storage performance, not read-replica count; RDS Proxy pools connections but does not add read capacity.

q: Five independent analytics consumers read from the same Kinesis data stream, but each consumer only gets a fraction of the shard's 2 MB/s throughput because they share it, causing lag. Which feature gives every consumer full per-shard throughput?
options: Increase the number of shards to give each consumer its own shard
Register each consumer for enhanced fan-out, giving it a dedicated 2 MB/s per-shard throughput pipe
Enable server-side encryption on the stream to speed up reads
Switch the producers to Kinesis Data Firehose
explain: Enhanced fan-out provides each registered consumer a dedicated 2 MB/s per shard via HTTP/2 push, eliminating the shared-throughput contention of standard polling. Adding shards increases cost and resharding complexity; encryption does not affect throughput; Firehose is a delivery service, not a multi-consumer stream reader.

q: A DynamoDB table uses 'status' (only three possible values) as its partition key. Despite ample provisioned capacity, writes throttle during peak load and CloudWatch shows one partition consuming most throughput. Which design change resolves the hot partition?
options: Double the provisioned write capacity units on the table
Switch the table to on-demand capacity mode
Redesign the partition key to a high-cardinality attribute such as order ID so writes spread evenly across partitions
Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery to reduce partition load
explain: A low-cardinality partition key concentrates writes on a few partitions, and each partition has a fixed throughput ceiling (~1,000 WCU) that more provisioned capacity cannot raise. A high-cardinality key distributes writes evenly. Doubling WCUs or switching to on-demand does not lift the per-partition limit; point-in-time recovery aids restore, not throughput distribution.

q: A CloudFront distribution needs to add security headers and normalize URLs at the edge for every request. The logic is a few lines of JavaScript and must run with minimal latency and cost at 200 million requests per month. Which edge compute option fits best?
options: Lambda@Edge with functions in every Region for lowest latency
An EC2 fleet behind the origin to process headers centrally
AWS WAF rules to inject the security headers
CloudFront Functions, which run lightweight JavaScript at the edge with sub-millisecond startup at lower cost than Lambda@Edge
explain: CloudFront Functions are designed for simple, high-volume edge manipulations with sub-millisecond startup and pricing far below Lambda@Edge. Lambda@Edge suits heavier compute needing network access but costs more per request; EC2 centralizes what should happen at the edge; WAF inspects requests but does not inject response headers.

q: A genomics pipeline needs a high-throughput scratch file system that can process data stored in S3 and return results to S3, with sub-millisecond latencies and hundreds of GB/s of throughput for a short-lived job. Which storage service fits?
options: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket for parallel high-throughput scratch processing
Use EFS with Max I/O throughput mode for the scratch data
Use EBS gp3 volumes on a single instance for the whole pipeline
Use S3 Standard directly as the scratch file system
explain: FSx for Lustre integrates natively with S3 as a durable store and delivers hundreds of GB/s and sub-millisecond latency for parallel HPC scratch workloads. EFS Max I/O tops out far below Lustre throughput; a single instance's gp3 volumes cannot parallelize across the cluster; S3 is object storage without POSIX semantics or Lustre-class throughput.

q: An SAP HANA database on EC2 needs 200,000 provisioned IOPS with 64 TB volumes and cannot tolerate the IOPS-per-volume limits of standard io2. Which EBS volume type supports this requirement?
options: gp3 with 16,000 provisioned IOPS per volume
io2 Block Express, which supports up to 256,000 IOPS and 64 TB per volume
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) striped across instances
EBS Multi-Attach gp3 volumes for aggregated IOPS
explain: io2 Block Express scales to 256,000 IOPS, 4,000 MB/s throughput, and 64 TB per volume for the most demanding databases like SAP HANA. gp3 caps at 16,000 IOPS; st1 is a throughput HDD unsuitable for high random IOPS; Multi-Attach shares one volume rather than raising its IOPS ceiling.

q: A Redshift cluster's storage keeps growing and the team must resize the cluster just to add disk, paying for idle compute. They want storage to scale independently of compute nodes. Which Redshift architecture provides this?
options: Redshift Serverless with manual workgroup sizing
Dense Compute (DC2) node types with larger local disks
RA3 node types with Redshift managed storage that decouples compute from S3-backed storage
Concatenating multiple classic clusters behind a load balancer
explain: RA3 nodes use Redshift managed storage on S3, so storage scales independently and compute can be resized or paused without data movement. Serverless abstracts sizing but does not change the storage model question; DC2 ties storage to the node; multiple clusters add complexity without solving the coupling.

q: Regulators require that certain S3 objects be retained for 7 years and that NO ONE, including the root user, can delete or shorten retention during that period. Other objects need retention that administrators can lift in exceptional cases. Which Object Lock modes map to these needs?
options: Governance mode for both, with legal holds on the regulated objects
Compliance mode for the regulated objects (no deletion by anyone) and governance mode for the rest (admins with permission can override)
Versioning with MFA Delete for all objects
S3 Glacier Vault Lock for both object sets
explain: Compliance mode blocks deletion or retention changes by everyone including root until expiry, while governance mode lets users with special permission bypass retention. Governance alone cannot stop a root user; MFA Delete protects versions, not retention; Glacier Vault Lock applies to vaults, not S3 object-level retention.

q: A platform team lets product teams create their own IAM roles, but no role they create may ever grant access to the billing bucket or production KMS keys, regardless of the policies attached. Which IAM mechanism enforces this ceiling on every role the teams create?
options: Attach a permissions boundary to the teams' role-creation path so no created role can exceed it
Write an SCP that denies the billing bucket for the whole organization
Require MFA for all role assumptions
Put all team roles in a single IAM group with a restrictive policy
explain: Permissions boundaries set the maximum permissions for IAM roles, so delegated administrators cannot create roles exceeding the boundary even with permissive identity policies. An SCP is organization-level rather than scoped to the delegation path; MFA adds authentication, not a permission ceiling; group policies do not cap what policies can be attached to roles.

q: A security team needs a single CloudTrail trail that automatically captures management events in every current and future account in the organization, stored in one central S3 bucket. Which configuration delivers this?
options: Create a separate trail in each account pointing to the central bucket
Create an organization trail in the management account, which applies to all member accounts including new ones
Enable CloudTrail Insights in each account
Use AWS Config to record API calls across the organization
explain: An organization trail created in the management (or delegated admin) account automatically logs events for all current and future member accounts into one bucket. Per-account trails require manual setup for every new account; Insights detects anomalies rather than centralizing logs; Config records resource configuration changes, not the full API audit trail.

q: After a GuardDuty finding flags suspicious EC2 behavior, analysts need to investigate the attack timeline: which users, roles, and API calls were involved across accounts. Which service is purpose-built for this security investigation?
options: Amazon Inspector, to scan the instance for software vulnerabilities
AWS Security Hub, to aggregate the finding with others
Amazon Detective, which builds interactive visualizations of users, roles, and API activity over time
AWS Artifact, to download compliance reports about the incident
explain: Detective ingests CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, and GuardDuty findings to build time-ordered graphs of entities and activity for root-cause investigation. Inspector finds vulnerabilities rather than investigating incidents; Security Hub aggregates findings without the investigation timeline; Artifact provides compliance documents, not incident analysis.

q: Application servers in an Auto Scaling group must accept traffic only from the ALB, whose IP addresses change constantly. Hard-coding CIDR ranges in the instance security group keeps breaking. Which security group design stays correct automatically?
options: Open the instance security group to 0.0.0.0/0 on the application port
Reference the ALB's security group ID as the source in the instance security group rule
Put the ALB and instances in the same security group
Use a network ACL with the ALB's current IP addresses
explain: Referencing a security group ID as the rule source allows traffic from any current member of that group, tracking ALB changes automatically. Opening to the world removes the restriction; sharing one security group grants broader access than intended; NACLs are stateless and cannot reference security groups.

q: Microservices inside a VPC need TLS certificates for mutual authentication between services, but the services are internal-only and must not use public certificates. Which AWS service issues private certificates for this internal PKI?
options: AWS Private CA, which creates a private certificate authority for issuing internal certificates
AWS Certificate Manager public certificates attached to the services
IAM server certificates uploaded for each microservice
Self-signed certificates generated on each instance with no central authority
explain: AWS Private CA provides a managed private CA hierarchy for issuing and revoking internal TLS certificates. ACM public certificates are for public-facing endpoints and cannot serve as an internal CA; IAM server certificates are legacy and unmanaged; self-signed certificates per instance create trust and rotation chaos.

q: A team writes a lifecycle rule to transition S3 objects to S3 Standard-IA after 7 days to save money, but the rule never fires for young objects. Which S3 lifecycle constraint explains this?
options: Lifecycle rules only run once per month regardless of configuration
Objects must be stored at least 30 days before they can transition to Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, or Glacier storage classes
Transitions to Infrequent Access require objects larger than 1 GB
Lifecycle rules cannot target objects with versioning enabled
explain: S3 requires a minimum of 30 days of storage before transitioning objects to Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, or Glacier classes, so a 7-day transition is invalid. Lifecycle rules evaluate daily; there is a 128 KB minimum billable size for IA classes, not 1 GB; versioned objects transition normally.

q: A batch workload runs on Spot Instances but suffers frequent interruptions because it launches into a single instance pool. Which Spot best practice most reduces interruptions?
options: Use the lowest-price allocation strategy across all pools
Request Spot Instances in only one Availability Zone to keep networking simple
Use the capacity-optimized allocation strategy diversified across many instance types and Availability Zones
Set the maximum Spot price far above On-Demand to prevent interruptions
explain: The capacity-optimized strategy launches into the pools with the most available capacity, and diversifying across instance types and AZs avoids single-pool exhaustion, the main cause of interruptions. Lowest-price packs into the cheapest (often thinnest) pools; single-AZ concentrates risk; max price does not prevent capacity-driven interruptions.

q: Development RDS instances sit idle nights and weekends but run 24/7 because no one remembers to stop them. Which built-in RDS capability cuts this waste with the least operational effort?
options: Enable Multi-AZ so idle instances consume fewer resources
Take daily snapshots and delete the instances each night
Convert the instances to Aurora Serverless v1 with auto-pause
Stop the instances when idle; RDS supports stopping and starting DB instances, restarting automatically after 7 days if forgotten
explain: RDS stop/start halts billing for compute (storage still billed) and instances auto-start after 7 days as a safety net, requiring no scripts. Multi-AZ doubles cost rather than cutting it; snapshot-delete-restore nightly is operationally heavy; Aurora Serverless v1 auto-pause exists but requires engine migration.

q: A DynamoDB table stores user sessions that expire after 24 hours. A nightly job scans and deletes expired items, consuming thousands of write capacity units. Which feature deletes expired items without consuming provisioned throughput?
options: Enable DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) so expired items are deleted automatically at no write cost
Switch the table to on-demand mode for the nightly delete window
Enable DynamoDB Streams to capture the expired items
Export expired items to S3 before deleting them
explain: DynamoDB TTL automatically deletes items past their expiry timestamp in the background with no write-capacity consumption and no charge. On-demand still bills for delete writes; Streams capture changes but do not delete; exporting to S3 adds cost without removing the delete workload.

q: A migration must apply a retention tag to 400 million existing S3 objects. Calling PutObjectTagging per object would cost a fortune in request fees and take weeks. Which approach applies the tag efficiently?
options: Enable S3 Versioning and tag each version individually
Use S3 Batch Operations with a tag job to apply the tag across all objects in one managed job
Use S3 Select to filter objects before tagging them
Copy each object onto itself with the new tag
explain: S3 Batch Operations runs a single managed job over billions of objects with one job fee plus per-object operation pricing far below individual API request costs. Versioning multiplies the work; S3 Select queries content but cannot tag; self-copy still issues 400 million COPY requests.

q: A company runs steady-state EC2 across many instance families and Regions, plus some Fargate and Lambda usage. Reserved Instances feel too rigid because instance types change often. Which pricing model gives the biggest discount with the most flexibility?
options: Standard Reserved Instances for each specific instance type
Convertible Reserved Instances with manual exchanges each quarter
Compute Savings Plans, which discount EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage across families, sizes, and Regions automatically
Scheduled Reserved Instances for the nightly batch window
explain: Compute Savings Plans apply to usage across instance families, sizes, Regions, plus Fargate and Lambda, automatically following workload changes. Standard RIs lock to a family/Region; Convertible RIs allow exchanges but remain EC2-only and manual; Scheduled RIs were retired and never covered Fargate or Lambda.

q: An order-processing system must handle payment messages in exact order with no duplicates, even if producers retry. Standard SQS sometimes delivers out of order and twice. Which SQS configuration guarantees ordering and exactly-once processing?
options: Increase the standard queue's visibility timeout to 12 hours
Use an SQS FIFO queue with message group IDs and content-based deduplication
Add more consumers to the standard queue to drain it faster
Enable long polling on the standard queue
explain: FIFO queues preserve per-group ordering and provide exactly-once processing with deduplication IDs. Longer visibility timeouts and long polling do not fix ordering or duplicates; more consumers on a standard queue increase the chance of out-of-order processing.

q: A checkout workflow calls inventory, payment, and shipping services in sequence with retries, timeouts, and compensation logic when a step fails. Chaining SQS queues has made the state hard to track and failures hard to unwind. Which service is designed for this orchestration?
options: Amazon SNS with message filtering between the services
Amazon EventBridge Pipes with no state tracking
AWS Lambda with increased memory for the whole workflow
AWS Step Functions, which models the workflow as a state machine with built-in retries, catch blocks, and visual execution history
explain: Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows with durable state, per-state retries, error catching, and compensation paths, plus a visual console of each execution. SNS and Pipes move messages without workflow state; a single Lambda cannot durably track long multi-step state across failures.

q: A team runs RDS MySQL with a Multi-AZ instance deployment and wants readable standby replicas for reporting without adding separate read replicas. Which RDS deployment model provides two readable standby instances across three Availability Zones?
options: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster, which provides a writer plus two readable standby instances in three AZs
A standard Multi-AZ DB instance deployment, whose standby already accepts reads
A single-AZ instance with automated backups enabled
An RDS read replica promoted to a standalone instance
explain: A Multi-AZ DB cluster runs one writer and two readable standbys across three AZs with faster failover than instance deployments. In a classic Multi-AZ instance deployment the standby is not readable; single-AZ offers no standby; a promoted read replica becomes standalone and loses the cluster topology.

q: An Auto Scaling group launches 200 instances from a 500 GB snapshot-backed AMI during traffic spikes, but the first reads on each new volume are slow while blocks are lazily fetched from S3. Which EBS feature eliminates this initialization penalty?
options: Enable EBS encryption on the snapshot to speed up block fetches
Use Provisioned IOPS volumes for the root device
Enable EBS fast snapshot restore (FSR) on the snapshot in each AZ so volumes are fully initialized at creation
Increase the snapshot's volume size to raise baseline performance
explain: Fast snapshot restore pre-warms the snapshot so new volumes deliver full performance immediately, removing lazy-load latency during mass scale-out. Encryption does not change fetch behavior; provisioned IOPS does not pre-fetch blocks; larger volumes still lazy-load on first access.

q: A company must keep daily backups of production databases in a separate AWS account so a compromise of the production account cannot destroy backups. Which AWS Backup approach meets this requirement?
options: Create the backup vault in the production account and share it with IAM users
Enable cross-Region copy within the same production account
Export backups to an S3 bucket with public read access for the second account
Copy recovery points to a backup vault in a dedicated backup account using cross-account backup
explain: Cross-account backup copies recovery points into a vault owned by a separate account, isolating them from production-account compromise. A vault in the production account shares its fate; cross-Region copy stays in the same account; public S3 access is insecure and outside Backup's management.

q: An Auto Scaling group runs a web fleet on Spot Instances. When EC2 reclaims Spot capacity, instances terminate with only a two-minute warning and the fleet briefly drops below desired capacity. Which ASG feature proactively replaces Spot instances before interruption?
options: Enable Capacity Rebalancing so the group launches replacement instances when EC2 issues a rebalance recommendation
Set the Spot maximum price far above On-Demand to prevent reclamation
Enable detailed CloudWatch monitoring on the instances
Suspend the group's health checks during Spot interruptions
explain: Capacity Rebalancing acts on EC2's rebalance recommendation signal, launching replacements before Spot instances are reclaimed so capacity never dips. A higher max price does not prevent capacity-driven interruptions; detailed monitoring only observes; suspending health checks leaves terminated instances in service.

q: A global application caches session data in ElastiCache for Redis in us-east-1, but users in ap-southeast-2 see high read latency. The team needs active-active regional caches with sub-second cross-Region replication. Which ElastiCache feature provides this?
options: Redis Cluster mode with more shards in us-east-1
ElastiCache for Redis Global Datastore, which replicates to a secondary Region with typical sub-second lag
Increase the node type in the primary Region
Enable Redis AUTH token for faster authentication
explain: Global Datastore provides managed cross-Region replication of Redis with typical lag under one second and promotes the secondary for disaster recovery. More shards or bigger nodes do not shorten cross-Region latency; AUTH tokens address security, not performance.

q: An application downloads 20 GB S3 objects to EC2 for processing, but single GET requests saturate neither the instance nor the network, and downloads take too long. Which S3 technique parallelizes a single object's download?
options: Use S3 byte-range fetches (Range GET) to download parts of the object in parallel and reassemble them
Enable S3 Versioning to read from multiple versions simultaneously
Use S3 Select to download the object faster
Request the object through CloudFront with a longer TTL
explain: Byte-range fetches split one object into ranges retrieved concurrently, multiplying throughput for large objects. Versioning does not parallelize reads; S3 Select retrieves subsets of data, not faster full downloads; CloudFront caching helps repeated requests, not first-byte throughput to EC2.

q: A team runs self-managed Kafka on EC2 and spends significant effort on broker patching, ZooKeeper quorum management, and partition rebalancing. They want managed Kafka with the same protocol so producers and consumers need no code changes. Which service fits?
options: Migrate the producers to Kinesis Data Streams with the Kafka protocol
Replace Kafka with SQS FIFO queues for the same semantics
Use Kinesis Data Firehose as a drop-in Kafka replacement
Use Amazon MSK, a managed Kafka service supporting the native Kafka APIs
explain: Amazon MSK runs real Apache Kafka with managed brokers, patching, and scaling while existing Kafka clients connect unchanged. Kinesis Data Streams speaks its own API (the MSK-compatible layer is MSK itself); SQS FIFO and Firehose do not speak the Kafka protocol.

q: A fraud-detection engine traverses relationships between accounts, devices, and transactions up to six hops deep. In RDS, these queries require expensive recursive joins that time out. Which database service is purpose-built for multi-hop relationship queries?
options: Amazon DynamoDB with a global secondary index per hop
Amazon RDS with read replicas to parallelize the joins
Amazon Neptune, a graph database optimized for traversing highly connected data
Amazon Redshift with dense compute nodes for the join workload
explain: Neptune stores data as a graph and executes multi-hop traversals natively without recursive joins. DynamoDB GSIs do not model graph traversals; read replicas scale reads but not join complexity; Redshift is an analytical warehouse, not a graph engine.

q: An EFS file system serves bursty rendering jobs: idle most of the day, then needing 5 GB/s for two hours. The team does not want to pay for provisioned throughput around the clock. Which EFS throughput mode matches this pattern?
options: Elastic Throughput, which automatically scales throughput up and down with actual usage
Bursting Throughput with a small file system for maximum burst credits
Provisioned Throughput set to 5 GB/s permanently
Max I/O mode, which provisions the highest fixed throughput
explain: Elastic Throughput automatically scales to meet workload demand and bills for actual usage, ideal for spiky patterns. Bursting ties throughput to stored data size, which fails for large bursts on small file systems; permanent provisioned throughput wastes money during idle hours; Max I/O is a performance mode, not a billing mode.

q: A multiplayer game uses a custom UDP protocol and needs fixed anycast IP addresses that route players to the nearest healthy Region with fast failover. CloudFront only handles HTTP. Which service provides global static IPs for TCP/UDP workloads?
options: Route 53 latency-based routing with Elastic IPs
An NLB in each Region with cross-Region DNS round robin
CloudFront with a UDP-enabled origin
AWS Global Accelerator, which provides static anycast IPs routing TCP/UDP traffic to optimal Regional endpoints
explain: Global Accelerator assigns static anycast IPs and routes TCP/UDP to the nearest healthy endpoint with fast failover. Route 53 alone does not provide static anycast IPs or health-aware UDP routing; regional NLBs lack unified anycast; CloudFront is HTTP(S)-only.

q: A web server in a public subnet stops receiving responses after the team tightens the subnet's network ACL to allow inbound HTTPS only. The server can receive requests but responses never arrive. Which NACL property explains this?
options: Network ACLs are stateful, so the outbound rule must reference the inbound connection
Network ACLs are stateless: return traffic needs an explicit outbound rule allowing the ephemeral port range
Security groups override network ACL outbound rules
HTTPS responses require a separate inbound rule on port 443
explain: NACLs are stateless, so the inbound allow on 443 does not automatically permit the response; an outbound rule for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) is required. They are not stateful like security groups; security groups do not override NACLs since both are evaluated; the response leaves on an ephemeral port, not inbound 443.
