q: An AWS service needs permission to use a KMS key for encryption on behalf of many different users, but the team cannot modify every user's IAM policy. Which KMS mechanism delegates key usage without touching identity policies?
options: Add each user to the key policy's principal list individually
Create an IAM role per user with kms:Decrypt permission
Use KMS grants, which delegate specific key operations to a principal without changing IAM policies
Disable the key policy and rely on SCPs
explain: KMS grants let a key owner delegate precisely scoped key operations to AWS services or principals programmatically, the mechanism services like EBS and S3 use. Editing every key policy or creating per-user roles does not scale; disabling the key policy removes the primary authorization control.

q: A company runs application servers in its on-premises data center that need to call AWS APIs with temporary credentials instead of long-lived access keys. There is no VPN or Direct Connect identity federation in place. Which IAM feature issues temporary credentials to these servers?
options: IAM Roles Anywhere, which exchanges X.509 certificates for temporary AWS credentials
IAM instance profiles attached to the on-premises servers
Cognito identity pools with unauthenticated access
IAM access keys rotated manually every week
explain: IAM Roles Anywhere lets non-AWS workloads present X.509 certificates to obtain temporary credentials via STS. Instance profiles only work on EC2; Cognito identity pools target mobile/web users, not servers; manual key rotation keeps the long-lived credential risk.

q: Administrators currently SSH into EC2 instances through a bastion host, which requires maintaining SSH keys, bastion patching, and open inbound port 22. The team wants audited shell access with no inbound ports and no key management. Which solution provides this?
options: Move the bastion host to a public subnet with security group IP restrictions
Replace SSH keys with passwords rotated monthly
Open port 22 only to the corporate VPN range
Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for browser/CLI shell access with IAM authentication and session logging
explain: Session Manager tunnels shell access through the SSM agent with IAM authentication, requires no inbound ports or SSH keys, and logs sessions to S3 or CloudWatch. A hardened bastion still needs keys, patching, and port 22; passwords are weaker than keys; VPN-restricted port 22 still exposes SSH.

q: A bucket policy explicitly denies s3:GetObject to everyone except a CloudFront OAI, but some IAM users can still download objects directly. The users' identity policies allow s3:GetObject on the bucket. Why does access still succeed?
options: Bucket policies only apply to anonymous users, not IAM users
IAM identity policies override bucket policy denies
An explicit deny in either policy always wins; the team misconfigured the deny condition so it does not match these requests
S3 ignores bucket policies when versioning is enabled
explain: An explicit deny in any applicable policy always overrides allows, so if access succeeds the deny's condition or resource ARN is not matching these requests. Bucket policies apply to IAM principals too; identity allows never override explicit denies; versioning has no effect on policy evaluation.

q: Auditors need to run SQL queries over seven years of CloudTrail management events to investigate who changed security groups each quarter. The events are archived in S3 as JSON. Which solution enables SQL analysis without building a pipeline?
options: Load the JSON into DynamoDB and query with PartiQL
Use CloudTrail Lake, which ingests the trail into a managed queryable event data store with SQL
Enable CloudTrail Insights to run the SQL queries
Copy the logs to CloudWatch Logs and use metric filters
explain: CloudTrail Lake stores events in a managed data lake queryable with SQL for up to 7 years, with no ETL to build. DynamoDB would need a custom ingestion pipeline; Insights detects anomalous activity rather than running ad-hoc SQL; metric filters aggregate counts but do not provide SQL over raw events.

q: A company keeps all user accounts in its on-premises Active Directory and will not sync passwords or accounts to AWS. EC2-hosted applications need to authenticate users against the on-premises directory with minimal AWS-side directory infrastructure. Which Directory Service option fits?
options: AD Connector, which proxies authentication requests to the on-premises AD without syncing accounts
AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a one-way outgoing trust
Simple AD with manually duplicated user accounts
Cognito user pools with imported user passwords
explain: AD Connector is a directory gateway that forwards authentication to the on-premises AD, keeping all accounts and passwords on-premises with no sync. Managed Microsoft AD hosts its own directory (needing trusts and more infrastructure); Simple AD is a separate Samba directory; Cognito imports would violate the no-sync requirement.

q: Two chatty application tiers in different Availability Zones exchange 5 TB daily, and the bill shows significant inter-AZ data transfer charges. The application can tolerate both tiers in one AZ for non-critical workloads. Which design change reduces this charge?
options: Enable cross-zone load balancing on the ALB between the tiers
Add a NAT gateway in each AZ to localize the traffic
Replace the EC2 tiers with Lambda functions in the same AZs
Co-locate the chatty tiers in the same AZ where the architecture allows, avoiding the per-GB inter-AZ transfer charge
explain: Traffic between AZs incurs a per-GB charge in each direction, so placing tightly coupled tiers in the same AZ eliminates it where resilience requirements allow. Cross-zone load balancing increases inter-AZ traffic; NAT gateways add their own processing charges; Lambda still bills for cross-AZ data transfer.

q: An EBS volume has daily snapshots going back a year. The team worries that deleting old snapshots will break the snapshot chain and lose the ability to restore. Which statement about EBS snapshots is correct?
options: Deleting any snapshot invalidates all later snapshots in the chain
Snapshots form a dependent chain and only the oldest can be safely deleted
EBS snapshots are incremental but each snapshot contains all data needed to restore; deleting old snapshots only removes data unique to them
Snapshots must be copied to S3 before deletion to preserve restore capability
explain: EBS snapshots are incremental at the block level, but every snapshot logically contains the full volume state, so deleting old ones only discards blocks no longer referenced. There is no fragile chain to break; snapshots already live on S3-backed storage, so no manual copy is needed.

q: A company with 300 S3 buckets across 20 accounts has no visibility into which buckets drive storage costs or lack lifecycle rules. Which service provides organization-wide S3 storage and cost visibility?
options: Amazon S3 Storage Lens, which aggregates storage metrics and cost-optimization recommendations across accounts
S3 server access logging on each bucket
AWS CloudTrail data events for S3
S3 Inventory reports per bucket without aggregation
explain: S3 Storage Lens provides centralized dashboards of usage, activity, and cost-optimization findings across an organization. Access logs and CloudTrail record requests but do not aggregate cost insights; Inventory lists objects per bucket without org-wide analytics.

q: A startup wants automated, no-effort identification of idle EC2 instances, unassociated Elastic IPs, and underutilized EBS volumes each week. Which service delivers these cost findings without agents or custom code?
options: AWS Compute Optimizer, which only covers EC2 instance types
AWS Trusted Advisor cost-optimization checks, which flag idle resources, unassociated EIPs, and underutilized volumes
AWS Budgets with forecasted alerts
VPC Flow Logs analyzed in Athena
explain: Trusted Advisor's cost-optimization checks specifically flag idle EC2, unassociated Elastic IPs, underutilized EBS, idle load balancers, and similar waste. Compute Optimizer focuses on rightsizing; Budgets alert on spend without identifying the waste; flow logs show traffic, not cost findings.

q: A containerized rendering workload runs on Fargate, tolerates interruptions, and checkpoints progress every few minutes. The team wants the lowest Fargate price for this fault-tolerant batch work. Which capacity option fits?
options: Fargate with Savings Plans for the steady baseline
Fargate Spot, which offers spare capacity at a deep discount for interruption-tolerant tasks
Dedicated Fargate tasks with provisioned concurrency
Running the tasks on EC2 On-Demand instead
explain: Fargate Spot uses spare compute capacity at up to 70% off for tasks that tolerate interruption, matching the checkpointed rendering workload. Savings Plans suit steady baselines, not spiky batch; Fargate has no provisioned concurrency; EC2 On-Demand costs more than discounted spare capacity.

q: A SaaS application's Aurora MySQL database idles overnight but spikes to 40 ACUs during the business day. Provisioning for the peak wastes money overnight. Which Aurora option scales compute automatically with demand?
options: Aurora provisioned clusters with manual read replica scaling
Aurora Backtrack to reduce compute during idle hours
Aurora Serverless v2, which scales ACUs up and down in fine increments based on load
Aurora Global Database with a second Region
explain: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity from 0.5 ACU upward in fine increments as load changes, paying only for consumed capacity. Manual replica scaling is slow and coarse; Backtrack rewinds data rather than scaling; Global Database adds a Region and cost rather than elasticity.

q: A company with a hybrid network needs on-premises servers to resolve private Route 53 hosted-zone names, and EC2 instances to resolve on-premises DNS names. Which Route 53 Resolver design enables bidirectional hybrid DNS?
options: Create a public hosted zone mirroring the private zone records
Use the default VPC resolver for both directions
Forward all DNS queries to 8.8.8.8 from both environments
Deploy Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints (for on-premises queries to AWS) and outbound endpoints with forwarding rules (for AWS queries to on-premises)
explain: Inbound endpoints let on-premises DNS resolve private AWS names; outbound endpoints with forwarding rules let VPC resources resolve on-premises names. Public zones would expose private names; the default resolver cannot reach on-premises DNS; public resolvers know nothing about private zones.

q: An operator accidentally deletes a critical DynamoDB table at 2 PM and needs it restored to its 1:55 PM state. The last on-demand backup ran at midnight. Which DynamoDB feature enables restoration to 1:55 PM?
options: Point-in-time recovery (PITR), which allows restore to any second within the preceding 35 days
DynamoDB Streams, which replay the deleted table automatically
The midnight on-demand backup, which contains the 1:55 PM state
Global tables, which keep a deleted-table copy in the second Region
explain: PITR continuously backs up with per-second granularity for 35 days, enabling restore to 1:55 PM. Streams capture changes but do not restore tables; the midnight backup predates the needed state; global tables replicate deletes rather than preserving the table.

q: An operations team receives hundreds of individual CloudWatch alarms during incidents, making it hard to tell when the system is truly unhealthy. They want one alarm that fires only when several underlying conditions are simultaneously breached. Which feature provides this?
options: Increase every alarm's evaluation period to reduce notifications
Create an SNS topic per alarm to organize notifications
Use CloudWatch composite alarms to combine multiple alarms into a single overall state
Enable detailed monitoring on all instances
explain: Composite alarms aggregate child alarms with boolean logic, producing one meaningful signal and suppressing noise. Longer evaluation periods delay detection; more SNS topics organize but do not reduce alarm count; detailed monitoring increases metric granularity, not alarm logic.

q: An application uses an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager deployed in a single Availability Zone. During an AZ impairment, the application cannot reach Secrets Manager even though instances in other AZs are healthy. What is the resilient design?
options: Replace the interface endpoint with a NAT gateway in each AZ
Deploy the interface endpoint with ENIs in multiple Availability Zones so endpoint access survives a single AZ impairment
Move the application to a single AZ matching the endpoint
Access Secrets Manager over the public internet instead
explain: Interface endpoints are zonal: each AZ needs its own endpoint ENI, otherwise an AZ failure removes access for that AZ's traffic. NAT gateways add cost without fixing zonal endpoint design; consolidating to one AZ reduces resilience; public internet access defeats the private-connectivity goal.

q: Developers need a full copy of a 3 TB Aurora production cluster for load testing, refreshed weekly. Snapshot restore takes hours and doubles storage cost. Which Aurora feature provisions the test copy in minutes with minimal extra storage?
options: Create a cross-Region read replica for testing
Enable Backtrack and rewind the production cluster weekly
Restore from the automated snapshot to a smaller instance class
Use Aurora cloning, which creates a copy-on-write clone sharing the underlying storage pages
explain: Aurora cloning uses copy-on-write: the clone shares storage pages with the source and only new writes consume space, provisioning in minutes. Cross-Region replicas add latency and cost; Backtrack rewinds production data rather than creating a test copy; snapshot restore is slow and duplicates all storage.

q: A fleet of workers polls an SQS queue that is empty most of the time. CloudWatch shows millions of empty receives inflating the API bill without doing useful work. Which polling configuration reduces empty receives?
options: Decrease the visibility timeout to return messages faster
Increase the number of worker threads polling the queue
Enable long polling so each ReceiveMessage call waits up to 20 seconds for messages to arrive
Switch to short polling with a 1-second interval
explain: Long polling holds the request open until messages arrive or the wait expires, collapsing empty receives and cutting cost. Shorter visibility timeouts and more threads increase API calls; short polling returns immediately, maximizing empty receives.

q: A DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity sees uneven traffic: a few popular items get most reads while most of the table is cold. Throttling occurs even though total consumed capacity is below the provisioned total. Which DynamoDB behavior mitigates this without manual intervention?
options: Adaptive capacity, which automatically redistributes throughput to hot partitions in the background
Point-in-time recovery, which rebalances partition throughput
On-demand backup, which absorbs burst traffic
Global secondary indexes, which isolate hot items automatically
explain: Adaptive capacity automatically boosts throughput for hot partitions by borrowing unused capacity, enabled by default with no configuration. PITR and backups do not affect throughput; GSIs create new access paths but do not rebalance the base table's partitions.

q: A company uploads large media files to an S3 bucket in us-west-2 from creators across Asia and Europe. Uploads over the public internet are slow due to distance and packet loss. Which S3 feature accelerates these global uploads?
options: S3 Object Lock to speed up multipart uploads
S3 Inventory to optimize upload routing
S3 Versioning to parallelize uploads
S3 Transfer Acceleration, which routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations over optimized network paths
explain: Transfer Acceleration ingests uploads at nearby edge locations and moves them over AWS's optimized backbone to the bucket Region. Object Lock, Inventory, and Versioning have no effect on transfer speed.

q: An RDS MySQL instance shows high CPU but the team cannot tell whether the load comes from specific queries, connections, or background tasks. They need a visual breakdown of database load by wait state without installing agents. Which RDS feature provides this?
options: Enhanced Monitoring, which shows OS-level metrics per process
CloudTrail data events for the RDS API calls
Performance Insights, which visualizes DB load by SQL, wait events, and users from collected performance data
The RDS slow query log shipped to CloudWatch Logs only
explain: Performance Insights provides an interactive dashboard of database load segmented by waits, SQL statements, hosts, and users with no agent needed. Enhanced Monitoring shows OS metrics, not query-level waits; CloudTrail logs API calls, not query performance; the slow query log alone lacks the visual load analysis.

q: A CloudFront distribution caches personalized content incorrectly: logged-in users sometimes see another user's page because the cache key ignores the session cookie. Which CloudFront configuration separates caching behavior from origin request content?
options: Use cache policies to define the cache key (headers, cookies, query strings) separately from origin request policies that forward additional data to the origin
Disable caching entirely for the distribution
Set the TTL to zero and rely on the origin for every request
Use a single legacy cache behavior with all cookies forwarded
explain: Cache policies control exactly what forms the cache key, while origin request policies forward extra headers/cookies to the origin without affecting caching, fixing the personalization leak. Disabling caching or zero TTL destroys the CDN benefit; forwarding all cookies in the legacy model pollutes the cache key.

q: A Lambda function downloads a 6 GB reference dataset to /tmp on every cold start, but the default ephemeral storage is only 512 MB and the download fails. Which Lambda configuration supports this workload?
options: Increase the function's memory to 10 GB to enlarge /tmp automatically
Stream the dataset through Lambda response streaming instead
Attach an EFS file system as the only storage option
Configure ephemeral storage up to 10 GB so /tmp can hold the dataset
explain: Lambda supports configurable ephemeral storage from 512 MB to 10 GB, directly solving the /tmp capacity problem. Memory size does not change /tmp; response streaming sends data to clients rather than storing it; EFS works but adds VPC and file-system complexity for a simple scratch need.

q: A Windows-based engineering team needs shared file storage with native SMB protocol support, Active Directory integration, and Windows ACLs for their CAD applications. Which storage service is purpose-built for this?
options: Amazon EFS with NFSv4 mounts on the Windows instances
Amazon FSx for Lustre with an SMB gateway
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, which provides native SMB shares with AD integration and Windows ACLs
Amazon S3 with the File Gateway in SMB mode only
explain: FSx for Windows File Server is a native Windows file system with SMB, Active Directory integration, and Windows ACLs. EFS speaks NFS, not SMB; FSx for Lustre is a POSIX HPC file system; File Gateway presents S3 as SMB but lacks native Windows ACL and AD semantics.

q: A company discovers several S3 buckets are publicly readable due to overly permissive bucket policies set by different teams. They need an account-level guardrail that blocks public access regardless of individual bucket policies. Which feature provides this?
options: Enable MFA Delete on each bucket
Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level to override any public bucket policies or ACLs
Attach an SCP that denies s3:PutObject to all buckets
Enable default encryption on every bucket
explain: S3 Block Public Access at the account level blocks public ACLs and policies across all current and future buckets, overriding team-level mistakes. MFA Delete protects against version deletion, not public reads; denying PutObject breaks legitimate writes; encryption does not control public access.

q: A defense contractor must keep encryption keys in hardware security modules located in its own data centers, outside AWS infrastructure entirely, while still using AWS KMS APIs from applications. Which KMS feature supports keys stored outside AWS?
options: KMS multi-Region keys replicated to the contractor's data center
Imported key material into a standard KMS key
AWS CloudHSM cluster in the application's VPC
A KMS External Key Store (XKS) backed by the contractor's on-premises HSMs
explain: External Key Store (XKS) lets KMS use key material held in HSMs outside AWS while applications keep calling standard KMS APIs. Multi-Region keys stay within AWS; imported key material still resides in AWS KMS; CloudHSM runs inside AWS, not in the contractor's data centers.

q: An application on EC2 connects to RDS MySQL with a database password stored in an environment variable. A credential leak exposed the password, and the team wants to eliminate long-lived database passwords entirely. Which RDS authentication approach removes stored passwords?
options: Use RDS IAM database authentication, where the application obtains a short-lived auth token via IAM credentials instead of a password
Store the password in an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption
Embed the password in the AMI so it is never in an environment variable
Rotate the password manually every 90 days and email it to developers
explain: IAM database authentication replaces passwords with 15-minute auth tokens derived from IAM credentials, eliminating stored secrets and enabling IAM-based access control. An S3-stored password is still a long-lived secret; baking it into the AMI spreads it further; manual rotation keeps the password risk between rotations.

q: A security team learns attackers are uploading malware to an S3 bucket used for customer file uploads. They need automatic scanning of new objects with findings routed to the security workflow. Which GuardDuty capability provides this?
options: GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring for the EC2 instances
GuardDuty S3 Protection, which only logs API calls
GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3, which scans newly uploaded objects and generates findings
GuardDuty RDS Protection applied to the S3 bucket
explain: Malware Protection for S3 scans new objects on upload and emits findings with the threat details, no agent required. Runtime Monitoring covers EC2/ECS/Lambda execution; S3 Protection (the foundational plan) analyzes API and data events rather than scanning content; RDS Protection applies to database instances, not S3.

q: An audit finds IAM policies granting far more permissions than teams actually use. The team wants data-driven recommendations to trim policies to least privilege based on real access history. Which service generates these recommendations?
options: AWS IAM Access Analyzer, which identifies unused access and can generate least-privilege policies from CloudTrail history
AWS Organizations SCPs, which automatically trim identity policies
IAM credential reports, which rewrite policies automatically
AWS Config rules, which generate replacement policies
explain: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes CloudTrail access history to surface unused permissions and can generate scoped-down policies. SCPs set guardrails but do not rewrite identity policies; credential reports list key age, not policy trimming; Config rules detect drift but do not generate policies.

q: A CISO asks for one dashboard showing security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie across all accounts, with severity normalization and automated response hooks. Which service is the aggregation and response hub?
options: Amazon Detective, which aggregates findings from all services
AWS Security Lake, which stores raw security logs
AWS Security Hub, which centralizes, normalizes, and prioritizes findings with automated response via EventBridge
AWS Artifact, which consolidates compliance findings
explain: Security Hub aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and others into normalized formats (ASFF) with severity, insights, and EventBridge-driven automation. Detective investigates incidents rather than aggregating; Security Lake stores raw logs for analytics; Artifact provides compliance reports, not live findings.

q: A team compares storing rarely accessed backups in S3 Intelligent-Tiering's Archive Access tier versus a lifecycle rule to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Their restores are infrequent but urgent. Which cost factor favors Intelligent-Tiering here?
options: Intelligent-Tiering charges no retrieval fees while Glacier Flexible Retrieval charges per restore, and tiering is automatic with no lifecycle rules to manage
Glacier Flexible Retrieval has no minimum storage duration
Intelligent-Tiering storage costs are always lower than Glacier
Lifecycle rules to Glacier are free while Intelligent-Tiering charges per transition
explain: Intelligent-Tiering's archive tiers have no per-GB retrieval fees (unlike Glacier Flexible's expedited/standard restore fees) and move objects automatically without lifecycle rules. Glacier Flexible has a 90-day minimum duration; Intelligent-Tiering storage rates are higher than Glacier's; lifecycle transitions carry per-request fees too.

q: A VPC uses one NAT gateway for all private subnets. The bill shows high hourly charges plus per-GB processing, though most traffic is just EC2 pulling patches and S3 data. Which combination most reduces NAT-related spend?
options: Replace the NAT gateway with a larger NAT gateway for better throughput
Add a second NAT gateway in the same AZ for redundancy
Move all instances to public subnets to eliminate NAT entirely
Use VPC endpoints for AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, Systems Manager) so that traffic bypasses the NAT gateway, and consider NAT instances only if the remaining traffic justifies it
explain: VPC endpoints (gateway endpoints free; interface endpoints cheaper than NAT processing for AWS-service traffic) remove the per-GB NAT charge for service traffic, which is usually the bulk. Bigger or duplicated NAT gateways increase hourly cost; public subnets expose instances and still use internet data transfer.

q: Cost Explorer shows $3,000/month in EBS charges for volumes not attached to any instance, some unattached for over a year. Which practice eliminates this waste going forward?
options: Enable EBS encryption on all unattached volumes
Convert unattached volumes to io2 for lower cost
Identify unattached volumes via Trusted Advisor or Cost Explorer, snapshot the ones worth keeping, and delete the volumes since EBS bills for provisioned capacity regardless of attachment
Move unattached volumes to a cheaper Availability Zone
explain: EBS bills for provisioned capacity whether attached or not, so unattached volumes are pure waste; snapshot what matters and delete the rest. Encryption does not reduce cost; io2 is more expensive; volumes cannot move AZs and location does not change the waste.

q: A finance team wants alerts when spending deviates unexpectedly from historical patterns, without manually setting dozens of static thresholds per service. Which AWS cost tool uses machine learning for this?
options: AWS Budgets with fixed cost thresholds per department
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection, which learns spending patterns and alerts on unusual activity
Cost Explorer's monthly forecast reports
AWS Pricing Calculator estimates
explain: Cost Anomaly Detection applies ML to spending patterns and alerts on anomalies without manual thresholds. Budgets require predefined limits; Cost Explorer forecasts show trends but do not alert; the Pricing Calculator estimates future bills rather than monitoring actuals.

q: A compute-heavy web fleet runs on x86 EC2 instances at high utilization. The team can recompile their application and wants the best price-performance for sustained workloads. Which processor option should they evaluate?
options: Switch to memory-optimized x86 instances for compute workloads
Enable Intel Turbo Boost on the existing instances
Use previous-generation instance types at lower On-Demand prices
Evaluate AWS Graviton instances, which offer better price-performance for many workloads including web fleets
explain: Graviton (Arm-based) instances typically deliver significantly better price-performance than comparable x86 for web, containerized, and compute workloads. Memory-optimized instances suit memory workloads, not compute; Turbo Boost is not a purchasable option; previous-generation types are less efficient per dollar.

q: A Redshift cluster used only for weekday analytics reporting runs 24/7, wasting compute on nights and weekends. Which Redshift capability eliminates the idle compute cost?
options: Enable concurrency scaling to handle the reporting load
Switch to Dense Compute nodes for lower hourly cost
Pause the cluster when idle and resume it for reporting windows; compute billing stops while paused
Delete the cluster nightly and restore from snapshot each morning
explain: Pause/resume stops compute billing during idle periods while data persists on managed storage, resuming in minutes. Concurrency scaling handles bursts but does not stop idle billing; DC2 nodes still bill 24/7; nightly delete/restore is slow and operationally fragile.

q: A company commits to $10,000/month of compute spend across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda, but instance families shift quarterly as teams modernize. They want maximum discount without locking to specific instance types. Which commitment option fits?
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans locked to one instance family
Standard Reserved Instances for each workload
Convertible Reserved Instances exchanged manually each quarter
Compute Savings Plans, which apply the discount across EC2 instance families, Fargate, and Lambda automatically
explain: Compute Savings Plans offer the broadest flexibility, applying to EC2 regardless of family/Region plus Fargate and Lambda, ideal for shifting workloads. EC2 Instance Savings Plans lock to a family; Standard RIs lock to family and Region; Convertible RIs need manual exchanges and remain EC2-only.

q: A company is migrating a self-managed Oracle database to Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime. The schemas differ between engines, and the team must convert stored procedures and then replicate ongoing changes during cutover. Which combination meets these requirements?
options: Use AWS DMS alone for both schema conversion and data replication
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to convert the schema and code, then use AWS DMS with change data capture (CDC) for the data migration and ongoing replication
Take a native Oracle RMAN backup and restore it directly onto Aurora PostgreSQL
Use AWS DataSync to copy the database files to S3 and import them into Aurora
explain: This is a heterogeneous migration (Oracle to PostgreSQL), so SCT converts the schema and procedural code while DMS replicates the data and uses CDC to keep the target in sync until cutover. DMS alone cannot convert stored procedures between different engines; RMAN backups only restore onto Oracle; DataSync moves files, not live databases.

q: A company must move 60 TB of file data from an on-premises NFS share to Amazon S3 over the next two weeks. The network link is healthy, and the team needs scheduled incremental copies with integrity validation. Which service is purpose-built for this online migration?
options: AWS DataSync with an NFS source location and an S3 destination, running scheduled tasks with built-in verification
AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway joined to the on-premises share
AWS Snowball Edge with the data shipped back on the device
An S3 VPC endpoint attached to the on-premises network
explain: DataSync is the managed online transfer service for NFS/SMB to S3/EFS/FSx with scheduling, incremental sync, and checksum validation. File Gateway presents S3 as a persistent file share rather than performing a bounded migration; Snowball is the offline path when the network cannot carry the data; a VPC endpoint only exists inside a VPC and cannot reach on-premises storage.

q: An order-processing system publishes domain events to a custom EventBridge event bus. A new fraud-detection service is launching and needs to analyze the last 30 days of order events, not just new ones. What is the simplest way to give it the historical events?
options: Configure a dead-letter queue on the event bus and read the old messages from it
Enable CloudTrail data events and have the new service parse the trail logs
Create an EventBridge archive on the bus covering the last 30 days, then start a replay to the new target
Export the events to Kinesis Data Streams and use enhanced fan-out to re-read the stream
explain: EventBridge archives capture events on a bus and replay sends them back to the bus (to new targets) for a chosen time window, which is exactly the historical-backfill use case. A dead-letter queue only holds failed deliveries, not the full event history; CloudTrail records API calls, not application domain events; a Kinesis stream only helps if the events were published there in the first place.

q: A payment service consumes order messages from SQS. For each customer, events must be processed in the exact order they were sent, and a retried message must never be applied twice. Which configuration guarantees both requirements?
options: A FIFO queue using the customer ID as the MessageGroupId and content-based deduplication enabled
A standard SQS queue with long polling enabled
An SNS topic fanning out to multiple standard queues
A FIFO queue with a single shared MessageGroupId for all customers
explain: FIFO queues order messages within a message group and deduplicate identical sends, so per-customer grouping plus content-based deduplication gives ordered, exactly-once processing. Standard queues offer best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery; SNS fanout does not add ordering or dedup; a single group ID for all customers would serialize every customer behind one another, destroying parallelism.

q: A financial application runs on Aurora PostgreSQL and requires cross-Region disaster recovery with a recovery point objective near one second and fast automated failover. Which Aurora capability is designed for this?
options: Aurora Backtrack with a 72-hour window
Aurora Multi-AZ deployment with a standby instance
Aurora Serverless v2 auto-scaling
An Aurora Global Database with a secondary cluster in the DR Region
explain: Aurora Global Database replicates to up to five secondary Regions with typical lag under one second and supports managed failover with RPO of 1 second and RTO under a minute. Backtrack rewinds a single cluster in time; Multi-AZ protects within one Region only; Serverless v2 scales capacity but provides no cross-Region recovery.

q: A media site serves dynamic content from an Application Load Balancer origin through CloudFront. During origin outages the team wants visitors to see a static maintenance page instead of an error. Which CloudFront feature delivers this failover behavior?
options: A Route 53 failover routing policy pointing at the ALB
An origin group with the ALB as primary and an S3 bucket holding the maintenance page as secondary, failing over on 5xx responses
A Lambda@Edge function that rewrites all requests to the S3 bucket
Weighted origins splitting traffic 90/10 between the ALB and S3
explain: CloudFront origin groups define a primary and secondary origin and fail over when the primary returns configured error codes such as 5xx, so the S3-hosted maintenance page appears automatically during outages. Route 53 failover switches DNS between origins but cannot serve substitute content; Lambda@Edge rewriting would bypass the ALB permanently; weighted origins split traffic continuously rather than failing over.

q: An Auto Scaling group launches EC2 instances from a large encrypted EBS snapshot during scale-out events. New instances take many minutes to become ready because snapshot blocks are lazily loaded from Amazon S3 on first access. Which feature eliminates this first-access latency?
options: Increase the provisioned IOPS on the snapshot
Convert the snapshot to an unencrypted snapshot
Enable Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) on the snapshot in the Availability Zones where instances launch
Enable EBS encryption by default on the account
explain: Fast Snapshot Restore pre-warms snapshot blocks so volumes created from the snapshot are fully performant immediately, removing lazy-load delays during scale-out. Snapshots have no IOPS setting to provision; unencrypted snapshots cannot be created from encrypted data that way and encryption is not the cause; default encryption governs new volumes, not snapshot restore speed.

q: An application caches user sessions in ElastiCache for Redis. Session keys have TTLs, but some long-lived configuration keys have no expiry. When memory fills, the team wants Redis to evict only keys that have a TTL, never the configuration keys. Which eviction policy should they set?
options: volatile-lru, which evicts only keys with an expire set, using least-recently-used
allkeys-lru, which evicts any key using least-recently-used
noeviction, which returns errors on writes when memory is full
volatile-ttl, which evicts keys with the shortest remaining TTL first
explain: volatile-lru restricts eviction to keys that have an expire set, so the TTL-less configuration keys are never candidates. allkeys-lru can evict any key including the configuration data; noeviction causes write failures under memory pressure; volatile-ttl also only touches keys with a TTL but evicts by shortest remaining TTL, which could drop nearly-expired sessions the team may still want.

q: A .NET application running on EC2 needs shared Windows file storage with native SMB and Active Directory integration for access control. Which storage service fits best?
options: Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon EFS with an access point
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explain: FSx for Windows File Server is the native Windows file system service with SMB and full Active Directory integration. FSx for Lustre targets HPC scratch workloads; EFS is NFS-based Linux storage without native Windows ACL/AD support; ONTAP offers multi-protocol file services but the purpose-built Windows-native choice is FSx for Windows File Server.

q: A tightly coupled MPI simulation runs across dozens of EC2 instances and is sensitive to network latency between nodes. Which placement group strategy minimizes inter-instance latency?
options: A spread placement group across distinct racks
A cluster placement group packing instances into the same Availability Zone with low-latency networking
A partition placement group with one partition per simulation rank
No placement group, relying on default EC2 placement
explain: Cluster placement groups co-locate instances for the lowest network latency and highest bandwidth, which is what tightly coupled HPC workloads need. Spread groups maximize hardware separation for fault tolerance at the cost of latency; partition groups isolate failure domains for distributed systems like Kafka; default placement makes no latency guarantees.

q: A distributed machine-learning training job uses NCCL for collective communication and needs OS-bypass networking to reach full throughput between GPU instances. Which network interface should the instances use?
options: The standard Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) with jumbo frames
An instance store-backed ephemeral network path
The Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), which provides OS-bypass RDMA-like communication for HPC and ML workloads
A secondary ENA attached to a separate subnet
explain: EFA is the OS-bypass network interface designed for tightly coupled HPC and distributed ML traffic such as NCCL collectives. ENA is the standard virtualized interface without OS-bypass; instance storage is disk, not networking; adding a second ENA does not change the packet path through the OS network stack.

q: A read-heavy application queries DynamoDB and needs microsecond response times, but the team cannot change any application code. Which caching layer can be added transparently?
options: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), a write-through caching layer that works with existing DynamoDB API calls
ElastiCache for Redis with the application rewritten to check the cache first
DynamoDB global tables in a second Region
DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode
explain: DAX sits in front of DynamoDB and accelerates reads to microseconds while remaining API-compatible, so no code changes are required. ElastiCache requires the application to implement cache-aside logic; global tables add multi-Region writes rather than caching; on-demand mode changes capacity billing, not latency.

q: Users around the world upload large video files to an application, and uploads from distant Regions are slow. Which S3 feature accelerates uploads by routing them through the AWS edge network?
options: S3 multipart upload from the application servers
S3 Transfer Acceleration, which sends uploads to the nearest edge location and carries them over the AWS backbone
S3 Cross-Region Replication of the destination bucket
S3 Select to filter data before upload
explain: Transfer Acceleration terminates uploads at the nearest CloudFront edge location and moves the data over AWS's private backbone to the bucket Region, cutting long-haul internet latency. Multipart upload parallelizes a single upload but does not change the network path; replication copies objects after they arrive; S3 Select queries stored objects and is unrelated to upload speed.

q: EC2 instances in private subnets need access to Amazon S3, DynamoDB, and Secrets Manager. The architect wants to avoid NAT Gateway data-processing charges where possible. Which endpoint design is most cost-effective?
options: Route all traffic through a NAT Gateway in each Availability Zone
Gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (no hourly or data charges) plus an interface endpoint for Secrets Manager
Interface VPC endpoints for all three services
A VPC peering connection to a shared services VPC hosting a proxy
explain: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB carry no hourly or data-processing charges, while Secrets Manager has no gateway endpoint so it needs an interface endpoint; this removes the NAT path for the two highest-volume services. Routing everything through NAT Gateways incurs per-GB processing fees; interface endpoints for S3/DynamoDB would add unnecessary hourly and per-GB charges; peering does not provide AWS service access.

q: A company must let a partner's VPC consume an internal HTTPS API without traffic traversing the public internet and without merging networks via peering or a transit gateway. Which approach provides this private connectivity?
options: A public Application Load Balancer with IP allow-listing
A VPC peering connection with non-overlapping CIDRs
An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer, consumed through an interface VPC endpoint in the partner VPC
A Site-to-Site VPN between the two VPCs
explain: PrivateLink exposes a service through an endpoint service and NLB so consumers connect via interface endpoints with no internet traversal, no peering, and no CIDR coordination. A public ALB still traverses the internet; peering merges the networks and requires non-overlapping CIDRs; a VPN connects networks but does not publish a service privately to another VPC.

q: A company uses AWS Organizations and must guarantee that no member account, even one administered by a rogue administrator, can disable CloudTrail logging or delete log archives. Which control enforces this preventively?
options: A service control policy (SCP) attached at the organization root denying cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and s3:Delete* on the log archive bucket
An IAM policy on each administrator denying CloudTrail actions
An AWS Config rule that flags CloudTrail trails that are not logging
MFA Delete enabled on the CloudTrail log bucket
explain: SCPs set guardrails that apply even to account administrators, so a deny on stopping or deleting trails cannot be overridden inside a member account. IAM policies can be changed or removed by an administrator; Config rules are detective and only flag after the fact; MFA Delete protects object versions but does not prevent stopping the trail itself.

q: A data lake in Amazon S3 holds petabytes of mixed objects, and the security team needs to automatically discover where PII and financial data reside so retention policies can be applied. Which service performs this classification?
options: Amazon Inspector
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Macie, which uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data in S3
explain: Macie is purpose-built to scan S3 buckets and classify sensitive data such as PII and financial records. Inspector scans compute workloads and container images for vulnerabilities; Config tracks resource configuration compliance; GuardDuty detects threats and anomalous behavior rather than classifying stored data.

q: A company needs to share an encrypted EBS snapshot with a partner AWS account so the partner can create volumes from it. The snapshot is encrypted with the default aws/ebs KMS key. What must happen first?
options: Share the snapshot directly, because encryption keys are automatically shared with it
Copy the snapshot while re-encrypting it with a customer managed key, then share both the snapshot and the key with the partner account
Make the snapshot public so any account can copy it
Remove encryption from the snapshot before sharing
explain: Snapshots encrypted with the AWS managed aws/ebs key cannot be shared across accounts; you must copy the snapshot with a customer managed key and grant the partner account access to both the snapshot and the key. Encryption keys are never shared automatically; public snapshots are blocked for encrypted snapshots and would be a severe exposure; EBS encryption cannot be removed from an existing snapshot.

q: A platform team wants to let development team leads create IAM roles for their own teams, but no role they create may ever exceed a defined maximum set of permissions. Which IAM mechanism enforces this ceiling on delegated administration?
options: Service control policies applied to the development OUs
Session policies attached at role assumption time
Permissions boundaries, which set the maximum permissions an IAM entity can have regardless of its identity policies
Resource-based policies on each role
explain: Permissions boundaries define the maximum permissions for a user or role, so delegated administrators cannot grant anything beyond the boundary even if they write permissive identity policies. SCPs operate at the AWS Organizations level rather than delegating within an account; session policies only scope a single session; resource-based policies control who can access a resource, not the ceiling on what a role may be granted.

q: A workload in private subnets transfers large volumes of data to Amazon S3 through NAT Gateways, and the NAT data-processing charges dominate the bill. Which change eliminates those charges for the S3 traffic?
options: Add a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 so the traffic stays on the AWS network with no data-processing charge
Deploy larger NAT Gateways in each Availability Zone
Replace the NAT Gateways with NAT instances on Spot
Attach an internet gateway directly to the private subnets
explain: A gateway VPC endpoint routes S3 traffic privately within the AWS network with no hourly or per-GB processing charges, removing the NAT path for that traffic. Larger NAT Gateways still charge per GB processed; NAT instances still incur EC2 and data-transfer costs plus operational burden; an internet gateway cannot attach to private subnets without making them public.

q: A company serves billions of small image downloads per month directly from Amazon S3, and S3 data-transfer-out charges are the largest line item. Which architecture most reduces the per-GB delivery cost?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
Replicate the bucket to a second Region with Cross-Region Replication
Serve the images through CloudFront, since S3-to-CloudFront origin fetches incur no data-transfer charge and CloudFront per-GB rates are lower than S3 internet egress
Move the images to EBS volumes behind an Application Load Balancer
explain: CloudFront lowers delivery cost because origin fetches from S3 are free and CloudFront's per-GB egress rates are lower than S3 direct internet egress, while also improving performance. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, not downloads, and adds a surcharge; cross-Region replication adds replication transfer and storage costs; serving from EBS behind an ALB replaces cheap object storage with expensive block storage and EC2 data transfer.

q: The finance team needs hourly, resource-level billing line items delivered to S3 so they can join cost data with internal chargeback tags in their own analytics pipeline. Which AWS source provides this granular data?
options: AWS Cost Explorer with hourly granularity enabled
The AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR), which delivers detailed line-item billing data to S3
AWS Budgets cost reports
CloudWatch billing metrics
explain: CUR is the authoritative detailed billing dataset, delivered as line items to S3 for custom analysis and joins. Cost Explorer visualizes aggregated costs but does not deliver raw line-item files to S3; Budgets tracks against thresholds and sends alerts; CloudWatch billing metrics provide high-level estimated charges, not resource-level line items.

q: A startup wants an alert when forecasted month-end spend is projected to exceed 80% of its budget, before the money is actually spent. Which capability provides forecast-based alerting?
options: A CloudWatch alarm on the EstimatedCharges billing metric
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection with a custom monitor
An AWS Budget with a forecasted-spend alert threshold at 80%
The AWS Cost and Usage Report delivered daily to S3
explain: AWS Budgets supports alerts on both actual and forecasted spend, so a forecasted alert at 80% fires before the budget is breached. CloudWatch billing alarms trigger on estimated actual charges, not forecasts; Cost Anomaly Detection flags unusual spend patterns rather than budget thresholds; CUR delivers raw data but performs no alerting.

q: An application stores millions of objects with unpredictable access patterns. The team wants S3 to automatically move objects that go unaccessed for months into cheaper archive tiers, while still allowing millisecond retrieval if an object is suddenly needed. Which storage approach fits?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with the Archive Access and Deep Archive Access tiers enabled
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access for all objects from day one
A lifecycle rule transitioning everything to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90 days
S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access for all objects
explain: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access patterns and automatically moves unaccessed objects to Infrequent Access, then Archive and Deep Archive tiers, while keeping millisecond retrieval available. Standard-IA charges per-GB retrieval fees that punish unpredictable access; Glacier Flexible Retrieval imposes hours-long retrieval delays; One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing durability.

q: A company runs EC2 workloads with usage that shifts across instance families, sizes, and Regions as teams deploy new services. They want the deepest reliable discount without committing to specific instance types or Regions. Which pricing model fits best?
options: Standard Reserved Instances for each workload
On-Demand with Auto Scaling only
Spot Instances for the entire fleet
Compute Savings Plans, which discount usage across instance families, sizes, Regions, and even Fargate and Lambda
explain: Compute Savings Plans apply to any EC2 instance family, size, or Region (plus Fargate and Lambda), giving flexible coverage for shifting workloads in exchange for a usage commitment. Standard RIs lock to an instance family and Region; On-Demand carries no discount; running everything on Spot risks interruptions for workloads that cannot tolerate them.

q: A company connects development, production, and shared-services VPCs to a transit gateway. Production and development must never route to each other, but both need access to the shared-services VPC. How should the transit gateway be configured?
options: Attach all VPCs to a single transit gateway route table with full propagation
Peer the development and production VPCs directly and bypass the transit gateway
Use separate transit gateway route tables: associate development and production attachments with isolated route tables, and propagate only the shared-services routes into both
Place all subnets in a single shared VPC instead
explain: Transit gateway route tables control which attachments can reach each other, so isolated tables for dev and prod with only shared-services routes propagated gives segmentation plus shared access. A single route table with full propagation allows dev-to-prod traffic; VPC peering reintroduces mesh complexity the transit gateway was meant to remove; collapsing into one VPC destroys network isolation.

q: A company runs a Direct Connect connection as the primary path between its data center and AWS. It needs an automatic, encrypted backup path that takes over if the Direct Connect link fails, without manual intervention. Which design provides this?
options: A Site-to-Site VPN connection as a backup path, with BGP routing so traffic fails over automatically if Direct Connect goes down
A second Direct Connect connection in the same location with no routing changes
An internet gateway attached to the VPC as the backup path
A Transit Gateway Connect peer over the public internet
explain: A Site-to-Site VPN paired with BGP provides an encrypted backup path that automatically carries traffic when the Direct Connect route is withdrawn. A second DX in the same location shares fate with the first on local failures; an internet gateway does not extend to the data center; Transit Gateway Connect is for SD-WAN appliances, not a generic encrypted backup for DX.

q: An analytics application reads customer records from S3, but a new privacy rule requires Social Security numbers to be redacted for one class of readers. The team cannot duplicate the objects or change the writers. How can S3 serve redacted views of the same objects?
options: Create a second bucket with redacted copies and keep them in sync with replication
Use S3 Select to filter columns at query time for all readers
Apply a bucket policy that denies access to the sensitive prefix
Use S3 Object Lambda to invoke a Lambda function that redacts the sensitive fields as objects are retrieved, exposed through an Object Lambda access point
explain: S3 Object Lambda transforms objects on retrieval, so one stored object can serve both full and redacted views through different access points. Duplicating buckets doubles storage and sync burden; S3 Select only helps SQL-like queries, not general GETs; a deny policy blocks access entirely rather than redacting.

q: A workflow orchestrates order fulfillment across five services, runs for up to two hours per execution, and must execute each step exactly once even if retries occur. Which Step Functions configuration fits?
options: An Express workflow, which is optimized for high event rates
A Standard workflow, which supports long-running executions up to one year with exactly-once execution semantics
A set of SQS FIFO queues chained together with Lambda triggers
An Express workflow with idempotency handled by the caller
explain: Standard workflows run up to a year and guarantee exactly-once execution, matching the long-running, exactly-once requirement. Express workflows cap at five minutes and offer at-least-once semantics; chained FIFO queues can order messages but do not orchestrate multi-step workflows with state; pushing idempotency to the caller reimplements what Standard provides natively.

q: A web application runs active-passive across two Regions behind Route 53. The team wants DNS to stop sending traffic to the primary Region within a minute of an outage and only restore it after the endpoint is healthy again. Which setup achieves this?
options: A Route 53 failover routing policy with health checks on the primary endpoint, failing over to the secondary record when the health check fails
A weighted routing policy with 100% weight on the primary
A geolocation routing policy mapping all users to the primary Region
Multivalue answer routing with both endpoints returned
explain: Failover routing combined with health checks removes the primary record from DNS answers when it becomes unhealthy and restores it on recovery. Weighted 100/0 never shifts traffic automatically; geolocation routes by user location regardless of health; multivalue answer routing returns multiple healthy records for load distribution, not active-passive failover.

q: A media company stores 500 TB of production assets on EFS in us-east-1 and needs a disaster-recovery copy in eu-west-1 with an RPO measured in minutes. Which EFS capability provides this?
options: EFS lifecycle management moving files to Infrequent Access
EFS replication to a second Region, which continuously replicates data with minutes-level RPO
EFS backup to AWS Backup once per day
An EFS access point in eu-west-1 pointing at the us-east-1 file system
explain: EFS replication continuously copies data to a file system in another Region with an RPO of minutes, designed for disaster recovery. Lifecycle management only changes storage classes within one file system; daily backups give a 24-hour RPO; an access point in another Region cannot reach across Regions to the source file system.

q: A CloudFront distribution needs a lightweight transformation: appending a security header and normalizing URL casing on every viewer request. The team wants the cheapest, lowest-latency option that runs at the edge. Which should they choose?
options: Lambda@Edge on viewer request with 512 MB of memory
CloudFront Functions, which run lightweight JavaScript at the edge for viewer request and response events
An origin-request Lambda function in the primary Region
An Application Load Balancer rule rewriting the headers
explain: CloudFront Functions are built for simple, high-scale edge transformations on viewer events with sub-millisecond startup and lower cost than Lambda@Edge. Lambda@Edge supports heavier compute but costs more and starts slower; origin-request functions run in the Region, adding latency; ALB rules cannot execute arbitrary header and URL logic at the edge.

q: A global real-time gaming platform needs fixed IP addresses for firewall allow-listing, UDP support, and automatic routing of players to the healthiest Regional endpoint. Which AWS service provides all three?
options: CloudFront with static IP pinning
Route 53 latency-based routing alone
An Application Load Balancer in each Region
AWS Global Accelerator, which provides static Anycast IPs, supports TCP and UDP, and routes to healthy endpoints
explain: Global Accelerator allocates static Anycast IPs, handles TCP and UDP, and continuously health-checks endpoints to steer traffic to the best Region. CloudFront IP ranges are large and shared, not fixed per customer; Route 53 alone cannot provide static IPs or UDP proxying; ALBs get dynamic IPs and do not steer globally.

q: A clickstream pipeline writes events to Kinesis Data Streams. Three independent consumers must each read every event in order per user, without one consumer's slow reads blocking the others. Which design meets these needs?
options: Enhanced fan-out with a dedicated consumer per application, preserving per-partition-key ordering for each
A single shared consumer that fans out to the three applications
Three separate streams with the producer writing to each
Kinesis Data Firehose delivering to S3 for each consumer to poll
explain: Enhanced fan-out gives each consumer dedicated 2 MB/s throughput per shard so slow consumers never block others, while ordering per partition key is preserved. A single shared consumer couples all three applications' throughput; triple-writing multiplies producer cost and complexity; Firehose batches to destinations and does not provide per-consumer ordered stream reads.

q: Analysts need to run ad-hoc SQL queries over several terabytes of CSV and Parquet files in S3. Queries run a few times per day, and the team wants no infrastructure to manage. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon EMR with long-running clusters
Amazon Redshift provisioned clusters with Redshift Spectrum
Amazon Athena, a serverless query engine that reads directly from S3 and charges per query
AWS Glue ETL jobs writing to RDS
explain: Athena is serverless, queries S3 data in place, and bills per query, which suits infrequent ad-hoc analysis with zero infrastructure. EMR clusters idle between runs; provisioned Redshift requires cluster management and Spectrum still needs the cluster; Glue ETL plus RDS adds a pipeline and database for what is a read-only query need.

q: An HPC job writes 20 TB of temporary scratch data during a run and deletes it afterward. The instances need the highest local disk throughput and the data must not survive instance termination. Which storage choice is optimal?
options: EBS io2 volumes with Multi-Attach
NVMe instance store volumes, which provide high local throughput for ephemeral scratch data
EFS with provisioned throughput
S3 Standard with multipart upload
explain: Instance store volumes are physically attached NVMe SSDs offering very high local throughput for temporary data, and their ephemerality matches scratch semantics. io2 Multi-Attach is for shared durable block storage; EFS adds network latency and cost for data that will be deleted; S3 is object storage with higher per-operation latency, unsuitable as scratch disk.

q: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster serves a read-heavy reporting workload with sharp, unpredictable spikes. Reads must scale out automatically within minutes, and the writer must be unaffected. Which approach meets this?
options: Vertically scaling the writer instance on a schedule
Enabling Performance Insights on the writer
Migrating to Aurora Serverless v1
Aurora Auto Scaling for read replicas, which adds replicas as read load increases
explain: Aurora Auto Scaling adds read replicas in response to load, scaling reads horizontally without touching the writer. Vertical scaling requires downtime and does not help reads specifically; Performance Insights monitors rather than scales; Serverless v1 pauses and has connection limits that suit intermittent rather than spiky reporting workloads.

q: A leaderboard service needs a simple distributed cache with automatic sharding across nodes, and it can tolerate losing all cached data on a failure. Persistence and Multi-AZ failover are unnecessary. Which engine fits?
options: ElastiCache for Memcached, which shards across nodes with no persistence overhead
ElastiCache for Redis with cluster mode disabled and Multi-AZ enabled
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Amazon Neptune
explain: Memcached is the simple sharded caching engine with no persistence, matching a cache that can be rebuilt after failure. Redis with Multi-AZ adds replication and failover machinery the workload does not need; DAX only caches DynamoDB; Neptune is a graph database, not a cache.

q: A company encrypts millions of small S3 objects with SSE-KMS and notices KMS API costs climbing because every object generates a separate KMS request. Which S3 feature reduces these KMS call costs?
options: Switching to SSE-S3 for all objects
Disabling bucket versioning
S3 Bucket Keys, which use a per-bucket data key to reduce calls to KMS
Enabling S3 Object Lock
explain: S3 Bucket Keys generate a bucket-level data key from KMS and reuse it for objects, cutting KMS request volume and cost by up to 99%. SSE-S3 removes KMS entirely but changes the key-management model rather than optimizing it; versioning is unrelated to KMS calls; Object Lock governs immutability, not encryption costs.

q: A regulated company must prove that its CloudTrail logs have not been tampered with, and it operates 30 member accounts under AWS Organizations. Which design satisfies both the integrity and multi-account requirements?
options: A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter on each trail
An organization trail in the management account with log file validation enabled, delivering digest files that detect tampering
Separate trails in each account with S3 default encryption
AWS Config recording CloudTrail configuration changes
explain: An organization trail aggregates all member-account events centrally, and log file validation creates signed digest files that reveal any tampering with the logs. Subscription filters stream events but do not prove integrity; per-account trails fragment the audit record; Config records configuration changes but does not validate log integrity.

q: A public API behind an Application Load Balancer is being hit by a distributed flood of requests from thousands of IPs, each staying under normal per-IP rates. Which control best mitigates this Layer 7 flood?
options: A security group limiting connections per IP
AWS Shield Standard on the load balancer
Network ACLs blocking the offending CIDR ranges
AWS WAF with a rate-based rule on the ALB, optionally fronted by Shield Advanced for DDoS response support
explain: WAF rate-based rules track request rates and block floods at Layer 7, and Shield Advanced adds DDoS mitigation support for the ALB. Security groups cannot rate-limit; Shield Standard covers only Layer 3/4; NACLs are static and cannot adapt to thousands of rotating source IPs.

q: A mobile app needs users to sign up and sign in, and then call AWS APIs directly with temporary, least-privilege credentials. Which Cognito combination provides both?
options: A Cognito user pool for authentication combined with a Cognito identity pool that vends temporary AWS credentials
A Cognito identity pool alone with developer-authenticated identities
IAM users created for each mobile user
An Application Load Balancer with OIDC authentication only
explain: User pools handle sign-up and sign-in while identity pools exchange the resulting tokens for temporary AWS credentials scoped by IAM roles. An identity pool alone has no built-in user directory; per-user IAM users do not scale and cannot be federated to mobile sign-in; ALB authentication protects the ALB but does not vend AWS credentials to the app.

q: A database password is stored in AWS Secrets Manager and must be rotated every 30 days without application downtime or code changes. Which approach meets this?
options: Store the password in Systems Manager Parameter Store as a SecureString and rotate it manually
Enable automatic rotation in Secrets Manager with a Lambda rotation function, using the staged AWSCURRENT/AWSPENDING version pattern so applications pick up the new secret safely
Embed the password in the application configuration and redeploy monthly
Rotate the password in the database and update the secret in a maintenance window
explain: Secrets Manager rotation uses a Lambda function and staged secret versions so the database credential changes while applications continue reading the current version until cutover. Parameter Store SecureString has no built-in rotation; embedded credentials require redeploys and risk downtime; manual rotation in a maintenance window defeats the zero-downtime requirement.

q: Three teams share one S3 bucket but each team needs its own access policy with a distinct prefix and its own CloudWatch metrics. Creating separate buckets is not allowed. Which S3 feature provides per-team endpoints with independent policies?
options: Three separate IAM roles with path-based conditions
S3 Replication to team-specific prefixes
S3 Access Points, each with its own policy, prefix scope, and metrics
S3 Object Lambda access points for each team
explain: S3 Access Points provide named endpoints on a shared bucket, each with its own access policy and metrics, delegating per-team control without new buckets. IAM roles alone cannot scope prefixes with separate metrics; replication copies data rather than scoping access; Object Lambda transforms retrieved data instead of providing policy endpoints.

q: A VPC has private subnets in three Availability Zones but only one NAT Gateway, placed in us-east-1a. Traffic from the other two AZs crosses Availability Zone boundaries to reach it. Which change removes the cross-AZ data-transfer charges on NAT traffic?
options: Enable enhanced networking on the instances
Deploy one NAT Gateway per Availability Zone so each subnet routes locally
Replace the NAT Gateway with an internet gateway
Move all workloads into a single Availability Zone
explain: A NAT Gateway in each AZ keeps NAT traffic zonal, eliminating the per-GB cross-AZ charge incurred when subnets use a NAT Gateway in another AZ. Enhanced networking improves throughput, not routing charges; an internet gateway cannot serve private subnets; consolidating to one AZ sacrifices high availability.

q: A compliance archive must retain objects for seven years, with retrieval expected at most once or twice per year and a 12-hour retrieval window acceptable. Which is the lowest-cost S3 strategy?
options: A lifecycle rule transitioning objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost storage class for rarely accessed long-term data
S3 Standard with versioning for the full seven years
S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive tiers disabled
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for all objects
explain: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 storage class and its 12-to-48-hour retrieval window fits the stated tolerance. S3 Standard for seven years is far more expensive; Intelligent-Tiering without archive tiers never reaches the cheapest tiers; Glacier Instant Retrieval costs more per GB for millisecond access the workload does not need.

q: A company suspects many EC2 instances are over-provisioned but does not want to guess at smaller sizes manually. Which AWS service analyzes utilization and recommends optimal instance types?
options: AWS Cost Explorer rightsizing reports only
AWS Compute Optimizer, which uses machine learning on CloudWatch metrics to recommend instance types and sizes
AWS Budgets with utilization alerts
Amazon CloudWatch anomaly detection alarms
explain: Compute Optimizer analyzes historical utilization with machine learning and recommends specific instance types, including Graviton options. Cost Explorer shows spend but does not recommend sizes; Budgets alert on spend thresholds; CloudWatch anomaly detection flags metric deviations rather than recommending instance types.

q: A compute-heavy batch workload runs on x86 EC2 instances. The team wants better price-performance without changing instance count or rewriting code, and the application already supports ARM. Which change delivers this?
options: Switching to larger x86 instance types
Moving the workload to On-Demand from Reserved Instances
Migrating to Graviton-based instances, which offer better price-performance for compatible workloads
Enabling detailed CloudWatch monitoring
explain: Graviton ARM-based instances deliver better price-performance than comparable x86 instances for compatible workloads with no code rewrite needed here. Larger x86 instances increase cost; moving from RIs to On-Demand raises cost; detailed monitoring improves visibility but does not change the price-performance ratio.

q: A finance team wants to be notified when any service's spend deviates unusually from its established pattern, without setting static thresholds for every service. Which capability does this?
options: AWS Budgets with a fixed monthly threshold per service
The AWS Cost and Usage Report with daily delivery
CloudWatch billing alarms on total estimated charges
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection, which uses machine learning to flag unusual spend without static thresholds
explain: Cost Anomaly Detection learns spend patterns per service and alerts on deviations, eliminating per-service static thresholds. Fixed Budgets thresholds require manual tuning per service; CUR provides data without alerting; CloudWatch billing alarms watch total estimated charges against one threshold.

q: A bucket holds 50 million tiny objects averaging 10 KB each, accessed unpredictably. The team considers S3 Intelligent-Tiering but worries about the per-object monitoring fee. What is the correct cost guidance?
options: Intelligent-Tiering is ideal because monitoring fees are waived for objects under 128 KB
S3 Intelligent-Tiering charges a small monthly per-object monitoring fee, so for tens of millions of tiny objects the fee can exceed the storage savings and Standard may be cheaper
Intelligent-Tiering has no per-object fees of any kind
Lifecycle rules cannot move objects smaller than 128 KB
explain: Intelligent-Tiering adds a monthly monitoring and automation fee per object, which can outweigh storage savings when objects are tiny and numerous, making Standard the cheaper choice. Fees are not waived for small objects; claiming zero per-object fees is incorrect; lifecycle transitions work regardless of object size.

q: A serverless application uses Lambda functions that open thousands of short-lived connections to Aurora PostgreSQL during traffic spikes. The database CPU saturates from connection churn, and failovers take minutes to drain. Which service addresses both problems?
options: Amazon RDS Proxy, which pools and multiplexes database connections and fails over faster by preserving the proxy endpoint
Adding more Aurora read replicas
Increasing the max_connections parameter on the writer
Moving the Lambda functions into a VPC with larger subnets
explain: RDS Proxy pools connections and multiplexes them to the database, absorbing Lambda connection storms, and its stable endpoint with faster failover cuts recovery time. More read replicas do not reduce connection churn on the writer; raising max_connections worsens CPU contention; VPC subnet sizing is unrelated to connection overhead.

q: A healthcare company must retain financial records in S3 for seven years such that no one, including account administrators, can delete or overwrite them before the retention period ends. Which S3 feature enforces this?
options: S3 Versioning with cross-Region replication
S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode with a seven-year retention period
S3 server-side encryption with KMS
An S3 lifecycle rule expiring objects after seven years
explain: Object Lock Compliance mode makes objects immutable for the retention period, blocking deletion even by administrators. Versioning preserves prior versions but still allows deletes; SSE-KMS encrypts without preventing deletion; a lifecycle expiration rule deletes objects rather than protecting them.

q: A shopping cart service on DynamoDB must serve reads and writes from both us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with single-digit-millisecond latency, and stay available for local traffic if one Region fails. Which DynamoDB feature provides active-active multi-Region tables?
options: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
DynamoDB Streams with Lambda triggers
DynamoDB global tables, which replicate tables across Regions with active-active reads and writes
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in each Region
explain: Global tables replicate DynamoDB tables across Regions with multi-active reads and writes and automatic conflict resolution. Point-in-time recovery restores to a past state; Streams capture changes for processing, not multi-Region serving; DAX caches reads but does not replicate writes across Regions.

q: A company is lifting an application that depends on the MQTT and AMQP protocols to AWS and wants a managed message broker without rewriting the messaging layer. Which service fits?
options: Amazon SQS standard queues
Amazon SNS topics
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon MQ, a managed broker supporting ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ engines with native MQTT and AMQP support
explain: Amazon MQ provides managed ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ brokers, preserving MQTT/AMQP protocol compatibility without code changes. SQS and SNS use AWS-native APIs, not MQTT/AMQP; Kinesis is a streaming data service, not a message broker with these protocols.

q: A company with 25 AWS accounts needs centralized, policy-driven backups of EC2, RDS, EFS, and DynamoDB with copies replicated to a second Region and backup vaults isolated from production accounts. Which approach meets this?
options: AWS Backup with a centralized backup vault, organization-wide backup policies, and cross-Region copy rules
Manual EBS snapshots in each account with no replication
S3 Versioning on all data stores
CloudFormation StackSets deploying cron jobs that call snapshot APIs
explain: AWS Backup centralizes backup policies across accounts and services, supports cross-Region copies, and isolates vaults from production accounts. Manual snapshots do not scale across 25 accounts; versioning only applies to S3; custom cron jobs reimplement what Backup provides natively with less reliability.

q: A hybrid application has EC2 instances in a VPC that must resolve on-premises DNS names, while on-premises servers must resolve private AWS DNS names. Which Route 53 Resolver setup enables both directions?
options: A Route 53 private hosted zone shared with the on-premises network
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint for VPC-to-on-premises queries and an outbound endpoint with forwarding rules for on-premises-to-VPC queries
A public hosted zone with the private DNS records
VPC peering between the VPC and the on-premises network
explain: Resolver inbound endpoints let on-premises DNS forward queries into the VPC, while outbound endpoints with forwarding rules send VPC queries for on-premises domains to corporate DNS servers. A private hosted zone alone is not reachable from on-premises; public zones would expose private names; VPC peering connects VPCs, not on-premises networks.

q: A real-time bidding cache on ElastiCache for Redis has outgrown a single primary node. The workload needs horizontal scaling of both reads and writes beyond one node's capacity. Which Redis deployment supports this?
options: A single Redis primary with five read replicas
Redis with Multi-AZ automatic failover
Redis Sentinel managed manually on EC2
Redis Cluster mode enabled, which shards data across multiple primary nodes for horizontal scaling
explain: Cluster mode shards the keyspace across multiple primaries, scaling both read and write throughput horizontally. Read replicas scale reads only and still route all writes to one primary; Multi-AZ adds failover, not capacity; self-managed Sentinel adds operational burden without native sharding.

q: A training platform serves thousands of private video files per user session through CloudFront. Generating a unique signed URL per file adds significant overhead. Which approach authorizes the whole session efficiently?
options: CloudFront signed cookies, which grant access to multiple files with a single signed policy
A signed URL per file generated at login time
Origin Access Control with no signed URLs
Making the S3 bucket public with randomized object keys
