explain: Signed cookies apply one signed policy to many URLs, so a session authorizes thousands of files without per-file signing. Per-file signed URLs multiply signing work; OAC secures the S3 origin but does not authorize viewers; public buckets with random keys rely on obscurity, not authorization.

q: A log-ingestion workload writes large sequential batches to EBS and needs up to 1,000 MiB/s of throughput on a 500 GB volume without paying for unneeded IOPS. Which volume configuration fits?
options: io2 with 64,000 provisioned IOPS
gp3 with throughput provisioned independently up to 1,000 MiB/s, decoupled from IOPS and volume size
st1 with maximum volume size
gp2 relying on burst credits
explain: gp3 lets throughput be provisioned independently up to 1,000 MiB/s regardless of volume size, matching a throughput-heavy workload without overpaying for IOPS. io2 charges for provisioned IOPS the workload does not need; st1 is HDD with higher latency; gp2 throughput scales with size and depends on burst balance.

q: A DynamoDB table faces unpredictable traffic spikes. The team wants automatic capacity adjustment with no throttling during spikes and no manual intervention, and cost is secondary to hands-off operation. Which capacity mode fits?
options: Provisioned capacity with fixed read and write units
Provisioned capacity with Application Auto Scaling
Reserved capacity for the baseline
DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode, which instantly accommodates traffic spikes with no capacity planning
explain: On-demand mode scales instantly to any traffic level with zero capacity management, eliminating throttling during unpredictable spikes. Fixed provisioned capacity throttles above its limit; auto scaling reacts with delay and can still throttle on sudden spikes; reserved capacity only discounts a known baseline.

q: A machine-learning team trains models on 200 TB of image data stored in S3. Training jobs need POSIX file access with very high aggregate throughput, and the dataset changes weekly. Which storage service fits best?
options: Amazon EFS with Max I/O mode
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to the S3 bucket, presenting the dataset as a high-throughput POSIX file system
Amazon EBS io2 volumes attached to each training instance
explain: FSx for Lustre provides a high-throughput parallel POSIX file system and can link directly to S3, lazily loading the dataset for training. EFS Max I/O suits general file workloads but not parallel HPC throughput; FSx for Windows is SMB-based; attaching io2 volumes per instance requires copying 200 TB to each.

q: A high-frequency trading gateway must handle millions of TCP connections per second with fixed source IP addresses for counterparty allow-listing. Which load balancer type is designed for this?
options: Network Load Balancer, which operates at Layer 4 with ultra-low latency, static IPs via Elastic IP assignment, and massive connection scale
Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions
Gateway Load Balancer with a firewall appliance fleet
Classic Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing
explain: NLB handles millions of Layer 4 connections with static IPs and minimal latency, matching the trading gateway's needs. ALB operates at Layer 7 with dynamic IPs and higher latency; Gateway Load Balancer inserts third-party appliances unnecessarily; Classic Load Balancer is legacy with lower scale limits.

q: A security team suspects several IAM roles have accumulated permissions they no longer use. They want evidence-based findings identifying unused permissions to drive least-privilege cleanup. Which service provides this?
options: AWS CloudTrail Insights
AWS Config managed rules
Amazon GuardDuty
IAM Access Analyzer unused access findings, which identify unused IAM permissions and roles
explain: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes access activity and generates findings for unused permissions, roles, and credentials to guide least-privilege reductions. CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity; Config rules check configuration compliance; GuardDuty detects threats, not permission hygiene.

q: A company wants continuous monitoring that alerts when an EC2 instance starts communicating with a known malicious IP or begins crypto-mining. Which service provides this threat detection?
options: Amazon Inspector
Amazon GuardDuty, which analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events for malicious activity
AWS WAF
AWS Security Hub
explain: GuardDuty is the threat-detection service that correlates flow, DNS, and CloudTrail data to find compromised instances, malicious IPs, and crypto-mining. Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities rather than active threats; WAF filters web traffic; Security Hub aggregates findings from services like GuardDuty but does not generate them.

q: A team deploys container images to ECR and Lambda functions weekly and needs continuous scanning for known software vulnerabilities in both. Which service covers EC2, ECR images, and Lambda functions?
options: Amazon Macie
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector, which continuously scans EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
explain: Inspector provides continuous vulnerability assessment across EC2, ECR images, and Lambda functions. Macie classifies sensitive data in S3; Config tracks resource configuration; Patch Manager applies OS patches but does not scan container images or Lambda code for CVEs.

q: A CISO wants a single pane of glass aggregating security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie, with compliance checks against the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Which service provides this?
options: AWS CloudTrail Lake
Amazon Detective
AWS Config conformance packs alone
AWS Security Hub, which aggregates findings and runs automated CIS and PCI DSS compliance checks
explain: Security Hub centralizes findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and others, and evaluates them against standards like CIS AWS Foundations. CloudTrail Lake queries audit logs; Detective investigates findings but does not aggregate them; Config conformance packs check configuration, not multi-service security findings.

q: Microservices inside a VPC need mutual TLS between each other using short-lived certificates issued by an internal authority the company controls. Which AWS service provides the private certificate authority?
options: AWS Certificate Manager Private CA, which issues private certificates for internal mTLS
ACM public certificates
AWS Secrets Manager
IAM server certificates
explain: ACM Private CA operates a private certificate authority for issuing internal certificates used in mTLS between services. ACM public certificates are only for publicly trusted domains; Secrets Manager stores secrets rather than issuing certificates; IAM server certificates are a legacy deployment mechanism, not a CA.

q: After a suspected breach, incident responders need a record of every network connection attempt, including rejected traffic, between instances in a VPC over the past week. Which VPC feature provides this network-level forensic data?
options: Security group logs
CloudTrail data events
VPC Flow Logs, which capture accepted and rejected IP traffic for network interfaces
Route 53 query logs
explain: VPC Flow Logs record allowed and denied IP flows at the network interface, subnet, or VPC level for forensic analysis. Security groups do not produce logs; CloudTrail records API calls, not packets; Route 53 query logs show DNS lookups only.

q: A company has an on-premises Active Directory and wants EC2-hosted applications to authenticate users against it without replicating the directory to AWS. Which Directory Service option fits with least operational overhead?
options: AD Connector, a directory gateway that proxies authentication requests to the on-premises Active Directory
AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust
Simple AD as a standalone directory
AWS IAM Identity Center with no directory connection
explain: AD Connector forwards sign-in requests to the existing on-premises AD without syncing or hosting directory data in AWS, minimizing operational overhead. Managed Microsoft AD with a trust works but runs a full directory in AWS; Simple AD is a standalone Samba directory, not a proxy; Identity Center without a directory connection cannot reach the on-premises users.

q: A fault-tolerant batch rendering job can tolerate interruptions and runs for 6 hours nightly. The team wants the lowest EC2 cost while avoiding mass simultaneous interruptions. Which Spot strategy fits?
options: A single Spot Instance type in one Availability Zone
Spot Fleet with the lowest-price allocation strategy on one instance type
On-Demand Instances with a Savings Plan
A diversified set of Spot Instance types across Availability Zones using the capacity-optimized allocation strategy
explain: Diversifying across instance types and AZs with the capacity-optimized strategy spreads interruption risk and finds the deepest spare capacity pools. A single type in one AZ concentrates interruption risk; lowest-price strategy chases the cheapest pool, which is often the first reclaimed; On-Demand forfeits Spot discounts for a workload that tolerates interruptions.

q: A company cannot attribute AWS spend to individual teams because resources are tagged inconsistently across 40 accounts. Which combination enforces consistent tagging and enables team-level cost breakdowns?
options: Activate cost allocation tags in the billing console and enforce required tags with tag policies in AWS Organizations
Rely on AWS Cost Explorer resource grouping without enabling any tags
Use service control policies (SCPs) to mandate tag values on resource creation
Export the Cost and Usage Report and manually map resources to teams in a spreadsheet
explain: Tag policies enforce which tags (and allowed values) must be present on resources across the organization, and activating them as cost allocation tags makes them appear in billing for team-level attribution. Cost Explorer cannot group by tags that do not exist; SCPs restrict permissions but do not enforce tagging; manual spreadsheet mapping does not scale across 40 accounts.

q: Development EC2 instances sit idle every night and weekend but engineers forget to stop them. Which solution automatically stops and starts them on a schedule with minimal effort?
options: Manually stopping instances via the console each evening
Auto Scaling scheduled actions scaling to zero
AWS Instance Scheduler, which stops and starts EC2 and RDS instances on defined schedules
Converting the instances to Spot
explain: Instance Scheduler automates start/stop schedules for EC2 and RDS, eliminating idle spend without manual effort. Manual stops depend on human discipline; Auto Scaling scheduled actions work but require per-group setup and do not cover RDS; Spot reduces hourly cost but instances still run and accrue charges overnight.

q: A data pipeline replicates 30 TB per month from S3 in us-east-1 to S3 in eu-west-1, and inter-Region transfer dominates the storage bill. The analytics team only queries the data from us-east-1. What is the most cost-effective change?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the destination bucket
Use S3 Batch Replication instead of live replication
Compress the objects before replication
Stop the cross-Region replication and keep a single copy in us-east-1, since nothing consumes the eu-west-1 copy
explain: If no workload reads the eu-west-1 copy, the replication serves no purpose and removing it eliminates the inter-Region transfer charge entirely. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads but does not reduce replication transfer costs; Batch Replication still copies the data; compression reduces but does not eliminate a transfer nobody needs.

q: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster has steady, predictable production traffic and the team expects it to run for the next two years. Which purchase most reduces the database cost?
options: Aurora read replicas on On-Demand
Aurora I/O-Optimized cluster storage configuration
Reserved Instances for the Aurora DB instances matching the steady baseline
Aurora Serverless v2 with aggressive scaling
explain: Reserved Instances discount steady-state Aurora capacity for a one- or three-year term, fitting the predictable two-year horizon. On-Demand replicas add cost; I/O-Optimized helps I/O-heavy variable workloads rather than steady baselines; Serverless v2 suits variable workloads and can cost more for constant load.

q: A fleet of gp2 volumes is consistently hitting burst-balance limits. The team wants to eliminate burst throttling and lower cost at the same time. Which migration achieves both?
options: Over-provision gp2 volume sizes to gain baseline IOPS
Migrate the volumes to gp3, which provides a 3,000 IOPS baseline regardless of size at a lower price per GB than gp2
Migrate the volumes to io1 with provisioned IOPS
Add more gp2 volumes and stripe them with RAID 0
explain: gp3 starts at a 3,000 IOPS baseline independent of volume size and costs less per GB than gp2, removing burst-balance throttling while cutting spend. Over-provisioning gp2 pays for unused capacity; io1 adds provisioned-IOPS cost for a workload that only needs baseline performance; striping more gp2 volumes multiplies cost and complexity.

q: A company runs production EC2 workloads in us-east-1 and needs the ability to rebuild them in eu-west-1 after a Regional disaster. The AMIs and data volumes change weekly. Which backup approach enables a cross-Region rebuild?
options: Copy EBS snapshots and AMIs to eu-west-1 on a schedule, so instances can be launched from the copied images
Enable EBS encryption by default in us-east-1
Share the us-east-1 AMIs publicly so they resolve in eu-west-1
Rely on instance store volumes, which persist across Regions
explain: Copying snapshots and AMIs cross-Region on a schedule creates ready-to-launch images in the DR Region. Default encryption does not copy anything; public AMIs do not replicate across Regions and would expose the images; instance store volumes are ephemeral and Regional.

q: A developer accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table containing three months of order data. The table had no backups configured beyond default settings. What is the fastest path to recover the data?
options: Restore from the cross-Region replica of the table
Use DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR), which is enabled by default on new tables and retains 35 days of history
Replay the DynamoDB Streams records from the past three months
Contact AWS Support to restore the underlying storage
explain: PITR is enabled by default on newly created DynamoDB tables and keeps 35 days of continuous backups, allowing restore to any second within the window. There is no replica without global tables; Streams retain only 24 hours; AWS Support cannot recover deleted table data beyond PITR.

q: A public API backed by Lambda occasionally receives traffic bursts that overwhelm downstream capacity and cause cascading failures. Which API Gateway features protect the backend during bursts?
options: Enabling CORS on all resources
Deploying the API to a second stage
Throttling with usage plans and per-method rate limits, which cap request rates before they reach the backend
Increasing the Lambda memory allocation
explain: API Gateway throttling and usage plans cap request rates at the edge, shielding the backend from bursts. CORS governs browser cross-origin access, not load; a second stage duplicates rather than protects; more Lambda memory does not limit inbound request rates.

q: A compliance workload replicates S3 objects to a second Region and the auditor requires proof that 99.9% of objects replicate within 15 minutes. Which S3 replication feature provides this SLA?
options: Standard S3 Cross-Region Replication without additional configuration
S3 Replication Time Control (RTC), which provides a 15-minute replication SLA backed by CloudWatch metrics
S3 Batch Replication run hourly
S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket
explain: S3 Replication Time Control adds a 15-minute replication SLA with metrics and event notifications for compliance reporting. Standard replication offers no time SLA; Batch Replication is a one-time or scheduled job, not continuous with an SLA; Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads into S3, not replication between buckets.

q: A Lambda function processes records from a Kinesis data stream. One malformed record causes the entire batch to retry repeatedly, blocking all subsequent records. Which event source mapping feature isolates the bad record?
options: Bisect batch on function error, which splits the failing batch so the poisoned record is isolated and the rest proceed
Increasing the batch size to 10,000 records
Disabling the event source mapping and polling manually
Setting the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes
explain: Bisect-on-error recursively splits a failing batch until the bad record is isolated, letting good records process instead of blocking the shard. Larger batches worsen the blast radius; manual polling abandons managed scaling and checkpointing; a longer timeout does not fix a record that always fails.

q: A company connects its data center to AWS with a Site-to-Site VPN and needs the connection to survive the failure of any single tunnel or customer gateway device. Which design provides this resilience?
options: A single VPN tunnel with DPD enabled
A Site-to-Site VPN with two tunnels in different Availability Zones, BGP routing, and redundant customer gateway devices using active/active or active/passive failover
A client VPN endpoint for each user
A Direct Connect public VIF as the only path
explain: AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides two tunnels across AZs, and pairing them with redundant customer gateways and BGP delivers automatic failover at every layer. A single tunnel is a single point of failure; Client VPN serves remote users, not site connectivity; a public VIF alone is neither encrypted nor redundant.

q: A latency-sensitive API runs on Lambda and suffers cold starts of several seconds during sudden traffic spikes. The team needs consistent low latency without rewriting the function. Which Lambda feature addresses cold starts?
options: Increasing the function timeout
Lambda SnapStart for all runtimes
Provisioned concurrency, which keeps initialized execution environments ready to serve requests immediately
Reserved concurrency set to zero
explain: Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes execution environments so spikes are served without cold starts. Timeout changes do not affect initialization; SnapStart currently supports only Java (and select runtimes), not all; reserved concurrency of zero would block all invocations.

q: A Java-based Lambda function experiences long cold starts due to JVM initialization. The team wants faster startup with minimal code changes. Which feature is designed for this?
options: Increasing the Lambda memory to 10 GB
Moving the function to Fargate
Enabling active tracing with X-Ray
Lambda SnapStart, which snapshots an initialized JVM and restores it for fast cold starts
explain: SnapStart captures a snapshot of the initialized execution environment and restores it, cutting Java cold-start latency dramatically. More memory speeds execution but does not eliminate JVM init; Fargate changes the compute model entirely; X-Ray adds observability overhead rather than reducing startup time.

q: A video-transcoding file system sees huge throughput spikes for a few hours each day but sits nearly idle overnight. The team wants throughput to scale automatically with usage and to pay only for what they use. Which EFS throughput mode fits?
options: Bursting throughput mode
Provisioned throughput mode
Max I/O mode
Elastic throughput mode, which automatically scales throughput up and down with the workload
explain: Elastic throughput scales automatically with actual usage, matching spiky workloads without provisioning or paying for idle capacity. Bursting throughput ties throughput to stored data size; Provisioned mode requires pre-allocating capacity; Max I/O increases aggregate limits but does not auto-scale with demand.

q: A reporting application queries Aurora PostgreSQL heavily during business hours but is nearly idle overnight. The team wants the database to scale compute automatically with demand and scale to zero-ish minimums when idle. Which Aurora option fits?
options: Aurora provisioned clusters with scheduled scaling
Aurora Global Database
Aurora Backtrack
Aurora Serverless v2, which scales capacity up and down automatically based on demand
explain: Aurora Serverless v2 automatically adjusts capacity to demand, scaling down during idle periods without manual intervention. Scheduled scaling on provisioned clusters requires predicting the pattern; Global Database addresses multi-Region DR; Backtrack rewinds data in time.

q: A genomics company runs tens of thousands of short-lived batch jobs daily with varying CPU and memory needs. They want jobs scheduled automatically onto right-sized capacity without managing clusters. Which service fits?
options: AWS Batch, which dynamically provisions optimal compute resources and schedules batch jobs
A fixed Auto Scaling group of identical instances
AWS Lambda with 15-minute functions for every job
Amazon EMR long-running clusters
explain: AWS Batch plans, schedules, and executes batch workloads on dynamically provisioned compute matched to each job's needs. A fixed ASG cannot right-size per job; Lambda caps at 15 minutes and suits events, not batch HPC; long-running EMR clusters idle between jobs.

q: A company must encrypt 40 million existing S3 objects with SSE-KMS and add a legal-hold tag to each. Doing this object by object from EC2 would take weeks. Which S3 feature performs this at scale?
options: S3 Inventory reports
S3 Select queries run in a loop
S3 Batch Operations, which run copy or tagging jobs across billions of objects with a manifest
S3 Transfer Acceleration
explain: S3 Batch Operations executes large-scale operations like encryption changes and tagging across billions of objects from a manifest. S3 Select queries object content rather than transforming objects; Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads; Inventory lists objects but performs no actions.

q: A government contractor must use dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules for key storage to meet a contractual requirement that multi-tenant KMS does not satisfy. Which AWS service provides dedicated HSMs?
options: AWS Certificate Manager
AWS KMS with custom key stores
AWS CloudHSM, which provides dedicated single-tenant HSM instances in a VPC
AWS Secrets Manager
explain: CloudHSM provisions dedicated, single-tenant HSM appliances for customers who cannot use multi-tenant key management. KMS custom key stores still use multi-tenant KMS backed by CloudHSM, which may not satisfy the strictest single-tenancy wording; Secrets Manager stores secrets; ACM manages certificates.

q: An on-premises application running outside AWS needs to call AWS APIs using temporary credentials tied to an IAM role, without storing long-term access keys. Which IAM capability enables this?
options: IAM access keys rotated weekly
Cognito identity pools with unauthenticated access
IAM instance profiles
IAM Roles Anywhere, which lets workloads outside AWS obtain temporary credentials using X.509 certificates
explain: IAM Roles Anywhere allows on-premises servers and other external workloads to assume IAM roles with X.509 certificates, receiving temporary credentials with no long-term keys. Instance profiles only work on EC2; rotating access keys still leaves long-term credentials to manage; Cognito unauthenticated identities are for mobile/web clients, not server workloads.

q: A company must inspect all outbound VPC traffic and block connections to known malicious domains, with centralized rules applied across 30 accounts. Which service provides stateful network firewalling with centralized policy management?
options: Network ACLs on every subnet
AWS WAF on an internet-facing ALB
Security groups with outbound rules on each instance
AWS Network Firewall with AWS Firewall Manager policies distributed across the organization
explain: Network Firewall provides stateful L3-L7 inspection including domain-based filtering, and Firewall Manager centrally deploys its policies across accounts. Security groups are per-instance and lack domain filtering; NACLs are stateless and per-subnet; WAF protects inbound web traffic, not outbound VPC traffic.

q: A data lake bucket is accessed by multiple AWS accounts, and the bucket owner keeps losing control of objects uploaded by other accounts because the uploaders retain object ownership. Which S3 setting ensures the bucket owner owns all objects?
options: A bucket policy granting s3:* to everyone
Enabling S3 access logging
Enabling S3 Versioning
S3 Object Ownership set to Bucket owner enforced, which disables ACLs and gives the bucket owner full control of all objects
explain: Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs so the bucket owner automatically owns every object, regardless of which account uploaded it. Versioning preserves versions but not ownership; an open bucket policy is a security failure; access logging records requests without changing ownership.

q: A security team must enforce a baseline WAF rule set and a common set of security group rules across all 50 accounts in the organization, automatically remediating noncompliant resources. Which service centralizes this?
options: AWS Firewall Manager, which deploys and monitors WAF, security group, and firewall policies across accounts
AWS Config rules in each account
Manual CloudFormation templates shared by email
AWS Systems Manager Distributor
explain: Firewall Manager centrally defines WAF rules, security group policies, and Network Firewall policies and enforces them across organization accounts with automatic remediation. Per-account Config rules fragment management; emailed templates are not enforced; Systems Manager Distributor distributes software packages, not firewall policy.

q: A company wants to prevent EC2 instances from resolving known malicious domains as a defense against data exfiltration by malware. Which Route 53 Resolver feature blocks DNS queries to malicious domains?
options: Route 53 private hosted zones
Resolver inbound endpoints
Route 53 query logging
Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, which filters outbound DNS queries against managed threat domain lists
explain: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall inspects outbound DNS queries and blocks those matching threat-intelligence domain lists, stopping malware command-and-control resolution. Private hosted zones serve internal names; inbound endpoints receive queries from on-premises; query logging records DNS traffic without blocking it.

q: An analytics pipeline copies 20 TB per month from S3 in us-east-1 to EC2 instances in eu-west-1 for processing, incurring large inter-Region data-transfer charges. The data never leaves the pipeline. What is the most cost-effective fix?
options: Compress the data with a higher ratio
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket
Move the processing EC2 instances to us-east-1 so the data stays in-Region, where S3-to-EC2 transfer is free
Replicate the bucket with RTC to eu-west-1
explain: Data transfer between S3 and EC2 in the same Region is free, so co-locating processing with the data eliminates the inter-Region charge entirely. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads, not S3-to-EC2 reads; replication still pays inter-Region transfer; compression reduces but does not remove a charge caused purely by Region placement.

q: A company keeps seven years of EBS snapshots for compliance but restores from them only in rare audits. Snapshot storage costs keep growing. Which option most reduces long-term snapshot storage cost?
options: Increase the snapshot frequency
Convert the snapshots to AMIs
Move the rarely-accessed snapshots to EBS Snapshots Archive, a lower-cost tier for long-term retention
Copy the snapshots to a second Region
explain: EBS Snapshots Archive offers up to 75% lower storage cost for snapshots retained 90+ days that are rarely restored. AMIs reference snapshots without reducing their cost; cross-Region copies add storage cost; more frequent snapshots increase cost.

q: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster has highly variable I/O: quiet most of the month with intense batch windows. I/O charges under standard pricing spike during batch windows. Which cluster configuration gives predictable billing for this pattern?
options: Aurora I/O-Optimized, which charges a higher hourly instance rate but eliminates per-million-request I/O charges
Aurora provisioned with more read replicas
Aurora Serverless v1
Disabling Aurora storage auto-scaling
explain: I/O-Optimized trades a higher instance hourly rate for zero per-request I/O charges, making billing predictable for I/O-spiky workloads. More replicas add instance cost without changing I/O pricing; Serverless v1 has pausing limitations and its own pricing quirks; storage auto-scaling settings do not affect I/O charges.

q: A logging bucket with versioning enabled has grown 10x in a year, and most of the growth is old noncurrent versions nobody reads. Which lifecycle configuration controls this cost?
options: Disabling versioning on the bucket
Enabling S3 Object Lock on the log prefix
A lifecycle rule expiring current versions after 30 days
Transitioning noncurrent versions to cheaper storage and eventually expiring them with NoncurrentVersionExpiration
explain: NoncurrentVersion transitions and expiration specifically target old versions, cutting storage cost while keeping the current log data intact. Expiring current versions deletes live logs; disabling versioning does not remove already-stored versions; Object Lock would prevent deletion, worsening the cost.

q: A Lambda-based image-processing pipeline costs more than expected. Analysis shows each invocation is allocated 3 GB of memory but uses under 500 MB, and duration dominates the bill. Which tuning most reduces cost?
options: Enabling provisioned concurrency
Increasing memory to 10 GB for faster execution
Rightsizing memory toward actual usage, since Lambda bills on allocated memory multiplied by duration
Moving the code to a larger deployment package
explain: Lambda pricing multiplies configured memory by execution duration, so cutting allocated memory to match actual usage directly lowers cost. Provisioned concurrency adds cost for always-warm environments; more memory raises the per-millisecond rate; a larger package increases cold starts without reducing cost.

q: A company ships application logs to CloudWatch Logs from 500 instances with no retention setting, and log storage costs grow every month. Which change caps the ongoing storage cost?
options: Enabling CloudWatch detailed monitoring
Exporting logs to S3 with no retention change
Setting a CloudWatch Logs retention period (for example 30 days) so old log events expire automatically
Increasing the log level to DEBUG on all instances
explain: CloudWatch Logs retains log events indefinitely by default, so setting a retention period automatically expires old data and caps storage cost. Detailed monitoring affects metrics, not logs; exporting to S3 without retention just moves the growth; DEBUG logging increases ingestion volume and cost.

q: A startup is choosing a Region for a new workload and notices identical EC2 and S3 usage would cost noticeably less in us-east-1 than in their default Region. Which cost-optimization principle does this illustrate?
options: Reserved Instance arbitrage across Regions
Choosing a lower-cost Region when data residency and latency requirements allow it
Consolidated billing discounts
Spot Instance diversification
explain: AWS service prices vary by Region, so deploying in a cheaper Region is a valid optimization when latency and data-residency constraints permit. Reserved Instances are Region-specific and cannot arbitrage; consolidated billing gives volume discounts, not Regional price differences; Spot diversification manages interruption risk, not Regional pricing.

q: A company connects its on-premises data center to AWS with Direct Connect. EC2 instances in a VPC must resolve hostnames in the on-premises DNS domain corp.example.com, while every other query should keep using the VPC's default resolver. Which solution meets this requirement with the least operational overhead?
options: Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC and configure the on-premises servers to forward corp.example.com queries to it
Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint in the VPC and add a forwarding rule for corp.example.com pointing to the on-premises DNS servers
Change the VPC DHCP options set to use the on-premises DNS server addresses for all queries
Create a Route 53 private hosted zone for corp.example.com and duplicate every on-premises record in it
explain: An outbound Resolver endpoint forwards VPC-originated queries for specific domains to on-premises DNS, leaving all other resolution untouched. An inbound endpoint serves the reverse direction (on-premises resolving AWS names). Replacing the DHCP options set breaks resolution of AWS-provided names, and duplicating records in a private hosted zone drifts out of sync with on-premises changes.

q: A fleet of application servers holds thousands of persistent connections to an Aurora MySQL cluster. During a recent Availability Zone failover, applications reconnected all at once, exhausted max_connections, and the outage lasted far longer than the failover itself. Which solution best shortens application recovery after future failovers?
options: Place an RDS Proxy in front of the cluster to pool connections and absorb the reconnect storm during failover
Raise the max_connections parameter on the cluster
Enable Aurora Backtrack on the cluster
Add an Aurora read replica in the same Availability Zone
explain: RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool between applications and the database, so failovers complete without thousands of simultaneous new connections overwhelming the cluster. Raising max_connections only delays exhaustion, Backtrack rewinds data to fix bad writes rather than managing connections, and a read replica does nothing to absorb a reconnect storm.

q: A company must retain 30 days of EBS snapshots for 200 production volumes, automatically deleting older snapshots. Snapshots must be tagged by environment and copied to a second Region for disaster recovery. Which solution meets these requirements with the least operational overhead?
options: Write a Lambda function invoked on a schedule that snapshots each volume and deletes snapshots older than 30 days
Enable fast snapshot restore on every production volume
Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager with a lifecycle policy defining a 30-day retention schedule, target tags, and cross-Region copy
Create AMIs of every instance nightly and deregister AMIs older than 30 days
explain: Data Lifecycle Manager natively schedules EBS snapshots, enforces retention, applies tags, and copies across Regions with no custom code. A Lambda scheduler reinvents this managed service, fast snapshot restore only speeds up volume creation from snapshots, and nightly AMIs are heavier than snapshots and add instance-level coupling.

q: An Auto Scaling group runs a stateless web tier behind an Application Load Balancer. The team must replace all instances with a new AMI, but the rollout must pause automatically for manual validation after half the fleet is replaced, and instances must deregister cleanly from the load balancer before termination. Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Terminate every instance at once and let the Auto Scaling group launch replacements
Suspend the ReplaceUnhealthy process and swap each instance by hand
Run a blue/green deployment by cloning the whole stack and switching Route 53 weights manually
Run an instance refresh with a checkpoint at 50% and a minimum healthy percentage, relying on the target group deregistration delay
explain: Instance refresh rolls the fleet to the new AMI and supports checkpoints that pause the rollout for validation, while the ALB target group deregistration delay drains in-flight requests before termination. Terminating everything causes an outage, manual swaps add operational burden, and a full blue/green clone is far heavier than the built-in rolling mechanism.

q: A media company stores user uploads in S3 buckets in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with bidirectional replication. During a Regional outage, reads and writes must automatically fail over to the healthy Region through a single global endpoint with health-based routing. Which solution should the architect choose?
options: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication and update the application configuration to point at the healthy Region during an outage
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket in each Region
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point with failover controls that route traffic to the healthy Region
Copy objects between Regions on a schedule with AWS DataSync
explain: S3 Multi-Region Access Points provide one global endpoint with active-passive failover controls driven by replication and health status, so traffic shifts without application changes. Cross-Region Replication alone still needs manual or application-driven failover, Transfer Acceleration only speeds uploads, and scheduled DataSync copies add replication lag and no routing.

q: A trading firm requires the highest possible resiliency for Direct Connect: the complete loss of one Direct Connect location must not interrupt traffic between its data center and AWS. Which design meets this requirement?
options: Provision two dedicated connections terminating at two different Direct Connect locations, each with independent routers and diverse fiber paths
Provision a single hosted connection and add a Site-to-Site VPN as a backup path
Provision two dedicated connections at the same Direct Connect location on separate routers
Use a single dedicated connection configured as a link aggregation group (LAG) across two ports
explain: Two connections at two separate Direct Connect locations is AWS's maximum-resiliency model and survives the loss of an entire location. A single hosted connection plus VPN still depends on one location's physical plant, two connections at the same location share its fate, and a LAG only protects against single-port or single-device failure.

q: A company runs its order database on Aurora PostgreSQL in us-east-1. The disaster recovery plan requires a cross-Region recovery point objective of about one second and a recovery time objective of under a minute for a Regional disaster. Which solution meets these objectives with the least operational overhead?
options: Restore the most recent automated snapshot in us-west-2 when a disaster is declared
Maintain an Aurora read replica with asynchronous replication in us-west-2
Export nightly snapshots to S3 with cross-Region replication enabled
Deploy an Aurora global database with a secondary cluster in us-west-2
explain: An Aurora global database replicates at the storage layer with typical lag under one second and promotes the secondary cluster in under a minute. Snapshot restores take hours and lose all data since the snapshot, asynchronous read replicas have larger and variable lag, and nightly exports have a 24-hour recovery point.

q: A genomics startup runs a nightly HPC pipeline that needs a high-throughput POSIX scratch filesystem. Input data is staged from S3, results are written back to S3, and the filesystem is discarded after each run. Which storage solution delivers the highest throughput with the least operational overhead?
options: Provision an EFS file system and copy data from S3 with DataSync before each run
Create an FSx for Lustre file system linked to the S3 bucket as its data repository, then delete it after the run
Attach io2 Block Express volumes to each compute node and stripe them with RAID 0
Read and write intermediate data directly in S3 Standard over HTTPS
explain: FSx for Lustre natively links an S3 bucket as its data repository, lazily loading inputs and writing results back, with throughput far beyond general file systems. EFS adds a separate copy step and lower scratch throughput, manual RAID striping adds failure domains and management, and S3 over HTTPS is not a POSIX filesystem for HPC tools.

q: A CloudFront distribution fronts a dynamic API. The team must inject a security header into every response and normalize one query parameter, with sub-millisecond execution at the edge and minimal cost. Which solution is the best fit?
options: Use Lambda@Edge functions on viewer request and origin response triggers
Perform the header injection and parameter normalization on the EC2 origin servers
Use CloudFront Functions for the header injection and query normalization
Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a Lambda target in every Region
explain: CloudFront Functions are designed for lightweight edge manipulations with sub-millisecond startup at a fraction of Lambda@Edge cost. Lambda@Edge suits heavier compute but is overkill here, origin-side logic adds latency for every edge location, and per-Region load balancers with Lambda targets are far more infrastructure than a header task needs.

q: An application performs heavy repeated reads against DynamoDB, and p99 read latency must drop from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds. Which solution meets the latency requirement?
options: Add DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table
Enable DynamoDB auto scaling on the table
Migrate the table to provisioned capacity with higher read capacity units
Add a global secondary index covering the read patterns
explain: DAX is an in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB that serves repeated reads in microseconds. Auto scaling and higher RCUs increase throughput, not per-request latency; a global secondary index changes query flexibility but reads still hit DynamoDB at millisecond latency.

q: An OLTP database on EC2 needs a sustained 120,000 IOPS from a single EBS volume with sub-millisecond latency. The team knows gp3 volumes top out at 16,000 IOPS. Which volume type meets the requirement?
options: Stripe eight gp3 volumes in RAID 0 to aggregate their IOPS
Use a Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volume
Use an EFS file system with provisioned throughput
Use an io2 Block Express volume provisioned at 120,000 IOPS
explain: io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS per volume with sub-millisecond latency, covering the requirement on one volume. RAID 0 across gp3 volumes multiplies failure domains and management overhead, st1 is a throughput HDD unsuitable for IOPS-heavy OLTP, and EFS is network file storage, not low-latency block storage.

q: A mobile app emits telemetry that swings from near zero overnight to 50,000 records per second during live events. The team wants to use Kinesis Data Streams without manually managing shard counts or paying for peak capacity around the clock. Which capacity mode should they choose?
options: Provisioned mode with enough shards for the 50,000-records-per-second peak
On-demand mode so stream capacity scales automatically with incoming throughput
Provisioned mode with a single shard, relying on automatic resharding
Replace Kinesis Data Streams with SQS FIFO queues
explain: On-demand mode scales Kinesis capacity up and down automatically, matching spiky telemetry without shard management or idle peak capacity. Provisioning for the peak wastes money overnight, a single shard throttles far below peak (and Kinesis does not auto-reshard), and SQS FIFO is a queueing service with different ordering and throughput semantics.

q: Users on every continent upload 2-10 GB video files to an application hosted in us-east-1. Uploads over the public internet are painfully slow for distant users. Which solution accelerates uploads with the least operational overhead?
options: Deploy EC2-based upload proxies in each Region
Ask large uploaders to ship drives using AWS Snowball
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the destination bucket
Order Direct Connect connections for the largest customer offices
explain: S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the CloudFront edge network to the bucket over optimized paths, with a single bucket setting. Per-Region proxies add fleets to manage, Snowball is for offline bulk ingest rather than interactive uploads, and Direct Connect only helps offices with a physical connection.

q: A Lambda function needs permission to decrypt data with a specific KMS key for the next 48 hours only. The security team will not modify the key policy. Which mechanism grants this temporary, narrowly scoped permission?
options: Add an IAM policy to the Lambda execution role allowing kms:Decrypt on the key
Create a second KMS key and share its ARN with the Lambda function
Attach an SCP that denies kms:Decrypt once 48 hours have passed
Create a KMS grant on the key for the Lambda role with decrypt rights, then retire the grant after 48 hours
explain: A KMS grant delegates specific key operations to a principal without editing the key policy and can be retired when the window closes. An IAM policy alone cannot authorize KMS use unless the key policy also permits it, a second key cannot decrypt data encrypted under the first, and SCPs cannot cleanly express a 48-hour expiry.

q: A company with 40 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations must prevent any IAM user or role, including account administrators, from creating resources outside us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Which control enforces this requirement?
options: Attach a permissions boundary to every IAM role in every account
Apply a service control policy at the organization root that denies actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not us-east-1 or eu-west-1
Enable AWS Config rules in each account that flag resources created in other Regions
Remove permissions for other Regions from each account's AdministratorAccess policy
explain: A service control policy at the root applies to every account and restricts even administrators, and the aws:RequestedRegion condition key makes the Region guardrail precise. Permissions boundaries are per-identity and do not constrain administrators, Config rules detect after the fact rather than prevent, and AWS managed policies like AdministratorAccess cannot be edited.

q: EC2 instances in private subnets reach S3 through a gateway VPC endpoint. The security team must ensure the instances can access only the company's logging bucket and no other S3 bucket. Where should this restriction be enforced?
options: Attach an endpoint policy to the gateway VPC endpoint allowing S3 actions only on the logging bucket ARN
Add a bucket policy to the logging bucket denying every other principal
Configure the instances' security groups to allow HTTPS only to the logging bucket
Enable S3 Block Public Access on the logging bucket
explain: An endpoint policy controls which S3 resources are reachable through that VPC endpoint, so scoping it to the logging bucket ARN blocks access to all other buckets. A bucket policy on the logging bucket cannot restrict access to other buckets, security groups filter by IP and port rather than bucket name, and Block Public Access only governs public access.

q: A CloudFront distribution serves private content from an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS. The legacy setup used Origin Access Identity (OAI), and CloudFront now returns 403 errors on every object. Which fix restores access while keeping SSE-KMS?
options: Add the OAI canonical user ID to the KMS key policy
Change the bucket's default encryption from SSE-KMS to SSE-S3
Migrate the origin from OAI to Origin Access Control (OAC), which supports SigV4 and SSE-KMS origins
Make the S3 objects public and protect them with signed URLs instead
explain: Origin Access Control signs origin requests with SigV4 and supports SSE-KMS encrypted origins, while OAI does not, so migrating to OAC fixes the 403s. Adding the OAI to the key policy cannot overcome the OAI protocol limitation, switching to SSE-S3 weakens the encryption posture the team chose, and public objects defeat the private-content requirement.

q: A company stores database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Teams rotate them manually every 90 days, and missed rotations have caused outages. Which solution automates rotation with the least operational overhead?
options: Move the credentials to Systems Manager Parameter Store and trigger rotation with an EventBridge schedule
Send the team a calendar reminder to rotate credentials every 90 days
Write a custom Lambda function that rewrites application configuration files with new credentials
Enable automatic rotation in Secrets Manager using the managed rotation function for the database engine
explain: Secrets Manager provides managed rotation functions for RDS and other engines that rotate credentials and update the secret atomically on a schedule. Parameter Store needs custom rotation logic, calendar reminders keep the manual process that already fails, and a hand-written Lambda duplicates what the managed rotation function already does.

q: During a quarterly access review, the security team must identify IAM principals holding permissions they have not used in the last 90 days, so policies can be tightened toward least privilege. Which service produces these findings automatically?
options: AWS CloudTrail Lake with custom SQL queries
AWS Config with managed rules
Amazon GuardDuty
IAM Access Analyzer unused access findings
explain: IAM Access Analyzer continuously analyzes access activity and reports unused permissions and roles for least-privilege reviews. CloudTrail Lake requires hand-built queries over raw events, Config evaluates resource compliance rather than permission usage, and GuardDuty detects threats like compromised credentials rather than over-broad policies.

q: VPC Flow Logs show large traffic volumes from private EC2 instances to S3 and DynamoDB traversing the NAT gateway, incurring per-GB NAT data processing charges. This traffic never needs the public internet. Which change eliminates the NAT data-processing charges for this traffic?
options: Create gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and point the private route tables at them
Replace the NAT gateway with a self-managed NAT instance
Move the EC2 instances into public subnets with public IP addresses
Enable enhanced networking on the EC2 instances
explain: Gateway VPC endpoints carry S3 and DynamoDB traffic privately at no data-processing charge, bypassing the NAT gateway entirely. A NAT instance still incurs hourly and data-transfer costs, public subnets expose the instances to the internet, and enhanced networking improves throughput, not NAT billing.

q: A rendering farm on x86 EC2 instances averages 70% utilization. The CFO wants roughly 40% better price-performance without changing instance counts, and the rendering software is already compiled for ARM64. Which action delivers this improvement?
options: Move the fleet to larger x86 instance types to improve bin-packing
Purchase Dedicated Hosts for the rendering farm
Buy On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the farm's Availability Zones
Migrate the fleet to Graviton-based instances of equivalent size
explain: Graviton (ARM64) instances deliver substantially better price-performance than comparable x86 instances, and the software already supports ARM64, so this is a drop-in win. Larger x86 instances raise cost without the architectural efficiency gain, Dedicated Hosts add a premium for compliance scenarios, and Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity rather than discounting it.

q: A data lake bucket holds 500 TB with unpredictable access patterns: some objects are read daily, others sit untouched for months, and patterns shift over time. The team wants storage costs optimized automatically without maintaining lifecycle rules. Which storage class should they use?
options: S3 Standard with a lifecycle policy transitioning objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 One Zone-IA for the entire bucket
S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the bucket
S3 Standard-IA for the entire bucket
explain: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors each object and moves it between frequent, infrequent, and archive tiers automatically, fitting unpredictable patterns with no rules to tune. Lifecycle policies need predictable age-based patterns, One Zone-IA sacrifices durability for the whole dataset, and Standard-IA penalizes the frequently read objects with retrieval fees.

q: A company runs EC2 across three Regions and several instance families, plus Fargate containers. They want a single commitment vehicle that applies flexibly across Regions, instance families, sizes, and Fargate. Which offers the broadest applicability?
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans
Standard Reserved Instances
Compute Savings Plans
Convertible Reserved Instances
explain: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 usage in any Region, family, and size, plus Fargate and Lambda, making them the most flexible commitment. EC2 Instance Savings Plans are Region-locked, Standard RIs are the most rigid, and Convertible RIs allow family changes but remain EC2-only.

q: An e-commerce database on provisioned Aurora PostgreSQL sees 10x traffic spikes during flash sales and idles the rest of the time. The team over-provisions for the peaks and pays for idle capacity. Which change best aligns cost with this spiky pattern?
options: Add Aurora read replicas that run continuously
Migrate to Aurora Serverless v2 so capacity scales automatically with demand
Purchase Reserved Instances sized for the peak capacity
Enable Aurora Backtrack to reduce storage costs
explain: Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity up for flash-sale spikes and down when idle, so the company pays for what it uses. Permanent read replicas add more always-on cost, reserving peak capacity locks in the over-provisioning, and Backtrack provides point-in-time rewind, not cost savings.

q: Compliance requires retaining audit logs for 5 years. Logs are written once, retrieved within milliseconds a few times per quarter for audits, and must stay immediately accessible. Which is the MOST cost-effective storage class?
options: S3 Standard
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 One Zone-IA
explain: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval offers millisecond access at archive pricing, matching quarterly audit retrievals with immediate access. S3 Standard is overpriced for rarely read data, Glacier Flexible Retrieval restores in minutes to hours which misses the millisecond need, and One Zone-IA costs more per GB than archive tiers while reducing durability.

q: A company runs its web application in us-east-1 behind an Application Load Balancer, with a smaller standby deployment in eu-west-1. If the primary Region becomes unhealthy, all DNS queries must resolve to the standby; otherwise all traffic must stay in us-east-1. Which Route 53 configuration meets this requirement?
options: Failover routing with health checks on the primary record pointing to the us-east-1 load balancer and a secondary record for eu-west-1
Latency-based routing between the two load balancers
Weighted routing with 100% weight on us-east-1 and 0% on eu-west-1
Geolocation routing sending all continents to us-east-1 except Europe
explain: Failover routing sends all traffic to the primary record while its health check passes and flips to the secondary only on failure, which is exactly active-passive DR. Latency-based routing splits by user location rather than health, weighted routing with zero weight does not react to failures, and geolocation routing divides by geography rather than availability.

q: A team deploys a Node.js application with Elastic Beanstalk. Deployments must never reduce serving capacity: new instances must pass health checks before any old instance is terminated, even if the deployment temporarily doubles the fleet. Which deployment policy meets this requirement?
options: All at once
Immutable
Rolling
Traffic splitting
explain: Immutable deployments launch a full parallel fleet, wait for health checks to pass, then swap and terminate the old fleet, so capacity never dips. All at once causes downtime, rolling replaces in batches and can briefly reduce capacity, and traffic splitting is for canary testing rather than guaranteed full-capacity replacement.

q: A company stores shared project files on EFS in us-east-1. The business continuity plan requires the file system to be recoverable in eu-west-1 within minutes of a Regional outage, with ongoing replication rather than periodic backups. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Enable EFS automatic backups in us-east-1
Copy the files to EBS snapshots on a daily schedule
Create an EFS replication destination in eu-west-1
Mount the same EFS file system from EC2 instances in eu-west-1
explain: EFS replication continuously replicates data to a destination file system in another Region, ready for fast failover. Automatic backups stay in the source Region and restore slowly, EBS snapshots are for block volumes rather than file systems, and a single EFS file system cannot be mounted across Regions.

q: A gaming company needs player session data readable and writable in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-2 with single-digit millisecond latency in each Region and automatic conflict resolution. Which DynamoDB feature provides this active-active design?
options: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
DynamoDB Streams with Lambda replication
On-demand capacity mode
DynamoDB global tables
explain: Global tables replicate across Regions with multi-active writes and last-writer-wins conflict resolution at local latency. DAX is a read cache, not multi-Region replication; Streams plus Lambda is a hand-built replicator with lag and no conflict handling; on-demand mode only changes capacity billing.

q: A background worker fleet polls an SQS standard queue. A malformed message keeps failing processing, and each retry consumes worker capacity while blocking nothing else but wasting money. The team wants failing messages quarantined automatically after three unsuccessful receives. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: Increase the queue's visibility timeout to 12 hours
Configure a dead-letter queue with a maxReceiveCount of 3 and a redrive policy on the source queue
Convert the queue to FIFO to preserve message order
Enable long polling on the queue
explain: A dead-letter queue with maxReceiveCount 3 moves poison messages aside automatically after three failed receives, freeing workers. A longer visibility timeout only delays each retry, FIFO changes ordering semantics without quarantining failures, and long polling reduces empty receives rather than handling bad messages.

q: After a ransomware incident at a peer company, a CTO requires that AWS Backup recovery points cannot be deleted or altered by anyone, including administrators, for 90 days. Which feature enforces this immutability?
options: Copying backups to a second Region
Encrypting the backup vault with a customer managed KMS key
Enabling Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode with a 90-day retention period
Attaching a restrictive vault access policy
explain: Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode makes recovery points immutable for the retention period, blocking deletion even by administrators or the root user. Cross-Region copies add durability, not immutability; KMS encryption protects confidentiality, not deletion; and vault access policies can be changed by administrators.

q: An application needs a simple in-memory cache for session data with no persistence, replication, or complex data structures. The team wants the lowest operational overhead for this straightforward caching need. Which ElastiCache engine should they choose?
options: Redis with Multi-AZ automatic failover
Redis with cluster mode enabled
Valkey with Global Datastore
Memcached
explain: Memcached is the purpose-built simple cache: multithreaded, no persistence, minimal configuration. Redis options add persistence, replication, and clustering features the workload does not need, increasing cost and complexity for zero benefit on a plain session cache.

q: A REST API on API Gateway fronts Lambda functions that run an expensive product-search query. The same searches repeat constantly, and the team wants to serve repeats without invoking Lambda or hitting the database. Which feature addresses this with the least effort?
options: Enable API Gateway caching on the search method with an appropriate TTL
Enable throttling on the search method
Attach AWS WAF to the API
Increase the Lambda function's memory allocation
explain: API Gateway caching stores responses at the edge of the API and serves repeats without invoking Lambda or the database. Throttling limits request rates rather than avoiding backend calls, WAF filters malicious traffic rather than caching, and more Lambda memory speeds one invocation but still pays for every repeat.

q: A data warehouse holds 60 TB of analytics data and keeps growing. Queries scan large fact tables nightly. The team wants to scale compute and storage independently and pay only for the managed storage they use. Which Redshift architecture fits?
options: DC2 nodes with local SSD storage
RA3 nodes with managed storage
Single-node DC2 cluster
Redshift Spectrum alone with no cluster
explain: RA3 nodes separate compute from managed storage, scaling each independently and billing storage separately, which suits a growing 60 TB warehouse. DC2 couples compute to local SSDs and caps storage per node, a single node cannot hold 60 TB, and Spectrum queries S3 data but still requires a cluster to run.

q: Three analyst teams share one Athena setup against the same S3 data lake. Finance needs per-team tracking of query spend and a hard cap on how much data any single query can scan. Which Athena feature provides both?
options: Creating a separate AWS account per team
Partitioning the S3 data by team
Athena workgroups with per-query data usage controls
Enabling S3 Inventory on the data lake
explain: Athena workgroups isolate query execution per team, expose per-workgroup metrics for cost tracking, and enforce limits on data scanned per query. Separate accounts are heavy-handed for cost allocation, partitioning improves scan efficiency but adds no spending caps, and S3 Inventory reports on objects rather than query spend.

q: A company is migrating an on-premises streaming platform built on the Kafka protocol, including custom producers that use Kafka client libraries and exactly-once semantics. Rewriting the producers is out of scope. Which AWS streaming service preserves Kafka compatibility?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon SQS FIFO queues
Amazon EventBridge
Amazon MSK
explain: Amazon MSK runs Apache Kafka, so existing Kafka producers, consumers, and client libraries work unchanged. Kinesis Data Streams uses its own API and would require rewriting producers, SQS FIFO is message queueing without the Kafka protocol, and EventBridge is an event bus, not a Kafka-compatible log.

q: A real-time multiplayer game uses UDP on custom ports and serves players worldwide from game servers in two Regions. The team needs static entry IPs and fast failover of players to the healthy Region without relying on DNS propagation. Which service meets these requirements?
options: AWS Global Accelerator
Amazon CloudFront
Application Load Balancer
Route 53 latency-based routing
explain: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs, routes UDP and TCP over the AWS backbone, and fails over between Regional endpoints on health checks without DNS delays. CloudFront is for HTTP(S) caching, ALBs are Regional and TCP/HTTP only, and latency-based DNS routing still depends on DNS TTL propagation during failover.

q: An HPC cluster runs MPI workloads where microsecond latency between nodes directly determines job completion time. All instances are the same type in one Availability Zone. Which placement strategy minimizes inter-node latency?
options: Spread placement group
Cluster placement group
Partition placement group
No placement group, letting EC2 choose freely
explain: A cluster placement group packs instances on adjacent hardware for the lowest network latency and highest bandwidth, which is what MPI needs. Spread places instances on distinct hardware for fault isolation at the cost of latency, partition groups by rack for correlated-failure isolation, and no placement group gives EC2 no locality hint.

q: A public API behind CloudFront is receiving an HTTP flood from thousands of rotating IP addresses, each staying just under naive per-IP limits. The team needs to block the flood at the edge based on request rate. Which control addresses this Layer 7 attack?
options: AWS Shield Advanced
Network ACLs on the origin subnets
A WAF rate-based rule on the CloudFront distribution
Security groups on the origin instances
explain: A WAF rate-based rule tracks request rates and blocks IPs exceeding the threshold, and on CloudFront it executes at the edge before traffic reaches the origin. Shield Advanced mitigates Layer 3/4 DDoS rather than HTTP floods, while NACLs and security groups filter by IP and port and cannot evaluate HTTP request rates.

q: The security team needs continuous monitoring that flags EC2 instances communicating with known malicious domains and detects cryptocurrency mining activity, without installing agents. Which service provides this threat detection?
options: AWS Security Hub
Amazon Inspector
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
explain: GuardDuty analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS query logs, and CloudTrail with threat intelligence to detect malicious domains and crypto mining, agentless. Security Hub aggregates findings rather than generating these detections, Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and Config tracks configuration compliance rather than runtime threats.

q: Compliance requires that every command administrators run on production EC2 instances be recorded and stored immutably for audit, with no SSH keys to manage and no inbound ports open. Which solution meets all three requirements?
options: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with session logging to S3
A bastion host with verbose SSH daemon logging
AWS Client VPN with connection logging
EC2 Instance Connect with CloudTrail enabled
explain: Session Manager needs no SSH keys or inbound ports, and its session logging streams full command output to S3 or CloudWatch Logs for immutable audit. A bastion still needs keys and open port 22, Client VPN logs connections rather than commands, and EC2 Instance Connect still uses SSH keys while CloudTrail only records the API call, not the session contents.

q: A media company keeps published video masters in S3 and wants to protect them from accidental deletion by its own engineers. Legal must retain the ability to shorten retention on specific objects with special permission. Which S3 Object Lock mode fits?
options: Compliance mode with a 1-year retention period
Governance mode, which blocks most users from deleting objects but allows users with special permission to override
S3 Versioning without Object Lock
S3 Lifecycle expiration policies
explain: Governance mode protects objects from deletion by most users while permitting authorized users to alter retention or delete, matching the legal-override need. Compliance mode blocks everyone including administrators, plain versioning still allows permanent deletion of versions, and lifecycle expiration automates deletion rather than preventing it.

q: After an acquisition, the parent company's private certificate authority must start issuing internal certificates for the subsidiary's services, but the offline root CA must never be brought online for day-to-day issuance. Which design meets this requirement?
options: Issue all subsidiary certificates directly from the root CA
Buy public ACM certificates for the subsidiary's internal hostnames
Create a subordinate CA under AWS Private CA for the subsidiary, chaining to the offline root
Have the subsidiary self-sign its certificates
explain: A subordinate CA under AWS Private CA issues day-to-day certificates that chain up to the offline root, preserving the root's security while delegating issuance. Using the root directly violates the offline requirement, public certificates do not belong on internal hostnames, and self-signed certificates create trust-distribution chaos.

q: A mobile app's users sign in with social identity providers. After sign-in, the app must call AWS APIs directly, such as uploading profile photos to S3, using temporary credentials scoped to each user. Which Cognito component issues those temporary AWS credentials?
options: Cognito user pools
Cognito Sync
AWS STS directly from the mobile app
Cognito identity pools
explain: Cognito identity pools (federated identities) exchange the user's authenticated identity for temporary, scoped AWS credentials. User pools handle authentication and JWT tokens but do not issue AWS credentials, Cognito Sync synchronizes data rather than credentials, and calling STS directly from the app would require embedding long-lived credentials.

q: A nightly batch job runs for 4 hours on 200 EC2 instances and tolerates interruptions because completed chunks checkpoint to S3. The team wants the lowest compute price and must survive the loss of any single Spot capacity pool. Which strategy is best?
options: Run the fleet as Spot Instances diversified across many instance types, sizes, and Availability Zones
Run On-Demand Instances in a single Availability Zone
Use one Spot capacity pool with the cheapest instance type
Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the 200 instances
explain: Diversifying Spot across many pools means losing one pool only takes a fraction of capacity, while Spot pricing is the cheapest for interruption-tolerant batch work. On-Demand in one AZ is expensive and fragile, a single Spot pool is fully exposed to one interruption event, and Reserved Instances lock in a price for capacity that sits idle 20 hours a day.

q: A company runs fault-tolerant containerized workers on ECS with the Fargate launch type. The workers checkpoint progress and can be stopped and restarted safely. Which capacity option minimizes cost for these workers?
options: Fargate On-Demand
Fargate with EC2 launch type instead
Savings Plans for the container images
Fargate Spot
explain: Fargate Spot offers steep discounts for interruption-tolerant containers and fits checkpoint-restart workers. Fargate On-Demand is the full price, switching launch types does not change the pricing model choice, and Savings Plans apply to compute usage, not container images.

q: Regulations require keeping financial records for 7 years. The records are never accessed unless auditors request them, and retrieval within 48 hours is acceptable. Which is the MOST cost-effective storage for this requirement?
options: S3 Standard-IA
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 One Zone-IA
explain: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 tier and its retrieval time of under 48 hours fits the audit requirement. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA cost far more per GB for data never read, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval is priced for more frequent access than this near-never pattern needs.

q: A retailer expects a massive one-day sale and must guarantee EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone, even though they will pay On-Demand rates. Discounts are secondary to the capacity guarantee. Which option provides this assurance?
options: Compute Savings Plans
EC2 Spot Instances
Scheduled Reserved Instances
On-Demand Capacity Reservations
explain: On-Demand Capacity Reservations hold capacity in a specific AZ for when it is needed, which is exactly a guarantee without a discount. Savings Plans discount usage without reserving capacity, Spot can be reclaimed at any time, and Scheduled RIs recur on a schedule rather than covering one event.

q: A website serves 50 TB per month of images from S3 directly to internet users. The CFO asks whether putting CloudFront in front of the bucket would change data transfer costs. Which statement is correct?
options: Serving through CloudFront lowers the per-GB data transfer price versus serving directly from S3, and repeated requests are served from edge caches
CloudFront increases data transfer costs because of the additional edge locations
Data transfer pricing is identical whether served from S3 or CloudFront
S3 Transfer Acceleration must be enabled before CloudFront can reduce costs
explain: CloudFront data transfer to the internet is priced lower per GB than S3 data transfer in most Regions, and edge caching means repeat requests never reach the origin at all. CloudFront does not add cost on top of origin transfer for this pattern, pricing is not identical, and Transfer Acceleration is an upload feature unrelated to download pricing.

q: A database volume was provisioned with 20,000 IOPS for a migration weekend but now needs only 3,000 IOPS. The team is overpaying for unused provisioned IOPS on an io1 volume. Which change rightsizes cost while keeping 3,000 IOPS available on demand?
options: Take a snapshot and delete the volume
Enable EBS fast snapshot restore
Migrate the volume to gp3 with 3,000 provisioned IOPS
Add a second io1 volume and stripe them
explain: gp3 includes 3,000 baseline IOPS at no extra charge and lets IOPS scale independently of volume size, so migrating off io1 removes the provisioned-IOPS premium. Deleting the volume destroys the database, fast snapshot restore speeds restores rather than cutting IOPS cost, and striping more io1 volumes increases the provisioned-IOPS bill.

q: A company needs disaster recovery for a three-tier application with a recovery time objective of 4 hours and a recovery point objective of 1 hour. The budget is tight, so the standby environment must stay as small as possible while keeping data continuously replicated. Which DR strategy best fits?
options: Pilot light: a minimal standby environment with continuous database replication, scaled up only during failover
Multi-site active-active with full capacity in both Regions
Warm standby running the full application stack at reduced capacity
Nightly backups restored only when a disaster is declared
explain: Pilot light keeps only core data replication running and provisions the rest at failover time, meeting a 4-hour RTO and 1-hour RPO at the lowest standby cost. Active-active doubles cost, warm standby runs more idle capacity than the budget allows, and nightly backups have a 24-hour RPO that misses the 1-hour target.

q: An auditor discovers that several production resources were modified directly in the console, bypassing the CloudFormation templates that are supposed to manage them. The team needs to identify exactly which resources drifted from their templates. Which feature provides this?
options: CloudFormation change sets
CloudFormation drift detection
CloudFormation StackSets
AWS Config timeline alone
explain: Drift detection compares the live state of stack resources against their templates and reports exactly what changed outside CloudFormation. Change sets preview future updates rather than detecting past manual edits, StackSets deploy across accounts and Regions, and Config tracks changes but does not compare against the template definition.

q: A company keeps its DNS on premises but runs workloads in AWS that use a Route 53 private hosted zone. On-premises servers must resolve the private AWS hostnames over the existing Direct Connect link. Which component enables this?
options: A Route 53 public hosted zone with the same domain name
A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint in the VPC
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC with a forwarding rule on the on-premises DNS servers
An internet gateway with DNS port forwarding
explain: An inbound Resolver endpoint lets on-premises DNS forward queries for the AWS private zone into the VPC over Direct Connect. A public hosted zone would expose private names, an outbound endpoint serves the reverse direction (VPC to on-premises), and internet gateways do not forward DNS.

q: An application connects directly to the Aurora PostgreSQL writer instance endpoint. During a recent failover the application kept trying the old writer and stayed down until engineers updated the connection string. How should the application connect so future failovers are automatic?
options: Connect to the reader endpoint instead
Hard-code the IP address of the current writer
Put a Network Load Balancer in front of the cluster
Connect to the cluster endpoint, which always resolves to the current writer
explain: The cluster endpoint automatically points to the current writer after a failover, so the application recovers without changes. The reader endpoint load-balances reads and never targets the writer, hard-coding IPs or instance endpoints breaks on failover, and a load balancer in front adds complexity without understanding Aurora topology.

q: During rolling deployments, an Auto Scaling group terminates instances that are still serving long-running requests, causing user-visible errors. The load balancer already has access logs enabled. Which setting lets in-flight requests finish before the instance is terminated?
options: The ALB target group deregistration delay, which keeps the instance receiving no new connections while existing ones drain
The Auto Scaling health check grace period
The ALB idle timeout
The Auto Scaling termination policy
explain: The deregistration delay (deregistration delay / connection draining) gives in-flight requests time to complete after an instance is deregistered and before it is terminated. The health check grace period delays health evaluation on new instances, the idle timeout closes idle connections rather than draining, and termination policies choose which instance to terminate, not how gracefully.

q: A company must protect 300 on-premises servers with continuous block-level replication to AWS so any server can be launched in AWS within minutes of a site failure, with no agents to license per workload beyond the service itself. Which AWS service provides this?
options: AWS Server Migration Service (SMS)
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS)
AWS DataSync
VM Import/Export
explain: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates servers at the block level into low-cost staging and launches them in minutes during drills or disasters. SMS is the retired predecessor, DataSync moves files rather than replicating bootable servers, and VM Import/Export is a one-time migration tool without continuous replication.

q: An Aurora PostgreSQL cluster serves a SaaS application whose I/O swings unpredictably between 5,000 and 80,000 IOPS. The team is tired of paying for provisioned IOPS they rarely use, but standard Aurora throttles during spikes. Which configuration smooths out this unpredictable I/O cost?
options: Migrate to RDS for PostgreSQL with io1 volumes
Add read replicas to absorb the I/O spikes
Enable Aurora I/O-Optimized configuration, which uses predictable pay-per-use I/O pricing
Move the data to DynamoDB
explain: Aurora I/O-Optimized replaces unpredictable I/O charges with a predictable configuration better suited to spiky or I/O-heavy workloads. RDS io1 still bills provisioned IOPS, read replicas add compute cost without changing the I/O billing model, and migrating to DynamoDB is a full database rewrite.
