q: A backup application must upload a single 50 GB database dump to S3 as quickly as possible over a high-bandwidth link. A single PUT request fails for this object. Which approach completes the upload reliably and in parallel?
options: Compress the file below 5 GB and use a single PUT
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and retry the single PUT
Store the file in Glacier instead
Use S3 multipart upload to transfer parts in parallel
explain: Multipart upload splits the object into parts transferred in parallel and is required for objects over 5 GB, which is why the single PUT fails. Compressing below 5 GB loses parallelism, Transfer Acceleration speeds the network path but does not lift the single-PUT size limit, and Glacier is a storage class rather than an upload mechanism.

q: A database volume needs a sustained 10,000 IOPS but only 200 GB of capacity. With gp2, IOPS scale at 3 per GB, which would require a 3.4 TB volume. Which volume type delivers 10,000 IOPS on the 200 GB volume without overprovisioning capacity?
options: gp3 with 10,000 provisioned IOPS
gp2 with 200 GB
Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
Cold HDD (sc1)
explain: gp3 decouples IOPS from volume size, allowing 10,000 provisioned IOPS on a 200 GB volume. gp2 would need over 3 TB for that IOPS level, and st1/sc1 are throughput-oriented HDDs unsuitable for IOPS-heavy database workloads.

q: A Lambda function behind API Gateway suffers cold starts of 3 seconds during traffic bursts, and users abandon the slow first requests. The function must stay warm with execution environments initialized before requests arrive. Which feature eliminates the cold starts?
options: Increasing the function's memory to 10 GB
Lambda provisioned concurrency
Lambda reserved concurrency
Enabling Lambda SnapStart on a non-Java runtime
explain: Provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments initialized and ready, eliminating cold starts during bursts. More memory speeds execution but does not pre-warm, reserved concurrency only caps the maximum concurrent executions, and SnapStart accelerates cold starts for Java runtimes rather than eliminating them.

q: An order-processing workflow must charge payment, reserve inventory, and send confirmation in sequence, retrying failed steps with backoff and rolling back earlier steps on failure. Chaining SQS queues between Lambdas has become unmanageable. Which service is designed for this orchestration?
options: Amazon SNS fan-out
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
AWS Step Functions
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
explain: Step Functions provides visual workflow orchestration with sequencing, retries, error handling, and compensating transactions built in. SNS fan-out broadcasts rather than sequencing, EventBridge Scheduler triggers on schedules rather than orchestrating, and Kinesis is a streaming ingest service rather than a workflow engine.

q: A fraud-detection team must traverse relationships between accounts, devices, and transactions up to six hops deep in milliseconds. SQL joins across relational tables take seconds at this depth. Which database is purpose-built for this workload?
options: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with more read replicas
Amazon DynamoDB with adjacency lists
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis
Amazon Neptune
explain: Neptune is a graph database that traverses multi-hop relationships in milliseconds natively. Relational joins degrade exponentially with depth, DynamoDB adjacency lists require multiple round trips per hop, and Redis is a cache rather than a graph traversal engine.

q: A company writes an S3 bucket policy that must allow access only to IAM principals belonging to its own AWS Organization, regardless of which account they are in. Which condition key identifies the organization of the requesting principal?
options: aws:PrincipalOrgID
aws:PrincipalAccount
aws:PrincipalArn
aws:SourceVpc
explain: aws:PrincipalOrgID matches the organization ID of the requesting principal, covering all accounts in the organization with one condition. aws:PrincipalAccount matches a single account, aws:PrincipalArn matches specific identities rather than the org, and aws:SourceVpc constrains by network origin rather than organizational membership.

q: A company encrypts data with the same KMS key material in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-2 so that data encrypted in one Region can be decrypted in another without re-encryption. Managing three separate keys is causing operational pain. Which KMS feature provides one logical key across Regions?
options: KMS automatic key rotation
KMS key aliases
KMS multi-Region keys
KMS grants
explain: Multi-Region keys replicate the same key material across Regions as one logical key, so ciphertext is portable without re-encryption. Automatic rotation changes key material on a schedule, aliases are just friendly names, and grants delegate permissions rather than sharing key material.

q: A company runs 30 VPCs and must inspect and filter all outbound internet traffic centrally, blocking malicious domains and allowing only approved destinations, without deploying appliances in every VPC. Which service provides centralized network-layer filtering?
options: AWS WAF
Security groups with egress rules
Network ACLs on every subnet
AWS Network Firewall deployed in a central inspection VPC with Transit Gateway routing
explain: Network Firewall in a central inspection VPC with Transit Gateway routing applies stateful Layer 3-7 filtering, including domain filtering, to traffic from all spoke VPCs. WAF protects web applications at Layer 7 rather than general egress, security groups are per-instance, and NACLs are stateless subnet filters without domain awareness.

q: A company suspects customer email addresses and national ID numbers are scattered across hundreds of S3 buckets. They need an automated discovery service that finds and classifies this personally identifiable information. Which service does this?
options: Amazon Macie
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Security Hub
Amazon Detective
explain: Macie uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII in S3 at scale. GuardDuty detects runtime threats, Security Hub aggregates security findings rather than scanning data content, and Detective investigates past security events rather than discovering PII.

q: The security team must continuously scan EC2 instances and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, prioritized by risk, without installing agents on every host. Which service provides this assessment?
options: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
Amazon Inspector
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
explain: Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2, Lambda, and container workloads for vulnerabilities and network exposure, agentless, with risk-based prioritization. Patch Manager applies OS patches but does not assess application vulnerabilities, GuardDuty detects active threats rather than scanning for vulnerabilities, and Config tracks configuration compliance rather than vulnerability exposure.

q: A shared-services account owns a VPC whose subnets must be usable by application accounts so each team can launch resources into centrally managed subnets. The company wants no VPC peering mesh. Which service enables this cross-account subnet sharing?
options: VPC peering between every account
AWS Transit Gateway
AWS PrivateLink
AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) with VPC sharing
explain: RAM with VPC sharing lets the owner account share subnets so other accounts launch resources directly into them, with no peering mesh. Peering creates the mesh the company wants to avoid, Transit Gateway routes between VPCs rather than sharing subnets, and PrivateLink exposes services rather than subnets.

q: Engineers need to log in to Windows EC2 instances using their existing on-premises Active Directory credentials. The company will not migrate its directory to AWS but wants minimal directory infrastructure in the cloud. Which service connects EC2 authentication to the on-premises domain?
options: AWS Managed Microsoft AD
AD Connector
Simple AD
Amazon Cognito
explain: AD Connector is a directory gateway that proxies authentication to the on-premises Active Directory without hosting a directory in AWS. Managed Microsoft AD and Simple AD both host a directory in the cloud, which the company wants to avoid, and Cognito handles web and mobile user authentication rather than Windows logins.

q: Finance needs to charge each product team's AWS spend back to its cost center. Resources are already tagged with Team names, but the monthly bill shows no team breakdown. What must be done so the tags drive the chargeback report?
options: Enable the Team tags as cost allocation tags in the Billing console, then use Cost Explorer grouped by tag
Export the AWS Price List API
Enable AWS CloudTrail in every Region
Turn on S3 access logging for the billing bucket
explain: Tags only appear in billing after activation as cost allocation tags, after which Cost Explorer can group spend by tag for chargeback. The Price List API shows service prices rather than actual spend, CloudTrail records API activity rather than costs, and S3 access logs track bucket access rather than team spending.

q: A startup's AWS bill suddenly doubles in the middle of the month with no planned changes. The team wants an automatic alert the moment spending patterns deviate unusually, without setting static thresholds for every service. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Budgets with fixed monthly thresholds
AWS Cost Explorer manual reports
Consolidated billing
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
explain: Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn normal spend patterns and alerts on unusual deviations without manual thresholds. Budgets need static thresholds per service, Cost Explorer requires someone to look at reports, and consolidated billing aggregates accounts rather than detecting anomalies.

q: A DynamoDB table serves a steady 5,000 reads and 1,000 writes per second around the clock with almost no variation. The team currently uses on-demand mode and wants to cut the table's cost. Which capacity approach is cheapest for this flat workload?
options: Reserved capacity with provisioned mode sized to the steady throughput
On-demand mode with auto scaling
DAX in front of on-demand mode
Global tables with on-demand mode
explain: Provisioned mode with reserved capacity discounts the predictable baseline throughput, which is the cheapest for a flat workload. On-demand charges a premium for flexibility the workload does not need, DAX adds cache cost without changing table billing, and global tables replicate data across Regions at extra cost.

q: An engineer notices the second EBS snapshot of a 1 TB volume cost far less than the first, even though both snapshots show the full 1 TB size in the console. Why is the second snapshot cheaper?
options: Snapshots are compressed with gzip automatically
The second snapshot reused the first snapshot's S3 storage class
The volume was converted to gp3 between snapshots
EBS snapshots are incremental: only blocks changed since the previous snapshot are stored and billed
explain: EBS snapshots store only changed blocks, so the second snapshot bills just the delta while still presenting as a full point-in-time copy. Snapshots are not gzip-compressed, storage class reuse is not a billing concept for snapshots, and the volume type does not change how snapshot deltas are billed.

q: A batch processing fleet must scale out every weekday at 6 AM, run until 10 PM, and scale to zero overnight and on weekends. The schedule is fixed and known a year in advance. Which Auto Scaling approach fits best?
options: Target tracking scaling on CPU utilization
Step scaling on SQS queue depth
Scheduled scaling with cron-based actions
Manual scaling by an operator each day
explain: Scheduled scaling changes capacity on a known timetable, matching the fixed business-hours pattern exactly with no metric lag. Target tracking and step scaling react to metrics rather than a calendar, and manual scaling adds daily operational toil.

q: An analytics job downloads a 10 GB CSV from S3 every hour but only needs 100 MB of matching rows. Data transfer and request costs are adding up. Which S3 feature lets the job retrieve only the matching rows?
options: S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Object Lambda
S3 Versioning
S3 Select
explain: S3 Select runs SQL expressions against the object in S3 and returns only matching rows, cutting transfer to the 100 MB actually needed. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than filtering, Object Lambda transforms objects on retrieval but is heavier than a simple filter, and versioning keeps object history rather than subsetting data.

q: A company is growing to 50 VPCs across 4 accounts and needs hub-and-spoke connectivity with centralized routing control. A full mesh of VPC peering connections is becoming unmanageable. Which service simplifies this multi-VPC network?
options: AWS Transit Gateway as a central hub connecting all VPCs
AWS PrivateLink endpoints in each VPC
A NAT gateway in every VPC
VPC peering with automated route table scripts
explain: Transit Gateway acts as a central hub that connects dozens of VPCs with manageable routing, replacing an exploding peering mesh. PrivateLink exposes individual services rather than providing network transit, NAT gateways provide internet egress rather than inter-VPC routing, and scripted peering keeps the underlying mesh complexity.

q: An engineer accidentally deletes objects from a production S3 bucket every few months. The team needs protection against accidental deletion while keeping deletes possible through the normal application workflow. Which solution provides this safety net?
options: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
S3 Versioning, so deleted objects become delete markers that can be removed to restore the data
S3 Lifecycle expiration of all objects after 7 days
Disabling all IAM permissions for s3:DeleteObject
explain: Versioning turns deletes into delete markers, so accidental deletions are reversible by removing the marker, while the application workflow still works. Compliance-mode Object Lock would block the application's legitimate deletes, lifecycle expiration automates deletion rather than preventing it, and removing all delete permissions breaks the normal workflow.

q: An EventBridge rule triggers order-fulfillment workflows. During a two-hour outage of the downstream fulfillment service, events were lost because no target could receive them. The team wants to reprocess those missed events after recovery. Which feature enables this?
options: EventBridge dead-letter queues on the event bus
Increasing the event bus throughput quota
EventBridge archive and replay of the events from the outage window
Adding a second EventBridge rule with the same pattern
explain: EventBridge archives store published events and replay sends them to targets again, recovering the missed two-hour window. Dead-letter queues capture failed invocations rather than replaying history, throughput quotas do not retain events, and a duplicate rule would only affect future events, not the lost ones.

q: A junior DBA drops the wrong table in an RDS for PostgreSQL instance. The team needs the database restored to exactly 10 minutes before the drop, with minimal data loss and without rebuilding from last night's snapshot. Which capability provides this?
options: Restoring from the most recent manual snapshot
Promoting a read replica
Enabling Multi-AZ after the incident
RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery
explain: Automated backups combine daily snapshots with transaction logs to restore to any second within the retention window, covering the 10-minutes-before target. Manual snapshots only go back to last night, read replicas contain the dropped table too since they replicate the mistake, and Multi-AZ protects against AZ failure rather than human error.

q: An operations team receives 40 separate CloudWatch alarms during every deployment, most of them transient noise. They want a single alarm that fires only when a meaningful combination of conditions occurs, such as high error rate AND low healthy-host count. Which feature provides this?
options: CloudWatch metric math expressions
CloudWatch Logs Insights queries
SNS message filtering
CloudWatch composite alarms
explain: Composite alarms combine multiple alarms with boolean logic, firing only when the meaningful combination holds and suppressing the noise of individual alarms. Metric math derives new metrics but does not combine alarm states, Logs Insights queries log data rather than alarm states, and SNS filtering routes notifications rather than evaluating conditions.

q: A multi-Region application must shift traffic away from an impaired Availability Zone within seconds, faster than DNS propagation allows, with a pre-approved runbook the on-call engineer can trigger. Which AWS capability is designed for this rapid zonal shift?
options: Application Recovery Controller (ARC) zonal shift
Route 53 health checks with a 60-second TTL
Manually updating ALB target groups
AWS Backup restore to another AZ
explain: ARC zonal shift moves traffic away from an impaired AZ in seconds through pre-authorized controls, far faster than DNS TTL expiry. Route 53 failover still waits on DNS propagation, manual target-group edits are slow and error-prone under pressure, and Backup restores data rather than shifting live traffic.

q: A company runs Cassandra across 18 EC2 instances and needs rack awareness: correlated hardware failures must not take down multiple Cassandra racks at once, while keeping instances of the same rack close together. Which placement group type provides this?
options: Cluster placement group
Spread placement group
Partition placement group
No placement group
explain: Partition placement groups divide instances into partitions aligned with failure domains, matching Cassandra's rack concept: racks stay isolated from correlated failures while members of a partition stay close. Cluster packs everything together without failure isolation, spread isolates every single instance which wastes the rack grouping, and no placement group gives no topology control.

q: A Windows-based engineering application requires SMB file shares with Active Directory integration and consistent sub-millisecond metadata performance for thousands of small files. The team wants a managed service, not self-managed Windows File Servers. Which storage service fits?
options: Amazon EFS
Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon S3 with File Gateway
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explain: FSx for Windows File Server provides native SMB shares with Active Directory integration as a managed service. EFS is NFS-based for Linux, FSx for Lustre targets HPC scratch workloads rather than SMB, and File Gateway presents S3 over SMB but without native Windows semantics and AD integration at this level.

q: A startup needs to deploy a containerized web application publicly with automatic HTTPS, health checks, and deployments, and the team has no infrastructure engineers. Which service deploys the container with the least operational overhead?
options: Amazon ECS on EC2 with a self-managed ALB
Amazon EKS with managed node groups
AWS App Runner
AWS Batch
explain: App Runner builds, deploys, load-balances, and scales a containerized web app from a repository with automatic HTTPS and no cluster to manage. ECS on EC2 and EKS both require cluster and networking management, and Batch schedules batch jobs rather than serving web traffic.

q: A leaderboard service needs in-memory microsecond reads that survive node failures without data loss, with Multi-AZ durability built in. Standard Redis replication with manual failover is not durable enough. Which service meets these requirements?
options: ElastiCache for Memcached
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
Amazon RDS for Redis
Amazon MemoryDB
explain: MemoryDB provides Redis-compatible in-memory performance with a durable transaction log replicated across AZs, so data survives failures. Memcached has no persistence, DAX caches DynamoDB rather than serving as a durable primary store, and there is no such service as RDS for Redis.

q: A factory's IoT sensors emit 2 million timestamped readings per minute that must be ingested, stored cost-effectively for 2 years, and queried by time ranges with SQL-like syntax. Which purpose-built database fits this time-series workload?
options: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Timestream
Amazon Neptune
explain: Timestream is purpose-built for time-series data with automatic tiering, time-range queries, and SQL-like syntax at IoT scale. RDS would need manual partitioning at this ingest rate, DynamoDB requires custom time-bucketing design, and Neptune is a graph database unsuited to time-series.

q: A company has a Direct Connect connection in us-east-1 and needs private connectivity from its data center to VPCs in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-2 without provisioning a separate private VIF for every VPC. Which component enables this?
options: A Direct Connect gateway associated with virtual private gateways in each Region
A transit VIF to each VPC
A public VIF with BGP communities
AWS Site-to-Site VPN to each VPC
explain: A Direct Connect gateway connects one DX connection to virtual private gateways across Regions, avoiding per-VPC private VIFs. Transit VIFs connect to Transit Gateways rather than individual VPCs, public VIFs reach public AWS services rather than VPCs, and per-VPC VPNs add tunnels instead of consolidating the DX path.

q: A company distributes a confidential analyst report as a single PDF to 200 external recipients via email links. Each link must expire after 7 days and work without requiring an AWS account. Which mechanism secures this distribution?
options: S3 bucket policies with IP conditions
CloudFront signed cookies
IAM users for each recipient
CloudFront signed URLs with an expiry time
explain: Signed URLs grant time-limited access to a single object and work for anonymous recipients clicking an email link. Bucket policies with IP conditions cannot express per-link expiry, signed cookies suit multi-object sessions rather than one file, and creating IAM users for external recipients is heavy and inappropriate.

q: An application in Account A must read objects from an S3 bucket in Account B. The security team forbids long-lived credentials and forbids copying the data between accounts. Which approach grants this cross-account access securely?
options: Create an IAM user in Account B and embed its access keys in the application
Configure the application to assume an IAM role in Account B via STS with a trust policy allowing Account A
Make the bucket public and restrict by IP address
Replicate the bucket into Account A with S3 Batch Replication
explain: Assuming a cross-account role via STS issues temporary credentials governed by the role's trust policy, with no long-lived secrets and no data copying. Embedded IAM user keys are long-lived credentials, public buckets expose data broadly, and replication copies data, which the requirements forbid.

q: After a suspected unauthorized change to a production security group, the incident team must determine exactly which IAM principal made the change and when. Which service records this API activity?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
AWS Config
AWS CloudTrail
VPC Flow Logs
explain: CloudTrail records every AWS API call including the principal, action, and timestamp, answering who changed the security group and when. CloudWatch Logs holds application and service logs rather than API history, Config tracks configuration state changes without full API attribution, and VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic rather than control-plane actions.

q: Application servers cannot reach a database, and the security team suspects a network ACL or security group is rejecting the traffic. They need packet-level accept/reject records for the network interfaces to confirm. Which source provides this?
options: Route 53 Resolver query logs
AWS CloudTrail
Traffic Mirroring to an IDS appliance
VPC Flow Logs
explain: VPC Flow Logs record ACCEPT/REJECT decisions per network interface, directly showing whether security groups or NACLs dropped the packets. Resolver query logs cover DNS rather than TCP connectivity, CloudTrail logs API calls rather than data-plane packets, and Traffic Mirroring copies full packets for inspection but is heavier than needed to confirm a reject.

q: A company wants to consume a third-party SaaS analytics service from its VPC without sending traffic over the public internet and without the SaaS provider learning the company's internal IP addresses. Which connectivity model achieves this?
options: AWS PrivateLink with an interface endpoint to the provider's endpoint service
VPC peering with the provider's VPC
A NAT gateway with Elastic IP allowlisting
AWS Transit Gateway attachment to the provider
explain: PrivateLink connects the VPC to the provider's endpoint service privately, keeping traffic off the internet and hiding internal IPs behind the provider's service interface. Peering would expose internal addressing and require the provider's cooperation on routing, NAT gateways still traverse the internet, and Transit Gateway does not connect to third-party SaaS networks.

q: During a vendor security review, a customer asks for AWS's SOC 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate. The team needs official AWS compliance documentation to share under NDA. Where do they obtain these reports?
options: AWS Security Hub findings export
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Config conformance packs
AWS Artifact
explain: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for AWS compliance reports including SOC 2 and ISO 27001, shareable under NDA. Security Hub aggregates security findings rather than audit reports, Trusted Advisor gives operational best-practice checks, and Config conformance packs evaluate resource compliance rather than providing AWS's own certifications.

q: A company suspects many EC2 instances are over-provisioned but does not know which ones or what size they should be. They want automated, data-driven rightsizing recommendations based on actual CloudWatch utilization. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Budgets
AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Price List API
explain: Compute Optimizer analyzes CloudWatch utilization and recommends optimal instance types and sizes for over-provisioned resources. Budgets alert on spend thresholds rather than recommending sizes, Cost Explorer visualizes spend without rightsizing guidance, and the Price List API only publishes service prices.

q: A platform team manages 400 S3 buckets across 30 accounts and needs organization-wide visibility into storage growth, incomplete multipart uploads, and unencrypted buckets. Which service provides this aggregated storage analytics view?
options: S3 Inventory per bucket
CloudWatch metrics per bucket
AWS Config rules per account
S3 Storage Lens with an organization-level dashboard
explain: S3 Storage Lens aggregates metrics across all buckets and accounts into organization-level dashboards covering growth, multipart uploads, and encryption status. S3 Inventory produces per-bucket CSV listings without aggregation, CloudWatch metrics are per-bucket, and Config evaluates compliance rather than storage analytics.

q: Finance notices charges for 60 EBS volumes that have been unattached from any instance for months. The team wants an automated check that flags idle resources like these across the account. Which service includes this check?
options: Amazon CloudWatch alarms
AWS Trusted Advisor idle-resource checks
AWS Systems Manager Inventory
VPC Flow Logs analysis
explain: Trusted Advisor's cost-optimization checks flag unattached EBS volumes and other idle resources automatically. CloudWatch alarms need manual per-resource setup, Systems Manager Inventory tracks software and configuration rather than cost waste, and VPC Flow Logs analyze network traffic rather than idle volumes.

q: A Lambda-based image-processing workload runs millions of invocations monthly. The functions are compatible with ARM64, and the team wants to cut compute cost per invocation without changing performance. Which change delivers this?
options: Increase function memory to the maximum
Enable provisioned concurrency
Switch the functions to the arm64 (Graviton2) architecture
Split the workload across more functions
explain: Lambda's arm64 architecture is priced lower per millisecond than x86 with comparable performance, directly cutting per-invocation cost. More memory raises cost per millisecond, provisioned concurrency adds a fixed hourly charge, and splitting functions does not change the architecture pricing.

q: A team exposes simple HTTP APIs that only need JWT authorization and request routing, currently running on API Gateway REST APIs. They want to cut the per-request API cost while keeping a managed service. Which change reduces cost?
options: Add API Gateway caching to the REST APIs
Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics
Migrate the APIs to API Gateway HTTP APIs
Deploy a Network Load Balancer instead
explain: HTTP APIs are priced significantly lower per request than REST APIs and cover routing plus JWT authorization natively. Caching reduces backend calls but not the per-request API price, detailed metrics add cost, and an NLB is self-managed infrastructure rather than a cheaper managed API.

q: A team streams application logs through Kinesis Data Streams and runs a Lambda function just to batch records into S3 every 5 minutes. They want to remove the custom Lambda code entirely. Which service delivers stream data to S3 without custom consumers?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out
Amazon MSK with Kafka Connect
Amazon EventBridge Pipes
Amazon Data Firehose with an S3 destination
explain: Data Firehose delivers streaming data to S3 on a schedule with batching and compression built in, eliminating the Lambda consumer. Enhanced fan-out still needs a consumer, MSK with Kafka Connect adds Kafka cluster management, and EventBridge Pipes routes events but is not a managed S3 delivery loader.

q: A startup runs production, staging, and development in three separate AWS accounts. Their combined usage would qualify for volume discounts, but each account is billed separately at lower tiers. Which setup unlocks tiered volume discounts across all three accounts?
options: Purchasing Reserved Instances in each account separately
Keeping the accounts fully separate for isolation
Consolidated billing under AWS Organizations
Enabling Cost Explorer in each account
explain: Consolidated billing aggregates usage across member accounts so volume discounts apply to the combined total. Separate Reserved Instance purchases cannot pool usage tiers, keeping accounts separate preserves the fragmented billing, and Cost Explorer only visualizes spend rather than changing how it is billed.
